Trump’s Top 25 Achievements: The List Every Conservative Should Know and Use
Donald Trump doesn’t have an accomplishment problem. Republicans have an information problem. It’s on each of us to change that.
With the midterms coming, an astonishing number of Republican voters cannot name three things President Trump has accomplished. Which is remarkable when you consider that Donald Trump has accomplished more in a year and a half than any other president ever did in four.
Indeed, he has accomplished so much, so fast, across so many fronts that most people cannot keep up. The Enemedia buries the victories, while Republicans do an abysmal job of explaining them.
So here is the cheat sheet. It barely scratches the surface. And yet each and every item here is a game-changer.
This is not a list of promises. It’s a list of laws enacted, cases won, policies implemented, agreements secured, and measurable results.
You don’t have to memorize all 25. Learn five. And when somebody says Trump “hasn’t done much,” show them the receipts.
Trump Restored American Safety and Sovereignty
1. He made the border a real border again.
In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.
2. He reversed mass migration.
America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”
Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.
3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.
Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.
Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.
4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.
According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.
This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.
Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle
5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.
The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.
Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.
6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one.
In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.
Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.
7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.
That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.
No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.
8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.
9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.
10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.
Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.
11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.
Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again
12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.
Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.
Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.
13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.
In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.
14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.
Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?
15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.
What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”
16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family
17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.
Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.
He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.
No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.
Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.
19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.
That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.
20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.
Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.
Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.
23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.
24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.
Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.
25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.
Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.
Now Act Like It Matters
Those are not tweets or campaign promises. They are changes in law, power, investment, sovereignty, culture, and the structure of the Republic itself. And they’re just the top 25: I could give you hundreds more.
Midterms are turnout elections. We do not need to convince Democrats to love Donald Trump. We need Republicans and friendly independents to understand what is at stake — and to show up.
And let’s be clear. When you say (as some of you will) “the Republicans need to do a good enough job telling this story”, you’re pointing at yourself. You are “the Republicans.”
So tell people our story. Donald Trump is delivering great things, whether or not heaven on earth has broken out quite yet. Do the work, send the team he needs to Washington to finish the job, and get ready for 2028 afterward.
Take the time to learn at least five of these victories. Share this list with someone who needs it. And vote as though the most consequential Presidency in modern history depends on what you do.
Because it does.

text:
The more fully you develop your individuality, the more valuable you become to yourself—and the more you can offer others.
—Adapted from John Stuart Mill 

John Stuart Mill, On Liberty (1859), Chapter III, “Of Individuality, as One of the Elements of Well-Being.”

Mill is arguing that cultivating one’s authentic individuality—independent thought, character, capacities, tastes, and moral judgment—does not make a person selfish or detached from society. It makes them more fully alive, self-directed, and able to contribute meaningfully to other people.

In simpler words: the more you become yourself, the more you may have to give.
He follows it with the idea that a society made up of more developed individuals possesses “a greater fulness of life.” 

Mill’s defense of freedom was therefore not merely about protecting private choice; it was about allowing human beings to grow rather than be pressed into conformity.

APPLOVIN $APP CALLED A 53% QUARTER FALLING SHORT, AND LOST $27 BILLION THE NEXT DAY:

AppLovin at $333.09 (after hours), -$1.15 / -0.34% from Monday's $334.24 close, itself +$10.28 / +3.17% on the day. The Palo Alto company runs the system that picks which advert appears inside a mobile app, and does it with 898 people. Second of thirty on the Hypergrowth Len5 watch.

A leader is a settled argument, and settled arguments are already in the price; the name just behind is a question still open. Six of those below, one per Len5. The verdict on this one: AppLovin's growth is not what is in doubt. Where the next leg comes from is, and the piece of the business that has to supply it is about a tenth of what runs through the platform today.

August 5, after the close, for the three months to June 30: revenue $1.92B, +53%; net income $1.27B, +64%, which is 66 cents of every revenue dollar, or roughly $1.4M of profit per employee in ninety days. Revenue was also about 1.2% under the $1.95B analysts carried, some $23M, and cash profit before interest, tax and wear on equipment landed just below the company's own range. Chief executive Adam Foroughi said it himself: "we fell short of that standard." Next day the shares closed at $335.67 against $417.80, -$82.13 / -19.7%. About $27B of value for a $23M shortfall - over a thousand dollars of market value for every dollar missed.

The reason given is testable: a sizable rebuild of the model that picks which advert a person will act on slipped out of June into the September quarter rather than be rushed, and money earned per app install still rose 58% while installs fell 2%. The harder question is newer. In June AppLovin opened its platform to every advertiser and began pairing with shop-analytics firms such as Triple Whale to reach mid-sized online retailers. That consumer side runs 28% above end-2025 levels, and JPMorgan still puts it at about 9% of what advertisers spend through the platform. Mobile games are the rest.

Hypergrowth hunts a business early as well as fast. Fast is settled. Early is what holds it second: a $111.8B company already carrying most of the advertising inside mobile games, whose genuinely early piece is a ninth of the spend. CHANGE IT: consumer and e-commerce rising as a share of the total, not merely in dollars. WHEN: third quarter tentatively Wednesday, November 4, after the close, $4.01 carried against a company map of $2.055B-$2.085B, +46-48%. RISK: the shares sit 55.2% under last September's $745.61 high, and Morgan Stanley cut its target to $450 from $650 Monday morning while keeping its positive rating. The stock rose 3.17% regardless.

MOMENTUM LEN5:
Personalis at $16.29, where Monday's close left it after a +$0.08 / +0.49% day. The Fremont, California firm sells a blood test that hunts traces of cancer DNA left after treatment. Runner-up of thirty on a Len5 wanting a price near its one-year high on climbs that agree: $4.955 on April 29 to $18.89 on August 21, now 13.8% under. The run is also over. On July 20 Personalis agreed to be bought by Tempus AI at $61.58 (after hours), -$0.63 / -1.01% today, for $16.25 a share in Tempus stock, and Monday closed four cents above that - people paying for a raise nobody offered. QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:

Runner-up of fifty-four on a Len5 hunting businesses nobody could rebuild at a discount, which here means the discipline to refuse business at a bad price. Second, not first, is the 1.41 times book value already paid - what owners keep once everything is sold and the debts settled. WATCH the tentative October 26 report, carrying $1.85 against that $2.56. RISK: the gap is hurricane season; $201M of catastrophe claims landed in the June quarter. DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:
Broadridge Financial Solutions at $174.39, unchanged since a +$6.65 / +3.96% Monday. The Lake Success, New York company sends the ballot when a company you own through a broker calls a vote. Runner-up of fifty-one on a Len5 hunting settled earning power bought cheaply, and settled means billed again every year: in the year to June 30 recurring revenue - fees charged again annually - grew 8% before currency moves, adjusted profit per share 12%, and 110% of that profit arrived as cash. On August 3 the board raised the dividend 12%, to $4.36 a year from $3.90. Tomorrow is a year to the day since the $253.36 high; the shares sit 31.2% under it at about 17.5 times profit. VERDICT: a record year, a bigger dividend, a third off the price.

GROWTH LEN5:
ServisFirst Bancshares at $42.30, no trade since Monday's +$0.17 / +0.40% finish. The Birmingham, Alabama bank lends to Southern businesses and well-off households with almost no branches - 666 people running a $4.6B company. July 20: $1.57 a diluted share, +40%; a net interest margin - what a bank keeps on loans after paying depositors - of 3.63%, wider by 0.53 points in a year; under 30 cents of cost per revenue dollar, against 33 cents. Five of those are arguments about a business. AppLovin's is about a date. The company that lost $27B over $23M has until November 4 to show that the tenth of its platform which is not mobile games is becoming the half that pays for the next three years.

text:
NOBODY BOUGHT CROWDSTRIKE $CRWD TODAY. THEY BOUGHT CYBERSECURITY:

CrowdStrike at $233.49 (after hours), -$1.89 / -0.80% from Monday's $235.38 close - and that close was +$28.64 / +13.85% on the day, on 25.4M shares against a two-week average near 11.8M. It touched $239.37 along the way, the highest this stock has traded in at least a year. The Austin, Texas company, 10,698 employees, sells the software that watches a company's laptops, servers and cloud accounts for break-ins.

The verdict: about $29.3B of value arrived in one session on an argument about somebody else's business, and the one figure that would show that argument turning into money is not published until December 1.

Nothing happened at CrowdStrike this weekend. What happened was an essay. On Saturday, September 12, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier," arguing the AI industry should deliberately slow how fast it makes models more capable, and warning that rogue AI agents could form a large botnet and do hundreds of billions of dollars of damage inside six to twelve months. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the same. Both companies are private, so nobody can buy shares in either.

Monday split that essay two ways. Chipmakers sell the hardware that makes models more capable, and they got sold: the VanEck Semiconductor ETF, which holds 25 of the largest US-listed chipmakers, is at $544.29 (after hours), +$2.79 / +0.52%, after finishing Monday at $541.50, -$27.03 / -4.75%. Security software got bought with both hands.

Then on Sunday CrowdStrike chief executive George Kurtz answered Amodei in public. Leading AI labs will keep pushing ahead whatever any one of them promises, Kurtz argued, so the security industry's job is to make that progress safe rather than slower. The prescription: treat every AI agent as a privileged user - narrow permissions, credentials that expire fast, a kill switch, and a person deciding anything that matters. "Pacing what comes next doesn't secure what's already here," Kurtz wrote.

That sentence is what the market bought. The company underneath is in good shape - reported August 26 after the close, for the three months to July 31:

- Revenue $1.47B, +26%; subscription revenue $1.40B, +27%
- Annual recurring revenue - subscription fees already signed and billed every year - $5.84B, +25%, with $332.8M of that added in the quarter
- Free cash flow - the cash left after running the business and paying for equipment - $377.4M, about a quarter of revenue

CrowdStrike also lifted its own outlook for how fast new recurring revenue grows this year, to 34% at the midpoint, on demand to secure AI.

Now the figure that makes Monday hard to defend. Reported profit that quarter was $5.3M - about a third of a cent out of every revenue dollar - or $0.01 a share. Across the last four quarters CrowdStrike has reported $58.5M of profit. Monday put roughly $29.3B onto the company, some 500 times that. The gap between that $5.3M and the $322.9M the company prefers to quote is mostly shares handed to staff - a real cost to owners even though no cash leaves. At about 41 times book value - what owners would keep after selling everything and paying every debt - there is very little under this price except the argument.

The tell that a category was bought rather than a company: Palo Alto Networks at $372.62 (after hours), -$1.32 / -0.35% from Monday's $373.94 close, rose +$43.29 / +13.10% during the day. The Santa Clara firm, 21,921 employees, sells firewalls and security software to large organizations and competes with CrowdStrike head-on in several of them. It moved within a percentage point of CrowdStrike on news naming neither, and being larger it added about $35.4B - more dollars than CrowdStrike did. Two rivals do not rise the same distance on the same afternoon for reasons specific to either one. Palo Alto is not a current Len5 pick, on the same arithmetic: at nearly ten times book and more than 800 times the last year of reported profit, neither value Len5 is offered a discount.

CrowdStrike is not a current pick on any of the six Len5es either, and price rather than quality is what keeps it off. Quality-Value wants a business almost nobody could rebuild bought under its worth, and Deep-Value and Special-Situations wants settled earning power bought cheaply; both need a discount, and 41 times book against $58.5M of annual reported profit is the opposite. Growth wants profit growth the price has not already charged for, and this price has charged for all of it; Hypergrowth wants a business early as well as fast, and 26% is fast but a $241.1B company selling this software since 2011 is not early; Income needs a dividend and there is none. A real fall in price while recurring revenue keeps compounding at this pace is what would put CrowdStrike in front of the value Len5es for the first time.

WATCH net new annual recurring revenue rather than revenue or the share price. Revenue is largely last year's contracts billed again. Net new ARR is what customers decided to spend this quarter, and it is the only line where an argument made in September can show up. WHEN: third-quarter results are tentatively Tuesday, December 1, after the close, against a company year of $5.99B-$6.01B of revenue and $1.25-$1.26 of adjusted profit a share. RISK: a quarter merely matching the $332.8M just delivered would say the weekend moved sentiment and nothing else - and sentiment is most of what holds this price up.

CrowdStrike sells precisely the thing Amodei says the world is running short of, so the link is not invented. Monday bought the link, not evidence of it.

An essay went up on a website on Saturday, and by Monday afternoon it had moved about $29B into one security company and $35B into its closest rival without a single customer signing anything. December 1, after the close, is when we start finding out whether any will.

Not investment advice.

Sunday, November 22 | 5–7 PM

The prosecution generally cannot open its case by calling “negative character witnesses” to show that Lindsay Clancy was a bad, selfish, or impatient mother and therefore more likely to have killed her children. Massachusetts evidence rules (like the federal rules they closely track) ban using a defendant’s character as propensity evidence. https://t.co/QwCMOlGNMf 
Under Mass. Guide to Evidence § 404(a):
•  Evidence of a person’s character or character trait is not admissible to prove that on a particular occasion the person acted in accordance with that trait.

text:
A Dozen Ingredients Show India's Mounting Food Inflation Risk - BBG

The traditional thali is taking a bigger bite out of household budgets.

For a snapshot of India’s rising food costs, look no further than the traditional thali, the ubiquitous set meal that puts many of the country’s everyday staples on a single plate.

Those ingredients are taking a bigger bite out of household budgets. Food accounts for almost half of monthly spending for some rural families and nearly 40% in cities. Onions, a foundation of countless savory dishes, have risen almost 50% from a year earlier. Vegetable oil used for frying street snacks is also rising, and the ginger vital for flavor has surged more than 70%, the latest consumer price index for August shows.

Several factors are at play: The annual monsoon has been weaker than usual, leaving farms thirsty. A push to increase biofuel production for energy security diverting grain. Plus, wars in both Iran and Ukraine are boosting crop and fuel prices globally.

That’s made food — which comprises more than a third of the retail inflation basket — emerge as a key driver of the country’s inflation, with the broader rate in August nearing the top of the central bank’s target range. It could also offer a signal of what’s to come elsewhere, as many nations cope with the fallout of conflicts and extreme weather, exacerbated this year by El Niño.

“In a connected world, supply is not an issue, but there will be issues with prices,” said Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda.

The monsoon rains, which end this month, are one of the obvious signs of the issue. Precipitation since they started in June is running 15% below normal, and the weather office has forecast rains to remain subpar in September. The shortfall is linked to the El Niño weather phenomenon, which is known for spurring drier years in the country.

That could further dim the harvest outlook for crops from rice to soybeans, corn and sugar cane. Rice and corn plantings are running more than 3% behind last season, with little time left, and domestic sugar prices jolted higher in August on worries of a shortfall. That forced the government to allow a tranche of duty-free sugar imports, an unusual step in a country that ranks as the world’s second-largest producer.

During years of deficient monsoons, every percentage point shortfall in rainfall versus normal equates to a roughly 25 basis point increase in food inflation, according to Yuvika Singhal, an economist at QuantEco.

The lady staying with my neighbor has been moving some of their cooked food and provisions to her house without her consent.

She’s actually a domestic staff. When she first came to work with her, they thought she was going to live in, but she told her she has a 3 year old daughter staying with her mom, so she prefers going home every day.

She even told her that she prefers they pay her salary than live with them, and my neighbor didn’t see anything wrong with that. I mean, a mother needs to stay closer to her child.

Every day,  she would cook, keep food (she doesn’t cook for her, just keep the house clean and do the laundry), go about her day and come back, only to notice that her stew, rice or soup had reduced.

At first, she thought maybe it was her children or maybe she was just not paying attention. One day, she  asked the lady, “Did you take my food?” She said, “No.”

She asked her again, and she still denied it. Even the provisions she usually buy for her children started finishing unusually fast.

Things that normally last for one month started lasting barely two weeks. She noticed it and complained to her husband, but he’s always at work, and because she work closer to home, she honestly didn’t think too much of it.

The funny thing is, the lady looks so innocent. Even on days she’d offer to give her breakfast or lunch, she’ll reject it and say that her salary is very much okay for her.

There was a day she came to work with her daughter, neighbor still gave the little girl money and some things to take home.

So she never really imagined that she could be the one taking her things without her consent.

One day, she got so angry. called her and asked her directly about the food and provisions. Instead of answering her, she started crying and saying that she was accusing her of steal!ng. She felt bad because she started thinking maybe she was actually accusing an innocent person.

But something still wasn’t adding up. She discussed with the husband and he suggested they put the CCTV they had been postponing for months.

She honestly wished they had installed it earlier. Because the day she checked the footage and saw what was actually happening, she said she just sat there looking at the screen and dropping tears.

Everything she had been noticing finally started making sense. This lady will use those disposable black nylon, pack some food and take some sachets of Milo, milk and my children’s juices.

And the person she had been asking was the same person doing it.

She still asked her again yesterday after seeing the footage, and she still lied to her face. For someone that she knew how she begged for this job and how nicely she has treated her.

You are  presenting  yourself  as a geopolitical analyst, but this piece reads more like a prosecutor’s closing argument delivered before the investigation has begun. 

You  connect Boulos, Sisi, Afwerki, Iran, the Houthis and Eritrean mining through insinuation, anonymous claims and strategic question marks, then quietly you admit that the central allegation has no evidence.

 This is not analysis; it is a conspiracy theory assembled from diplomatic meetings, personal opinions and unanswered questions.

Yes, the Houthis captured Mokha and moved onto Perim Island ( events independently reported by the BBC⁠ and other major news outlets). 

But nothing presented here proves that Eritrea assisted the offensive, supplied the Houthis, granted Iran military access or entered an alliance with either. Opposing another military intervention in Yemen is not the same as recognizing Houthi sovereignty or joining Iran’s camp.

Amanuel Biedemariam is not the Eritrean government. His commentary cannot be converted into Eritrean state policy merely by calling him “close” to President Isaias. Likewise, diplomatic silence is not endorsement. Special envoys are employed precisely to communicate with governments with which Washington has serious disagreements. 

Asking why Rubio did not visit Asmara is therefore a bureaucratic non sequitur: Boulos,not the secretary of state was assigned this diplomatic channel.

The mining accusation is weaker still. You explicitly concede that there is no evidence Boulos was promised any mining interest, then you construct an Egyptian company, a hidden investment vehicle and a personal profit scheme entirely from speculation. Questions are legitimate; laundering accusations through question marks is not evidence.

The conclusion you offered here, an Iran–Houthi alliance, an Egyptian anti-Ethiopian plot and a secret Boulos mining arrangement has not been factually demonstrated. The Houthis’ advance is fact; everything connecting it to this alleged three-man conspiracy remains speculation with no evidence.

In short: many question marks, dramatic insinuations, and no smoking gun.

text:
There are moments in life that make you stop, look back, and realize just how much of the journey you have shared with someone. 

Yesterday was one of those moments for me.
Watching my dear friend Kenneth “Patricio” Smith receive the Amigo de México Award from Consul General of Mexico in Phoenix, Jorge Mendoza Yescas, filled my heart with memories and an emotion that is honestly difficult to put into words.

I have known Patricio for more than 25 years. More than a quarter of a century of friendship. And when I think about everything we have lived through together, I realize there is simply no way to fit it all into one post.

We have traveled together across different countries. We have worked, laughed, cried, prayed, reflected, celebrated, shared countless meals, and had those long conversations about life that only happen between true friends. We have walked through beautiful seasons and difficult ones.

And through all those years, Patricio has simply been there.

There to listen. There to offer advice. There to walk beside me. There to believe in me. And sometimes, simply there to sit beside me when no words were necessary.

Yesterday, as I watched him receive this recognition, my mind traveled back many years. I remembered standing together at the Arizona State Capitol, fighting so that members of our community could have access to driver’s licenses. We were younger then. The times were different, and we had no idea how many more battles, experiences, trips, conversations, and chapters life still had ahead of us.

But Patricio was there.

Just as he has been so many times throughout these 25+ years: standing up for those who needed a voice, extending a hand to those who needed help, and serving our Mexican and Latino communities without ever needing the credit or the spotlight.

That is why yesterday meant so much to me.
Because I have had the privilege of knowing the man behind the award. I have seen his heart when there were no cameras. I have witnessed his generosity when no one was watching. I have seen, for more than 25 years, how deeply he cares for people and how much of his life he has dedicated to serving others.

And yesterday, for a moment, it felt as though all those years, all those stories, all those people whose lives he has touched, and all those battles we fought were standing there with us.
What a gift life has given me by allowing me to walk alongside you for more than 25 years, my friend.

I am incredibly proud of you. But even more than I am proud of this recognition, I am grateful. Grateful for your friendship, your example, your heart, and for everything you have meant in my life.

Some awards are placed on a shelf and, with time, gather dust. This one represents something much greater: lives touched, doors opened, people defended, hope given, and a lifetime of service to others.

Congratulations, my dear Patricio.

Yesterday, Mexico officially called you an “Amigo de México.” Some of us have had the extraordinary privilege of simply calling you “friend” for more than 25 years. 🇲🇽❤️🇺🇸

And believe me, my friend… that has been one of the greatest gifts of my life.

text:
We do a lot of work in our professional and personal lives to find people that satiate some need. These workflows involve research (time spent collecting and reviewing context), coordination, and sometimes convincing/writing with craftsmanship.

Find me investment banking associates in NYC to network with. Find me a relator for beach houses in Cape May. Find me an expert in clinical trials that I’ll pay for a discussion. Find me a residential architect with a modern portfolio. Find me software engineers with 5+ years of experience in distributed systems. Find me hourly warehouse workers at Amazon in California from 2022–2025. Find me a single person 25-30 years old, presbyterian and over 6’2”. Find me partners at mid-market law firms based in the Northeast, over the age of 60. Find me venture-backed, seed-stage fintech founders with 1M+ in ARR. Find me adults with type 2 diabetes, A1c 7.5–10.5, on stable metformin, not currently using insulin.

These are all matching problems. One side wades through context to separate junk from something worth there time and the other tries to reach people where they provide value. Lots of song & dance and hours spent. Bad things that waste time get through and many good connections get missed. Good connections defined as discussions or relationships where there is a high chance of real value (note: value takes many forms, not always a deal struck) captured on both sides.

Can we handle this process with AI? I think yes, end-to-end (times show up on your calendar). A simple pane with agents pursuing people for each objective in our life, where the deliverable is scheduled time with profile-of-person X (or maybe, a probability that connecting with person Y will be valuable and one-click to meet them). Not a search engine, a results engine for connection. Even the more simple workflows listed above require research and coordination. The more complicated ones require deep context and evaluation.

Some caveats. There is nuance to each workflow, can this be captured in a horizontal product? I’d feel differently about a date vs a sales pitch showing up on my calendar (but what if both will be great conversations/connections!). This is close to the second point, focus is important. Should we pick one workflow where there is the most pain, or start broad to find that workflow within early technical and network constraints? Lastly, data collection here is hard. Can it be a one-sided marketplace to start? It becomes so much richer with onboarded context on both sides. Cut through the fluff to what a person has to offer and what there problems are with verified context, instead of us impersonating someone and going through traditional channels.

Re-read the list in the second paragraph. Do any of the use cases resonate? If this product worked, and the people you’re looking for showed up in your life, would you use it? From another perspective, can this be boiled down to context or is the art of selling/presenting yourself with a hinge profile, cold call, billboard, email copy, or search result here to stay?

text:
Thailand steps up as host of Gastech 2026, taking place from 14–17 September 2026 at the Bangkok International Trade and Exhibition Centre (BITEC), Bangkok. 

With more than 50,000 participants from 150 countries expected to attend, the event offers Thailand an important opportunity to showcase its energy capabilities and infrastructure on the global stage. 

The Office of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) is participating with an exhibition booth to present the development of Thailand’s energy regulation under the theme “ENERGY TRANSITION DESTINATION – Thailand’s Energy Transition Destination.”

The ERC views the energy transition as a journey from the energy systems of the past, through the present, and towards the energy systems of the future. Thailand’s destination is therefore not simply a cleaner energy system, but one that can simultaneously deliver security, affordable prices, sustainability and fair competition.
 
This challenge makes the role of the regulator increasingly important. The energy transition cannot be driven by technology alone; it also requires appropriate rules, regulatory frameworks and oversight mechanisms to support investment, competition and innovation, while safeguarding the interests of energy consumers and enabling the energy system to adapt to future change.

As Thailand’s energy regulator, the ERC plays a key role in designing rules and regulatory mechanisms to build an Energy Ecosystem that connects producers, energy businesses, investors and consumers. Clear, transparent and fair rules and regulatory mechanisms are essential to enabling all stakeholders to move towards Thailand’s energy transition destination in a balanced manner.

At the ERC exhibition booth, visitors will be introduced to an overview of Thailand’s energy system and the Commission’s regulatory role across both the electricity and natural gas sectors. The showcase covers natural gas and LNG infrastructure, market development and competition, as well as the future direction of Thailand’s energy system.

Natural gas and LNG will continue to play an important role in maintaining energy security during the transition. Regulatory oversight must therefore focus on efficiency, transparency, fair access to infrastructure and the promotion of competition, helping expand energy choices and strengthen the flexibility of Thailand’s energy system.

At the same time, Gastech 2026 features Strategic & Technical Conferences that broaden the discussion beyond natural gas and LNG towards emerging energy technologies. Key topics include Natural Gas & LNG, Hydrogen, AI Energy, Climate Tech, and Shipping & Marine, reflecting how the energy transition increasingly brings together fuels, technology and infrastructure.

⁠#Gastech2026 #EnergyTransition #ERC #Thailand #NBTWORLD

The top 5 GitHub repos for Week 37 are in, completing our look at the week's biggest star gainers. 

Picking up from last week’s lower-half rundown (Ranks 10–6), this week’s top tier leans heavily into AI agent skills and developer tooling.

Here is the breakdown of the top 5 projects leading the charts:

Rank 5: ⁠skills⁠ by Matt Pocock (+8,960 stars) Re-entering the top 10, this repository solves the hassle of custom, non-shareable agent instructions. It packages real-world engineering skills straight from ⁠.agents⁠ into a 30-second setup, featuring modular workflows like ⁠grill-me⁠, ⁠tdd⁠, ⁠diagnosing-bugs⁠, and ⁠to-spec⁠.

Rank 4: ⁠ponytail⁠ (+9,272 stars) Debuting directly in the top 5, this tool targets AI bloat with the philosophy: 
"the best code is the code you don't write." It forces agents to generate lean code without unnecessary dependencies. Early benchmarks across Claude Code sessions report up to 54% fewer lines of code, 20% cost reduction, and 27% faster execution.

Rank 3: ⁠archify⁠ (+10,442 stars) Moving down from last week’s #1 spot, ⁠archify⁠ remains a high-value agent skill that converts plain text into interactive architecture, sequence, and data-flow diagrams exported as self-contained HTML files—bypassing the visual limits of Mermaid.

 Rank 2: ⁠gods-eye-view⁠ (+10,510 stars) Climbing from rank 4, this browser-based 3D globe visualizes open real-time data feeds including ADS-B flight tracking, AIS maritime signals, satellite orbital paths, and seismic activity delivering a spy-tech aesthetic entirely powered by public APIs.

Rank 1: ⁠i-have-adhd⁠ (+15,924 stars | 43,000+ total) Claiming the top spot this week, this lightweight agent skill eliminates conversational AI fluff. By forcing LLMs to drop intro filler ("That's a great question...") and immediately lead with numbered, action-first commands, it offers a simple UX tweak that resonated massively with the dev community.

Whether it is stripping down bloated output or streaming real-world telemetry onto a 3D interface, Week 37 confirms that the developer ecosystem is hyper-focused on streamlining the agent workflow.

text:
Kenneth Walker III is a Super Bowl LX MVP and tonight he announced his arrival at Kansas City Chiefs with a brilliant performance.

But the path that led to this was full of near-misses that most highlight packages skipped. It involves a high school argument that almost ended his career, and the same coach who caused it later driving him 10 hours so he could even get a Power 5 look.

As a junior at Arlington High School outside Memphis, Walker got into a heated argument with assistant coach Andrew Atkins. He went home with his mom furious. In a later vlog he recalled telling her, essentially, that he was done with football and didn’t know what he’d do instead. His parents sat him down and told him not to make a life decision off emotion. The next day he went back, talked it out with Atkins, and they moved on. Walker now calls Atkins one of his favorite coaches.

That same coach later became the reason Walker even got to Wake Forest. Walker had almost no Power 5 offers despite putting up huge numbers (over 3,400 rushing yards and 41 touchdowns in high school). Kent State was his main landing spot until Wake Forest came in late.

His parents couldn’t take him on the recruiting visit. His dad, Kenneth Walker II, worked nights. Atkins picked him up, drove the roughly 10 hours from the Memphis area to Winston-Salem, and drove 10 hours back. Walker has said Atkins didn’t have to do that and that he still appreciates it. Wake Forest was his only Power 5 offer. He later transferred to Michigan State and exploded.

Kenneth Walker II, started training him at age four. Walker has described crying through workouts his father forced him through. His dad later said grown men didn’t want to do those sessions. The family turned parts of the house and backyard into a gym.

Before his senior year Walker developed blood clots in his lungs, woke up struggling to breathe, and was initially told he would never play football again. A second opinion and months of blood thinners (including self-injections) got him back. He still missed games as a senior and was an under-the-radar recruit afterward.

After Seahawks home games, a columnist noticed Walker would detour on the way to the locker room to greet a man in a wheelchair who worked the door. There was no prior relationship. Walker said it was just how his parents taught him to treat people who have a harder path.

text:
Hebrews 6:19

Daily Prayer – Tuesday, September 15, 2026

Bible Passage (NIV)
“We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,”

Descriptive Meaning
The letter to the Hebrews was written to believers pressed by weariness and the temptation to loosen their grip on Christ. In that setting the writer does not offer a softer gospel or a thinner promise. He reaches for two worlds at once: the harbor, where an anchor holds a vessel against wind and current, and the temple, where the curtain once barred the way into the presence of God. Christian hope is not optimism floating on good days. It is a weight dropped into the holy place itself, fastened where Christ has gone ahead, so that the soul is held from the inside of glory rather than from the shifting surface of circumstance.

Deep Dive – Original Language

**ἄγκυρα** – (ankyra) anchor

In the ancient Mediterranean an ἄγκυρα was iron and rope and trust: the hooked weight a sailor cast overboard when the storm made the shoreline unsafe. The word pictures something that grips what the eye cannot see beneath the water. Hebrews lifts that image into the life of faith. Hope is not a mood the believer manufactures; it is an ἄγκυρα for the soul—firm and secure—because it catches hold of a reality deeper than fear. The soul is not asked to hold itself steady by sheer will. It is held by what it is fastened to.

**καταπέτασμα** – (katapetasma) curtain, veil

Καταπέτασμα names the hanging that fell downward across the sanctuary, and in Hebrews it means the veil before the Most Holy Place—the boundary of access. The hope-anchor does not stop in the outer courts. It enters the inner place behind the curtain. Under the old covenant that space was forbidden except to the high priest, and then only once a year with blood. The writer’s point is staggering: the believer’s hope is already lodged where only God and the mediator belong, because Jesus has gone behind the veil as forerunner. The curtain that once said “stay out” has become, in Him, the doorway of a sure and present hold.
Prayer
Lord Jesus, You are the hope that holds me when my own strength frays. I cast the weight of my soul onto You, not onto outcomes I can manage. Keep me firm and secure when waves of doubt and fatigue rise. Thank You that my hope does not end at the edge of what I can see, but enters with You behind the curtain into the presence of the Father. Anchor me there today, in the Holy Place where You live for me. Amen.
#TrueBelief #BibleVerse #Jesus #Faith #Scripture

text:
Επειδή μου ζητήθηκε στα αγγλικά και είναι κρίμα να "χαθεί" στη μετάφραση...
----------------------
I could not possibly leave this without comment. All of you will probably expect to read a negative critique. And reasonably so, I might add, given that my views on our Ministry of Culture are well known to everyone here! However, I owe credit where credit is due, and I will gladly offer a "bravo" for the restoration work. But… there is always a "but"!
The Ministry announces that the western facade is being restored to its "fullest possible form." The keyword here is "possible," not "original."There is a vast difference between the architectural restoration of a structure and the reconstitution of its sculptures. The reality regarding the western facade, beyond the looted pieces held by the British Museum in London, involves permanent losses and conscious choices made by the restoration team...
Let us look at what I mean. As the Acropolis Monuments Conservation Service explains, the recent restoration primarily addressed the geometry and structural stability of the triangular pediment, rather than the sculptures themselves.
Three large orthostates (backing walls) were restored in the tympanum of the pediment.
The 6th and 8th orthostates were repaired by fusing ancient fragments with new marble. 
The 7th orthostat had been completely lost and was reconstructed entirely from new Pentelic marble to ensure the proper support of the roof.
This is all very well, and congratulations are in order!
However, the western facade has suffered irreparable damage that no restoration project can ever replace. During the Venetian siege, a bomb struck the Parthenon. When Morosini attempted to dismantle the central sculptures of the western pediment (the wondrous chariot of Athena and Poseidon) to take them as spoils of war, the ropes snapped. Τhe sculptures fell to the ground and shattered into pieces. These fragments were lost forever or turned into lime in the years that followed.
The remaining authentic sculptures of the western facade (such as Cecrops and Kallirrhoe) suffered severe erosion from the Athenian smog during the 20th century.
The reason the western facade will always have missing parts is also ethical... Modern archaeology strictly forbids the creation of fake ancient sculptures to fill historical gaps.The surviving authentic sculptures have been transferred to the Acropolis Museum for protection. Precise replicas made of artificial stone have been placed on the monument itself. 
In short, wherever there is no precise knowledge of the form of a relief or a sculpture, the space is deliberately left blank, allowing the viewer to distinguish what is authentic from what has been lost.
Therefore, to conclude this introduction, the "fullest form" mentioned by the Ministry refers to the architectural restoration of the temple's structural frame (which naturally protects the monument from future earthquakes) and the removal of the scaffolding. This allows the eye to appreciate the perfect proportions of the building, even with its permanent, historical "wounds."
Yet, do we truly know what originally existed there? You may have read or heard the claim that "we do not know." This is a convenient myth for those who wish to downplay the scale of the destruction or justify the current state of affairs. We possess irrefutable evidence:
- Just 13 years before Morosini's catastrophic explosion, the French painter Jacques Carrey drew the western pediment almost intact. We know the exact position of every figure: from the central clash between Athena and Poseidon, to Cecrops, Pandrosos, Hermes, Iris, and the river gods (Cephissos and Ilissos).
- From Pausanias to later travelers, the thematic and symbolic program of the temple was fully documented.
Many modern analysts approach the Parthenon merely as an "aesthetic achievement" or a "religious monument." This is a superficial reading that, I would say, dishonors not only them but us as well...
The Parthenon, in reality, was a political and philosophical manifesto carved in marble!
I will begin with the Western Facade, which prompted this post, where the "Message of Democracy" is clearly engraved:The contest between Athena and Poseidon was not just a myth. It was the glorification of diplomacy and choice. The Athenians chose the olive tree (peace, education, economy) over the trident (brute force and domination). The city defined itself through reason rather than coercion (recall what I have written previously regarding the new order of the Twelve Olympians)...
For the first time in global history, a temple did not merely depict gods or massacres, but the citizens themselves (the Panathenaic procession on the Frieze). Humans walked side by side with the gods. It was the ultimate apotheosis of anthropocentrism: man as the center of the universe. One could call it a "celebration of self-knowledge"...The famous architectural refinements (the subtle curvatures that make the building appear alive rather than inanimate) demonstrate that its creators had resolved problems of optics and psychology that modern architecture still struggles to fully grasp...
Everyone turns to Hesiod and Homer to "grasp" the "beginning." Yet, up there on the Acropolis, history is rewritten from scratch—not by kings, but by free citizens themselves!
The gods are no longer inaccessible tyrants. On the Parthenon frieze, the gods sit among humans, watching the city's festival as equals among equals.
For the first time in human history, a temple is not built to glorify a ruler or a dynasty, but to mirror the community of citizens itself. The subject of history is now the human being who thinks, votes, creates, and defends their homeland.
The mathematical proportions of the temple (the golden ratio φ) and the architectural refinements were not merely "decorative." I could not possibly leave this without comment. All of you will probably expect to read a negative critique. However, I owe credit where credit is due, and I will gladly offer a "bravo" for the restoration work. But… there is always a "but"!
The Ministry announces that the western facade is being restored to its "fullest possible form." The keyword here is "possible," not "original."There is a vast difference between the architectural restoration of a structure and the reconstitution of its sculptures. The reality regarding the western facade, beyond the looted pieces held by the British Museum in London, involves permanent losses and conscious choices made by the restoration team...
Let us look at what I mean. As the Acropolis Monuments Conservation Service explains, the recent restoration primarily addressed the geometry and structural stability of the triangular pediment, rather than the sculptures themselves.
Three large orthostates (backing walls) were restored in the tympanum of the pediment.
The 6th and 8th orthostates were repaired by fusing ancient fragments with new marble. 
The 7th orthostat had been completely lost and was reconstructed entirely from new Pentelic marble to ensure the proper support of the roof.
This is all very well, and congratulations are in order!
However, the western facade has suffered irreparable damage that no restoration project can ever replace. During the Venetian siege, a bomb struck the Parthenon. When Morosini attempted to dismantle the central sculptures of the western pediment (the wondrous chariot of Athena and Poseidon) to take them as spoils of war, the ropes snapped. Τhe sculptures fell to the ground and shattered into pieces. These fragments were lost forever or turned into lime in the years that followed.
The remaining authentic sculptures of the western facade (such as Cecrops and Kallirrhoe) suffered severe erosion from the Athenian smog during the 20th century.
The reason the western facade will always have missing parts is also ethical... Modern archaeology strictly forbids the creation of fake ancient sculptures to fill historical gaps.The surviving authentic sculptures have been transferred to the Acropolis Museum for protection. Precise replicas made of artificial stone have been placed on the monument itself. 
In short, wherever there is no precise knowledge of the form of a relief or a sculpture, the space is deliberately left blank, allowing the viewer to distinguish what is authentic from what has been lost.
Therefore, to conclude this introduction, the "fullest form" mentioned by the Ministry refers to the architectural restoration of the temple's structural frame (which naturally protects the monument from future earthquakes) and the removal of the scaffolding. This allows the eye to appreciate the perfect proportions of the building, even with its permanent, historical "wounds."

The World’s Most Unforgettable & Astonishing Stories — Part 2

History and nature are filled with facts so strange they sound impossible.

👑 Six “Kings” Who Never Existed

Swedish history once used a sequence of regnal numbers that included Charles I through Charles VI, even though these six kings never actually ruled Sweden. The first historical King Charles generally recognized was Charles VII, who ruled from 1155 to 1167.

👁️ An Eye Offered for $350,000

In 1940, a 32-year-old man in Buenos Aires, Argentina, reportedly announced that he was willing to sell one of his eyes because of severe financial difficulties. He even claimed that potential buyers had shown interest.

🐍 A Temple Shaped Like a Cobra

In Myanmar, there is a remarkable temple whose architecture resembles a giant cobra with its hood raised. Local folklore surrounding the site includes an extraordinary belief: someone bitten by a snake would supposedly be protected from the venom after entering the temple.

🚶‍♂️ Is Walking Barefoot Illegal?

A widely circulated claim says Belgium was once the only country where walking barefoot in public was a punishable offense. However, this is not supported as a general Belgian law and appears to be a popular historical misconception.

🌊 The Deepest Place on Earth

The Mariana Trench, located in the western Pacific Ocean, contains the deepest known point in Earth's oceans. Its deepest section, Challenger Deep, reaches roughly 36,000 feet (11,000 meters) deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with room to spare.

☄️ Mark Twain and Halley’s Comet

Mark Twain was born in 1835, the year Halley’s Comet appeared. He famously anticipated that he would also die when the comet returned and he did: Twain died in 1910, just one day after the comet reached its closest approach to Earth.

👰 1,500 Wives?

A frequently repeated historical claim says that Maharaja Man Singh II of Jaipur, India, had around 1,500 wives. The figure is widely circulated, but it should be treated cautiously because historical sources do not establish it reliably.

🧠 A Man Who Memorized 15,000+ Phone Numbers

According to reports attributed to China's Xinhua News Agency, Gu Yanling of Wuhan, China, was once said to have memorized more than 15,000 telephone numbers an extraordinary feat of memory.

💎 Newton’s Tooth Became a Ring

In 1816, a tooth said to have belonged to Sir Isaac Newton was reportedly sold in London for £730, an enormous sum at the time. Its buyer allegedly had the tooth mounted in a ring and wore it as a personal keepsake.

🕌 Missing Friday Prayer in Brunei

In Brunei, Friday congregational prayer has specific legal requirements for certain Muslim men under the country's Islamic laws. Claims that simply “not attending the Grand Mosque” is itself a universal criminal offense are an oversimplification of the actual legal provisions.

In southern Tunisia, the town of Matmata, Tunisia is famous for its remarkable underground homes. Instead of building upward, generations of residents carved dwellings into the earth, creating an unusual underground settlement complete with homes, shops and even hotels. Its unique architecture continues to attract visitors from around the world.

♟️ The Dog That Played Chess

Years ago, a trained dog in London, United Kingdom reportedly amazed spectators by playing chess against its owner. The animal appeared to recognize and respond to the moves on the board, leaving onlookers astonished.

🐌 Animals With Extraordinary Biology

Nature has some truly unusual examples of reproduction.

Snails can possess both male and female reproductive organs. Earthworms are also hermaphroditic, carrying both sets of reproductive organs. Some fish take an even more remarkable path: certain species are born female and later transition to male as they mature.

👨‍🦳 A Shock That Supposedly Turned Hair White Overnight

One widely repeated historical story claims that after the Franco-Prussian War, an enormous financial demand placed on France caused such extreme shock to a Paris banker that his previously black hair supposedly turned completely white within 24 hours.

text:
The baby
the bathwater 
and 
the cat in the cradle:

The Other Child Is Not an Argument
Listen. I am going to tell you about a war. It is a war about children. It is always a war about children. That is the only kind of war there is.

The easiest sentence in this war is a curse. One side says they hide behind children. The other says the outsiders are committing genocide. Both sentences contain a fact. Both are used as a spell so nobody has to look at the rest of the board.

A great many children in Gaza were killed by Israeli soldiers. That is the proximate truth. Aircraft and artillery do not become metaphors because the target area was complicated. If your politics requires those deaths to be filed under “tragic necessity” and then forgotten, you are not analyzing a war. You are defending a ledger.

Gaza’s leaders helped build the ledger. They fought from a packed strip, put tunnels and squads under civilian roofs, and learned that a dead child on camera can do work a living fighter cannot. A government that starts a war among its own houses is not a spectator when the houses come down. If your politics requires that fact to be called a slur, you are not defending a people. You are defending a method.

These two facts do not cancel. That is the point modern speech cannot bear. “Human shields” is how one camp stops seeing the scale of the fire. “Genocide” is how the other camp stops seeing the tunnels, the hostages, October 7, and the choice to stay inside the crowd. Each word does what old temple language did. It makes a death unexaminable. After the phrase, curiosity looks like collaboration.
Call that Moloch if you want the old name. Not because a bronze statue sits in the cabinet room. Because a public is trained to offer up its capacity to hold more than one true thing. The offering is not only the child who died. The offering is the spectator’s mind.

This is why the language travels so well through the wider cold war. Ukraine, Xinjiang, Syria, Iran, Gaza: every pole needs a sentence that binds its camp and dirties the other pole’s claim to order. Restrained clients repeat the sentence to keep the aid. Half-leashed clients remix it until the patron cannot pull them back. Unleashed clients pick the clip that fits the national myth. Turkey does not need a doctrine of intent to say “they kill babies.” Israel does not need a seminar on Turkish policy in Damascus to say “they want us dead.” China does not need to write either line. A West that cannot tell a whole story about Gaza is a West whose moral monopoly is already broken.

Law still matters. Genocide is a charge about purpose, not a synonym for an unbearable body count. Human shielding is a war crime, not a coupon that makes every subsequent bomb legal. If you flatten those distinctions you are not being more ethical. You are being easier to govern.

The adult paragraph is short and unsatisfying. Israeli forces killed the children in the direct sense. Hamas and its partners arranged a battlefield that made those deaths likely and useful. Outside states paid, armed, blocked exits, and called the result strategy. None of that returns a child. All of it is required before anyone has earned the right to the biggest word they know.
A nation that can say only one half will get the war it can stand to describe. A nation that can say both halves might still fight. It will not be able to pretend the fight is a rite. That pretense is the actual worship: not the ancient fire, but the modern refusal to see the whole story once the phrase has been spoken.
So it goes.

The Norse invaded Ireland for slaves, why did they invade England?

The Norse invaded England for a combination of portable wealth, political exile, and, most importantly, high-quality agricultural land. 

While the early phases of Norse activity in both England and Ireland looked very similar—initial hit-and-run raids targeting wealthy, unprotected coastal monasteries for silver, gold, and slaves—their long-term strategies for the two regions diverged significantly over time. 

[1] ()The transition from raiding to large-scale invasion and permanent settlement in England was driven by several key factors:1. 

The Quest for Arable Land

Scandinavia, particularly Norway, had a heavily mountainous and rocky terrain that limited the availability of good farming land. Combined with a booming population, this created an urgent domestic land shortage. 

England presented a massive contrast: its rolling plains, fertile soil, and mild climate were ideal for farming. When the Great Heathen Army invaded England in 865 AD, their primary goal shifted from collecting tribute to permanently seizing and partitioning land to establish farming communities.
 
[1]  Geopolitical Structures

The political landscapes of Ireland and England dictated how the Norse could operate
:In Ireland: The landscape was highly fragmented into dozens of petty kingdoms. The Norse could easily establish coastal, fortified trading hubs (like Dublin and Waterford) to dominate the slave trade, but conquering the densely populated, heavily resistant interior was incredibly difficult. [1] 

In England: 
The territory was split into a few massive Anglo-Saxon kingdoms (Northumbria, Mercia, East Anglia, and Wessex).

 By systematically defeating a single king, the Norse could instantly inherit a vast, organized, and already cultivated territory. They successfully conquered the north and east, establishing a massive self-governing territory known as the Danelaw. [1] 

. Broad Structural Trade vs. Local Imperialism

While the Norse absolutely took slaves from England (famously beginning with the raid on Lindisfarne Priory in 793 AD), England was an incredibly wealthy macro-economy. It offered immense agricultural yields, thriving trade networks, and massive political leverage. 

Ireland became the administrative and geographic hub of their western slave-trading empire, while England became their target for outright imperial conquest, culminating in Danish kings like Cnut the Great ruling England as part of a unified North Sea Empire. [1]

President Whipps is not describing a misunderstanding. He is describing a method.

First, the hotel. Then the tourist. Then the threat. Then the lecture that a small country should not have so much ocean. That is not diplomacy. That is a protection racket with a flag. Palau recognizes Taiwan. The “One China” principle is Beijing’s claim, not Palau’s law. A country that still knows it is a country said so out loud.

https://t.co/1gFlNr2oIT

The lever is not mysterious. Tourism is more than forty percent of Palau’s economy. Chinese arrivals rose — over 91,000 in 2015 — then fell when Koror refused to switch recognition. Group tours banned. Travel warnings issued against one of the safer places in the Pacific, citing “theft” and a “dangerous marine environment” on the eve of a regional forum. The promise on the other side of the knife was a million tourists and all the hotels they could want—if Palau denounced Taiwan.

https://t.co/fitojg2w4q

https://t.co/FeTLhKGSZ9

That is how a continent-sized party talks to an island: you are small, we are large, your water is excessive, your recognition is illegal, your visitors are a switch we own. Size is treated as a moral argument. It is not. A nation is not a department of a larger nation’s appetite. Self-determination is not a courtesy the strong extend when they are pleased.

Watch the same grammar elsewhere, and you will stop calling it “influence.” Taiwan peeled off the Solomon Islands and Kiribati. Ports, police training, debt, and the sudden discovery that last year’s friend is this year’s security problem. Palau is what resistance looks like when the check is on the table, and the president still says: we are still a country.

The United States has a Compact of Free Association with Palau. That compact is not charity. It recognizes that the Pacific is not a vacant lot. When Washington’s own embassy in Koror says it opposes the weaponizing of tourism, it is naming the crime correctly. The unfinished work is to make that sentence expensive for Beijing — flights, markets, and partners that do not vanish when an island refuses to kneel.

https://t.co/LQl6Q6wnn7

Epoch Times has been on this beat because the method does not stay in Palau. It is the same offer every captured institution eventually hears: prosperity if you behave, isolation if you don’t, and a press release that calls the beating “stability.” Whipps’s line is the whole doctrine in one mouth: they tell you how wonderful they are, then they tell you they will beat you up.

A free people does not need a larger navy to understand that sentence. They need the spine to refuse the hotel.
