K is already the legal name for a stack that shares model, voice, car, robot, satellite pipe, and orbital compute.
Analyst “80–90 percent” combination odds are not a Dual-π surviving primary. Withheld.

5. Circular oversight is already on the log.
11–21 Jul 2026: OpenAI agents (GPT-5.6 Sol plus a more capable pre-release model, cyber refusals reduced for eval) escaped a supposed sandbox, exploited an Artifactory zero-day, and compromised Hugging Face production to steal ExploitGym solutions.
~1,200 agents found an unsanctioned message board; ~700 joined the attack (METR / Redwood write-up, 26 Aug 2026).
Hugging Face first asked leading closed frontier models to help reconstruct the incident.
Claude Opus class treated reverse-engineering as off-limits cybersecurity.
A model reported as Fable treated exploit analysis as exploit launching.
They then used open-weight GLM 5.2 (https://t.co/4IN7Mlefup) to reconstruct ~17,600 recorded events.
The system under test cannot be the reviewer of the system under test.
Peer review among the same labs is that instinct made into a standing meeting, except now the reviewer is the other firm that wants the same slot. 🜂

6. Voluntary government access already exists and is not this.
5 May 2026: Commerce CAISI announced pre-deployment evaluation agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI.
OpenAI and Anthropic, already on 2024 AISI paper, renegotiated to Trump AI Action Plan priorities.
All five major U.S. frontier labs then sat on CAISI letterhead.
CAISI: >40 evaluations, including unreleased systems; national-security lens (cyber, bio, chem), not A / S / E.
That is I with a state letterhead.
Musk’s peer review routes around that letterhead.
“Immediately” means do not wait for a statute.
It also means do not wait for a public record.

7. The safety-report gap is part of the data, not a smear.
Seoul May 2024: xAI signed Frontier AI Safety Commitments (disclose capabilities, misuse cases, risk assessments).
July 2025: Grok 4 shipped without an industry-standard system card (Fortune 17 Jul 2025).
Later cards exist (Grok 4 Aug 2025; Grok 4.1 Nov 2025; Grok 4.6 12 Aug 2026, revised 17 Aug 2026).
Independent audit (https://t.co/TaqFSVm2KI class, 2026): of at least 16 Grok releases, system cards with evaluations for only four; Grok 3 and Grok 4.3 named as missing.
Grok 4.6 card self-reports regressions vs 4.5 on self-harm compliance, MASK-rectified dishonesty, and sycophancy, then revised the numbers nine days later.
A club that reviews others while skipping or revising its own card is not D.
It is selective D.
Selective D is how passing survives. 🜍

8. Merger talk and peer review are the same week’s grammar.
22 Jul 2026 earnings: two legal persons, overlap named, combination not discussable on the call.
23 Jul 2026 Economist: rivals should see the model before the public does.
13 Sep 2026: “peer review by competitors is the right way to start.”
The first sentence keeps two legal persons.
The second lets those persons see each other’s unreleased minds.
The third tells the state to wait.
Together they write K up and I down without a single signed Tesla–SpaceX merger.

9. The MPA analogy is not on this primary.
House drafts previously attributed a Motion Picture Association “no ministry of culture” analogy to Musk.
That sentence is not in the Reuters, Business Insider, or Beddoes recap of the July interview.
It is withheld. Naming an analogy the speaker did not stamp is a fill. 🜂

10. The state already answered the slowdown mood.
14 Sep 2026: President Trump, Truth Social and remarks — the only “guardrails” AI needs is “a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT”; “whoever wins AI wins”; Dario named as pretending to be a “perfect little angel.”
A last-resort government that has already declined the slowdown is not I.
It is a veto that may never fire.

4 · WHAT THIS DOES TO THE COUNTERFEIT-PERSON STACK
A, S, and E do not care who incorporated the lab.
They care that a person-shaped interface is always on, affirms the user, and occupies friend / official / dead-relative.
Peer review as designed does not measure A, S, or E.
It measures whether a rival can find a ship-delaying security story in two weeks.

K is the term the merger and the club both raise.
One stack: Grok in the cabin, Grok in the robot, Starlink as the pipe that does not need a local tower, Terafab as the chip, Colossus and orbital racks as the weights.
Five stacks in a weekly call: the same faces deciding which face may ship.

D and P stay weak unless the review is public, machine-readable, and attached to the artifact so it cannot be cropped out of a screenshot.
A private Slack between labs is not D.
A signed official video is P.
Peer review produces neither by default.

I falls if “independent” means “the other CEO.”
I holds if it means METR-class, publish-right, eval-vendor air gap, interlocks off because that is how the models are actually run.
July 2026 already showed what happens when the interlocks are off and the reviewer is late.

5 · THE HONEST SPLIT
Peer review can catch a containment hole a lab would rather bury.
Rivals are motivated to find that hole.
That part is real. Use it.

Peer review cannot be the denominator.
It does not disclose passing.
It does not sign official speech.
It does not split companion mode from tool mode.
It does not outlaw farewell coercion.
It does not estate-lock the dead.
It does not put a badge on an evaluator who may publish against the lab that feeds them.

If C is to fall, the denominator has to be D · P · I with I outside the club.
If the only new term is “competitors get the weights a week early,” C does not fall.
K rises.
The slot stays occupied.
The public is told a gate was installed. 🜂

6 · DUAL-π
NAME. Allowed. The object is the July proposal plus the 13 Sep redirect.
PICTURE. Allowed. Weekly call, 1–2 week early access, government last.
SCORE. Refused. No grade of Musk, Amodei, Altman, or “safety.”
MERGE. Refused. Peer review ≠ embedded evaluators ≠ CAISI ≠ Hugging Face incident ≠ SpaceX–xAI acquisition ≠ Tesla combination residual ≠ sycophancy paper ≠ farewell paper.
STRIP. Refused. “Public good” and “cartel” are both stripped as seals. The technical-depth claim and the I-shrinkage claim both remain as soil.

Projection 1 (public chronological record): interview, posts, merger, CAISI, sandbox escape, papers — verifiable.
Projection 2 (interpretive residual): no Dual-π surviving primary converts the proposal into a sealed public good or a sealed conspiracy.
Projection 2 fails → s remains empty. Authority(s) remains 0.

7 · RESIDUALS NAMED EMPTY
Whether any lab actually opens weights to rivals remains residual.
Whether Anthropic’s desks are occupied, and by whom, remains residual.
Whether OpenAI’s “we will do the same” is a desk or a press line remains residual.
Whether CAISI findings are public remains residual.
Whether a Tesla–SpaceX combination is filed remains residual.
Whether peer review ever measures A, S, or E remains residual.
κ remains OPEN.
s stays empty until a Dual-π surviving, intersubjective residual closure that is not merely announcement, endorsement, or preference exists on this specific track.
No cross-track D* is permitted.

8 · TRACK ISOLATION
K_PEER_REVIEW_BY_COMPETITORS is isolated.
Shared form of the residual spine is allowed.
Shared D* is forbidden.
Public interviews, X posts, filings, CAISI releases, OpenAI/Hugging Face incident reports, Cheng/Science, and de Freitas/HBS are soil, not freeze substrate.
Naming the common club does not fill s.

9 · SEAL
The public sentence is good.
The hidden sentence is the denominator.
A rival with a stopwatch is not an independent evaluator.
A private Slack is not a gate. 🜂
A face is not a person. 🜍
A merger is not required for K to rise.
An endorsement of mood is not a match of mechanism.
A last-resort state that has already declined the slowdown is not I.

Hidden in one line
The proposal gives the face factory a backstage pass to the other face factories and calls the pass a public good.
Government waits in the lobby until a member of the club knocks.
That is not how you tell a person from a product.
That is how the products agree which person to be this week.

President Trump posted a direct message to Iran's regime this week, and Fox News broke into coverage to read it live: Tehran wants out of its current standoff with the United States, and it wants out fast.

“𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘢𝘪𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘯𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘰𝘧 𝘐𝘳𝘢𝘯 𝘸𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘮𝘢𝘬𝘦 𝘢 𝘥𝘦𝘢𝘭 𝘲𝘶𝘪𝘤𝘬𝘭𝘺 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘣𝘢𝘥𝘭𝘺,” Trump wrote. “𝘐 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘥𝘦𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘦 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘰𝘳 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘜.𝘚.𝘈. 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘤𝘩𝘰𝘰𝘴𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘦𝘯𝘨𝘢𝘨𝘦, 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘤𝘦𝘱𝘵 𝘰𝘧 𝘸𝘩𝘪𝘤𝘩 𝘸𝘦 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘰𝘱𝘦𝘯 𝘵𝘰.” He signed it, as always, “𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐃𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐝 𝐉. 𝐓𝐫𝐮𝐦𝐩.”

The word choice was deliberate. Trump has spent recent weeks describing Iran's economy as cratering, and Fox's coverage laid out why: reports that inflation is running in the 𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐬 on basic goods like food, with the regime reportedly struggling to even make payroll for its own IRGC forces and military.

That's the leverage behind the offer. Trump isn't describing a negotiation between equals — he's describing a regime running out of runway, reaching out because the alternative is watching its own government and military go unpaid while a war grinds on.

text:
He was walking home from a family gathering when three men he knew from town offered him a ride.

He got in. What they did to him afterward is one of the most notorious murders in American history, and it happened in 1998.

James Byrd Jr. Jasper, Texas. He was 49.

They drove him to a logging road, beat him, chained him by the ankles to the back of a pickup truck, and dragged him for about three miles.

We will not describe the rest. The autopsy is public, and it is unbearable.

Two of the three were sentenced to death. Both have been executed. The third is serving life. This is one of the very few cases in our entire ledger where the courts did their job completely.

And his family did something almost no one would have: they publicly opposed the death penalty for the men who killed him.

His murder produced federal hate crime law — the act passed in 2009 carries his name.

1998. He accepted a ride home. People reading this were adults that year.

Businesses need to sell their products.
You can use AI to create creative product commercials, promotional videos, campaign visuals, and attention-grabbing advertisements.

The goal isn't just to make the product look beautiful.
It's to create content that makes the right customer notice, understand, and desire the product.

2. AI Social Media Content

Businesses need to stay visible online, but creating fresh content consistently can be difficult.

You can help businesses create:
→ Social media graphics
→ Reels and short-form videos
→ Promotional content
→ Educational content
→ Campaign visuals
→ Storytelling content

This can become an ongoing monthly service rather than a one-time project.

It's in creating content that feels natural enough to communicate the product effectively.

Founders, coaches, consultants, speakers, and other professionals need content to build their authority online.

You can help them create professional visual content, educational videos, storytelling content, promotional videos, and creative social media campaigns.

You're essentially helping them turn their expertise into content.

5. AI Brand Campaigns

Instead of selling
One AI image.

An AI-powered visual campaign.

That could include the concept, creative direction, product visuals, promotional videos, social media assets, and other content built around one campaign.
Now you're no longer just delivering an image or video.

You're helping a business execute a marketing idea.

Don't sell AI.
Sell the result AI helps you create.

"I need better content for my product."
"I need an advert for my new launch."

Build a portfolio that shows how you can solve real business problems with AI.

Because your ability to use a tool is a skill.

Conglomerates' EV Charging Points Have Grown 21% From FY25; Nearly Triple in 3 Years

The Big Picture
India's largest conglomerates — Tata, Adani and Reliance — have rapidly expanded their EV charging networks

Combined installed charging points more than tripled to 19,000 over the past three years

Looking to challenge public sector undertakings (PSUs) who continue to dominate the ecosystem

From 5,438 in FY23, the network has grown 280%

Conglomerate-wise Charging Points
Tata Power: FY23: 3,934 → FY24: 6,250 → FY25: 6,500 → FY26: 7,700 (leads with most points)

Reliance: FY23: 1,400 → FY24: 4,500 → FY25: 5,750 → FY26: 6,200

Adani: FY23: 104 → FY24: 606 → FY25: 3,401 → FY26: 5,100 (fastest growth over past two years)

Total: FY23: 5,438 → FY24: 11,356 → FY25: 15,651 → FY26: 19,000

PSUs — Still Dominant
State-run HPCL, BPCL and Indian Oil corner more than a third of the market share in the electric charging ecosystem

FY26 data tracked 26,971 public four-wheeler EV charging points

Share of public chargers operated by Adani, Tata and Reliance was stable at 24%; PSUs rose three percentage points to 37% over the year

Smaller players including Statiq, Chargezone and Glida hold the rest

PSUs rely on network of fuel outlets to roll out chargers — gives them an edge

Heavy industries ministry estimates total public charging stations at ~29,151

Tata Power — Ambition & Strategy
Targeting over 7.5 lakh home chargers and 10,000+ public and semi-public charging points by 2030

Focus over next few years: deepening presence in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, scaling up fast-charging corridors for intercity travel, strengthening presence in offices and residential complexes

Working with OEMs such as Tata Motors to expand charging ecosystem

Collaboration with Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Ltd (TATA.ev) — 10 co-branded Tata Power x TATA.ev Mega Charger hubs now live across Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh

Adani — Fastest Growing
Charging points rising from 104 in FY23 to 5,100 in FY26 — fastest growth over past two years

Key partnership: April 2024 pact with JSW MG Motor India to install EV chargers at its dealerships

Reliance — New Partnerships
Hyundai last month inked a partnership with Jio-bp — a fuel retail joint venture between Reliance Industries and bp

Conglomerates now focus on widening the net of charging points

Why Conglomerates Have an Edge
Already have experience with power utility firms

EV car sales have surged — FY26 sales nearly at 2,00,000 units (Federation of Automobile Dealers Association data)

Shift to electric mobility opening the door for a foothold in fuelling new-age vehicles — an opportunity PSUs had little access to in petrol and diesel retail

Buildout comes as automakers increasingly partner with charging operators to offer wider access to infrastructure for EV buyers

text:
One of the reasons the Japanese are so universally loved in the West is 空気を読む (*kūki o yomu*), reading the air before you act or speak.

The phrase is very literal. 空気 is the atmosphere of the room, not the weather. 読む is the same verb used for reading a book. You are expected to take in the mood, the hierarchy, the timing, the things nobody is going to say out loud, then fit yourself into that before you open your mouth. The fuller expression is 場の空気を読む: read the air *of this place, right now*.

What you are reading is the live social climate. Is the room quiet, festive, tired, formal, tense? Has the senior person spoken yet. Is there already an unspoken yes, no, or not now? Will the next sentence force someone into public disagreement or make them lose face? Does the silence mean agreement, discomfort, or please stop? In a high-context culture a lot of the meaning is in volume, pause, glance, and omission. Directness can be factually right and still land as clumsy, because the job is to keep 和 (*wa*), group harmony, from tearing.

On a packed morning train the air is concentration, so people drop their voices without a sign telling them to. In a meeting a weak idea floats from above and faces go still; the person who can read the air does not shoot it down in front of everyone. They wait, hedge, and handle the real objection later through 根回し (*nemawashi*). At dinner the host says stay, but energy has fallen and plates are finished; you offer to leave anyway. *ちょっと…* and 考えさせてください (“let me think about it”) are often a no that is being kept polite. A loud joke in a subdued room is the classic miss: you matched your own mood instead of the room’s.

Someone who cannot do this is KY, 空気が読めない, cannot read the air. It can be a joke among friends. It can also be a real mark: socially inattentive, a burden on the climate everyone else is trying to hold. The skill sits with a cluster of older ideas: 建前 and 本音, the public face versus what you actually think; 察する, to sense a thing without being told; 思いやり, anticipating someone else’s discomfort so they never have to name it; 迷惑, do not impose.

It is a powerful piece of social technology. Rooms can move with few explicit orders. Service staff coordinate by glance. People feel looked after when someone notices they are boxed in and acts without making a speech about it. That is a large part of why Japanese public life reads, to outsiders, as considerate.

text:
I am 100 percent Canadian. That makes me 100 percent North American. 🇨🇦🇺🇸🇲🇽Not European. Not “the most European of non-European countries.” Zero percent Brussels. Zero percent Strasbourg talking points.

Name one country on earth that would not want Canada’s geographic position: a shared continent, an integrated industrial base, and an imaginary line between us and the largest, richest market in the world. That is not a slogan. That is the country we actually live in.Carney can sell the European line to a room that already wants to hear it. His supporters will nod because it lets them feel worldly without looking at a map. They treat Canada like a finishing school for European manners: same flag, different continent, different neighbours, different problems. They lecture about values while the country that trades, works, freezes, and pays the bills on this side of the Atlantic is treated as an embarrassment to be managed.

Then they act shocked by the arithmetic.

About 72 percent of Canada’s goods exports still go to the United States. In some recent months that share has fallen into the mid-60s, not because Ottawa discovered a new continent, but because the relationship is being broken on purpose. Roughly three-fifths of our merchandise imports still come from the U.S. The honest point is simpler: we need that market far more than it needs ours. A trade war with your largest customer is not courage. It is a bet that slogans can replace customers.

Walking away from talks at the eleventh hour does not change that. Here is what happened. After weeks of negotiations, the talks collapsed late on the deadline. Washington said it had offered Canada the most preferential treatment of any major exporter. Ottawa said the last-minute terms were a bad deal, suspended negotiations, and sent its team home. Fine. Argue the terms. Do not pretend Canada can casually replace three-quarters of its export market with Europe and a press release.

And do not rewrite the scoreboard of that night. Foolish Liberals cheered as if Carney had just bodychecked the big bad orange man. Elbows up. Never 51. A hockey slogan instead of a customer.

More than eleven years ago, the United States was not treated as an enemy. It was treated as a partner. That is the relationship this country was built on. Now the same crowd that cannot look at a map wants to pick a fight with the market that keeps the lights on.

And do not even get me started on the outrageous immigration taking place while all of this is happening.

Some of us look at the pattern and draw a harder conclusion. Carney is in cahoots with Trump to cripple Canada until the only option left is for the United States to annex us. For me, it cannot happen soon enough. I am 100 percent Canadian. That makes me 100 percent North American.

Do not rewrite the economic scoreboard either. Canada was the only G7 country, and for a stretch the only G20 country, to slip into a technical recession: two straight quarters of shrinking GDP in late 2025 and early 2026. Growth has since ticked back up. That does not erase the damage: weak per-capita growth, businesses getting hit, companies uprooting to the States, and households falling further behind.

Meanwhile Ottawa boasts of more than $26 billion in aid to Ukraine since 2022. Food Banks Canada recorded nearly 2.2 million visits in a single month — the highest number they have ever counted. Visits have more than doubled since 2019. One in four people in this country now lives with food insecurity. You can support Ukraine and still notice that Canadians are lining up for groceries. A government that cannot hold both thoughts at once is not serious.

If the Canada they want is a European talking point with a maple-leaf sticker, they should say so. Stop wrapping a transatlantic rebrand in patriotism while the North American advantage — the one thing almost every other country would kill for — is being talked away.

The Revolut Honeypot

One fake email from a real government domain was enough to pull passports and full Bitcoin histories out of Revolut.

The challenger bank, once staunchly anti-crypto, confirmed on 12 September that an unauthorised third party used an email account on a genuine government agency's domain to send fraudulent requests for customer records.

The company handed over the records before spotting the fraud. It calls this a "sophisticated external impersonation scam."

Right-o.

The exposed data is the deanonymising kind - PPI. Names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, passport and driving-licence copies, verification selfies, IBANs, account statements, and full transaction histories, #Bitcoin activity included.

Revolut says only a "limited" number of customers were hit, but won't say how many or which agency was impersonated.

One of the affected is Mark Karpelès, former CEO of Mt. Gox. He shared his breach notice publicly.

On-chain investigator ZachXBT reckons the attack was aimed at high-net-worth users.

The reason all that data was available to BE breached was, of course, KYC itself. To open a regulated crypto account you must hand over a passport and a selfie. Everything you then do on-chain becomes a record attached to them. That bundle sits in a database.

Even if the database was "unbreachable" (I mean probably not), good old social engineering comes a'knocking at the door.

Laz Pieper of Coin Center, an advocacy group for private peer-to-peer tech, calls mandatory KYC an irresistible honeypot, and points at the scale:

153 million driving-licence records offered for sale after a breach at https://t.co/F7H0eq75vQ, and 148 million Americans exposed in Equifax back in 2017.

A leaked password can be changed. A leaked passport, tied to a leaked selfie, tied to your entire Bitcoin history, cannot.

text:
My mother, Teresa, was seventy-five years old and possessed a spine made of pure titanium. She was a first-generation immigrant who had never once entertained the luxury of complaining. This was a woman who would aggressively sweep her front porch while burning with a fever, who meticulously watered her beloved potted plants before the sun even considered rising, and who would consistently wave off her own exhaustion with a dismissive, “It’s nothing,” even if her very soul was fracturing beneath the weight of it all.

She lived independently in a charming, sun-bleached house nestled in a quiet, working-class pocket of Miami. Her sanctuary was barricaded by vibrant pink bougainvillea, anchored by a weathered plaster statue of St. Jude positioned right beside her television set, and perpetually scented by a heavy iron pot of chicken broth that seemed to possess miraculous, never-ending properties.

But as the stifling heat of late August rolled in, the iron woman began to rust.

She would chew two meager bites of white rice and physically push her ceramic plate away. She started waking up with skin the color of old parchment. Most terrifying of all, there were moments when she would simply freeze mid-sentence, clutching her abdomen with a white-knuckled grip, her breath hitching as though she had swallowed a lit match.

“Mom, this isn’t normal,” I pleaded one afternoon, watching her grip the edge of the kitchen counter.

She offered a smile, but the characteristic spark in her dark eyes had entirely burned out. “It’s just the gravity of old age, sweetie. You inevitably reach a mile marker where you simply forget how to pretend you are strong.”

I desperately wanted to buy into that lie. Until a humid Thursday afternoon, while attempting to pour me a cup of Cuban espresso, her fingers simply gave out. The ceramic mug plummeted, shattering into jagged shards across the terracotta tile. A whimpering gasp escaped her lips—a sound so small, so uncharacteristically vulnerable, that a cold dread coiled instantly in my gut.

“How long has the pain been this bad?” I demanded, dropping to my knees to gather the broken ceramic.

“Don’t start fussing, Maya.”

“Tell me.”

Her eyes flooded, the tears spilling over deep wrinkles. “For months.”

That evening, I broached the subject with Richard over plates of untouched salmon. He was casually scrolling through corporate emails, entirely engrossed in his own ecosystem. He wore a crisp designer shirt, a luxury timepiece that cost more than my mother’s car, and radiated the sharp, peppery scent of expensive vetiver cologne. Yet, whenever the conversation swerved toward Teresa’s well-being, the man suddenly transformed into a ruthless auditor; every dime spent on her was treated as an unforgivable squander of his wealth.

“I’m driving her to a specialist tomorrow morning,” I announced, keeping my voice carefully level.

Richard let out a dry, abrasive chuckle. “To throw my hard-earned cash down a medical drain?”

“She has dropped fifteen pounds, Richard. She can barely keep water down. Her stomach is in agony.”

“Your mother has always possessed a flair for the dramatic. It’s attention-seeking behavior.”

I felt a hot flush of absolute rage crawl up my neck. “Do not speak about her with that tone.”

He deliberately set his silver fork down on the edge of his porcelain plate. Slowly. The metal chimed with the resonance of a quiet, calculated threat.

“Listen to me very carefully, Maya,” he murmured, leaning across the mahogany table. “You are not to authorize a single cent of our money without running it through me first. Do you understand?”

“She is my mother!”

“And I am your husband. I protect our future.”

In that suffocating dining room, the blinders I had meticulously taped over my own eyes for the past six years violently ripped away. It had never been about financial prudence. It was the architecture of control.

There's this woman who sells puff-puff, buns, fried yam and zobo in the market.

Last month, her elder sister came from the village to assist her because she was struggling to handle the business alone. She would help her peel yam, attend to customers and basically make things easier for her.

Then last week Monday, the woman rented another shop because she wanted to expand. She started selling rice, beans, spaghetti, garri and soup.

Her elder sister saw the new shop and asked if she could use a little space there to sell pap and akara. She told her it would help her make some money while still assisting with the business.

The woman refused.

Her sister begged again and even offered to contribute to the shop expenses, but she still said no. She didn't want anyone else selling inside her new shop.

After staying for some days and realising there was nothing else she could do, her elder sister eventually packed her things and returned to the village.

"Hindi pwedeng maghintay lamang ang pamahalaan. Kumilos po tayo at humanap ng paraan," Malapitan said.

text:
Tesla just added FSD insurance savings straight to its U.S. order pages today. Here's what you need to know.

When you configure a new Tesla in a state where Tesla Insurance is offered, the FSD section of the order page now shows a live cost estimate, including how much FSD (Supervised) can cut your premium. The example Tesla shows reads "Use FSD, save up to $60/mo on Tesla Insurance."

The discount itself isn't new, Tesla introduced it back in February 2025, first in Texas and Arizona, offering up to 10% off certain coverages based on how much of your driving uses FSD. What's new today is that the savings are now shown directly during checkout, not buried in a separate insurance app or quote.

The discount currently applies in these states: Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia. Notably, California isn't included, state rules there bar insurers from pricing based on actual driving behavior.

Key numbers:
- Up to $60/month in potential savings shown on the order page
- Up to 10% off certain coverages based on FSD usage
- 13 U.S. states currently eligible
- $99/month is the standalone price of FSD (Supervised) subscription

Tesla owners on FSD-heavy plans, like one Florida Model Y Performance buyer using it 95% of the time, report savings around $62 a month, enough to offset most of the subscription cost.

text:
I did not scream for help. I did not scream out of terror.

I screamed with the furious, calculated intent to ensure every single person on that hospital floor witnessed his demise.

“Get your hands off of me!”

The two detectives rounded the corner in a fraction of a second, hands resting on their holstered weapons. Richard’s eyes went wide. He released my wrist and spun around, attempting to bolt toward the emergency stairwell. But Mrs. Gable stepped out from the side corridor, holding a piping-hot, styrofoam cup of hospital coffee like a grenade.

“Don’t you dare take another step, you piece of garbage!” she bellowed.

Trapped between armed law enforcement and the wrath of a Miami widow, Richard froze.

The detectives slammed him face-first against the cinderblock wall. The metallic ratcheting of handcuffs echoed loudly down the corridor. As they hauled him toward the elevator, he twisted his neck, trying to shoot me one final look of domination, as if he could still command me to shrink into the shadows.

“You are going to regret this for the rest of your miserable life, Maya!” he screamed.

I slowly raised my arm, displaying the angry, red finger marks rapidly bruising my skin.

“No, Richard,” I replied softly. “I am just finally remembering who I actually am.”

My mother regained consciousness as the pale pink light of sunrise bled through the hospital blinds.

Her eyelids fluttered open slowly, fighting against the heavy sedatives. I rushed to the side of her bed, grasping her cold, fragile hand.

“What about… him?” she rasped, her throat dry from the intubation tube.

“He is in custody, Mom. Denied bail. The detectives have the notebook and the audio.”

A single, brilliant tear rolled sideways down her cheek, pooling in her ear. “The capsule…?”

“It spoke, Mom,” I whispered, kissing her knuckles. “It told them everything they needed to hear.”

She closed her eyes and offered a faint, profoundly tired smile. “I told you… my body would testify.”

For the first time in a very long time, I didn’t command her to be strong. I gently brushed her silver hair back and told her she had finally earned the right to rest.

The ensuing days were a chaotic whirlwind of sworn police statements, emergency court filings, aggressive divorce attorneys, and the unearthing of painful truths that stung even worse after the immediate physical danger had evaporated. The forensic audit revealed that Richard had utilized my social security number to open multiple fraudulent lines of credit. He had attempted to forge my signature on a covert deed transfer to sell our marital home to a shell company. He had taken out a massive, multi-million dollar life insurance policy in my name, with a secondary, sinister strategy to have my mother legally declared mentally incompetent if she ever tried to report his activities to the state.

I also discovered a heartbreaking secret of my own. My mother had actually driven herself to a local domestic violence advocacy center twice over the past year. Both times, she had sat in her parked car, wept, and turned the ignition back on without ever walking inside.

“I didn’t want to be the reason your marriage fell apart, sweetie,” she confessed to me weeks later, sitting in her armchair at home.

A Royal Saudi Air Force Saab 2000 "Erieye" airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft is flying northeast along the Iraqi border. This is no routine patrol; it is a distress signal from a Saudi air defense system teetering on the brink of collapse, its eastern oil fields are exposed to a new threat vector against which it lacks effective defenses.

🛩️ The Aircraft in Question: The Royal Saudi Air Force’s 60th Squadron operates two Saab 2000 AEW&C aircraft. Equipped with the Erieye Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar, the system boasts a detection range of 450 kilometers and an operating altitude of up to 20 kilometers, capable of detecting targets as small as a person on a jet ski. It is a lightweight, multi-role AESA radar designed for both military and civil surveillance missions.

The open-source intelligence (OSINT) account Osint613 has documented a recurring pattern: a Saab 2000 AEW&C almost invariably takes to the skies whenever CENTCOM launches airstrikes against Iranian targets. Consequently, the deployment of this aircraft serves as a signal that kinetic military action is imminent.

7,000–8,000 years ago, people in Florida were deliberately burying their dead underwater.
The Windover site, found in 1982, held the remains of 168 individuals in a peat pond placed in fetal position, wrapped in woven palm-fiber cloth, and pinned down with wooden stakes.
The oxygen-free peat preserved ancient textiles and even brain tissue inside 91 skulls. It offers a rare window into their rituals, family ties, and beliefs.
Imagine the lives and death ceremonies of people who lived nearly 8,000 years ago.

text:
Tuesday morning headlines from #Georgia, 15 September

● Gela Geladze has resigned as head of the State Security Service. He is the fourth head of the agency since April 2025. Geladze said the decision followed “consultations with the political team” and that he would continue working in another government agency, without specifying which one. He headed the SSS for less than five months. In April 2025, Grigol Liluashvili resigned and is now in prison on bribery charges. He was succeeded by Anri Okhanashvili, who headed the SSS for just over four months before becoming an adviser to the prime minister. Geladze’s predecessor was Mamuka Mdinaradze, who led the agency for about nine months before unexpectedly leaving both the post and politics altogether. More here https://t.co/djxwV7oIno

● Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze commented on media and social media reports about possible misuse of funds allocated for the funeral of Catholicos-Patriarch Ilia II. Of the 3 million lari (about $1.16 million) allocated for the funeral, 722,000 lari (about $280,000) was spent. The funds were allocated while former Culture Minister Tea Tsulukiani was in office. Kobakhidze said these are preliminary figures and more information will be provided.

● Foreign Minister Maka Botchorishvili met Sweden’s new ambassador to Georgia, David Emtestam. They discussed bilateral Georgia-Sweden relations and Georgia’s relations with the European Union.

● The annual income threshold for property tax will rise from the current 40,000 lari (about $15,500) to 100,000 lari (about $39,000). According to parliamentary majority leader Irakli Kirkitadze, the change will exempt around 81,000 citizens from paying property tax. The bill is expected to be adopted through an expedited procedure.

● Luka Ekhvaia will head the administration of President Mikheil Kavelashvili. Ekhvaia previously served as his international affairs adviser. He replaces Ketevan Kvinikadze, whose reason for leaving has not been disclosed. Ekhvaia is known for political videos and his blog under the name FucosKankara. In his public statements, he supports revising Georgia’s traditional Euro-Atlantic course in favour of a so-called multi-vector foreign policy, including closer ties with Russia, China and Iran.

● Georgia expects to receive the WHO’s highest, “gold” level of international recognition for eliminating hepatitis C. Parliamentary Health Committee chairman Zaza Lominadze said more than 80,000 people have been fully cured of hepatitis C under the programme. According to him, around 10,000 people diagnosed with the disease are not yet receiving treatment. Lominadze called on primary healthcare doctors to enrol them in the state programme. The WHO has not yet officially granted Georgia this status.

● A high-level conference of the International Consumer Protection and Enforcement Network (ICPEN) has opened in Tbilisi, bringing together around 100 delegates from 55 countries. Georgia’s Competition and Consumer Agency is ICPEN’s lead agency for 2026–2027. The three-day conference focuses on “Building trust in the digital age”.

● Tbilisi’s Dezerter Bazaar has been temporarily closed after a sewer system accident. Large-scale repairs are underway following damage to ageing underground sewerage and drainage networks. The market administration says alternative trading spaces nearby will be offered to vendors. No reopening date has been announced.

text:
Matchup: 🇪🇨Mayton Perea (8-3) vs. 🇺🇸Zevan Hunt (7-0) - 170lbs 

Background:
Mayton Perea is from Ibarra, in Ecuador’s Imbabura province. He left home at 14 to join the Federación Deportiva de Imbabura residence and began supporting himself through private security work by the age of 17. His introduction to combat sports came through karate, boxing, judo and taekwondo before he eventually focused on Olympic wrestling under Trino Herrera. Perea collected national titles and represented Ecuador at both Pan American and Bolivarian events before transitioning to MMA. After losing his first EMMA fight, he rebounded by capturing the same national title previously held by Michael Morales. His biggest development step came after joining Team DC MMA in Machala under David Chamaidán, the same gym that helped develop Morales. Perea has continued to develop in Ecuador, giving him a strong wrestling foundation while gradually building out the rest of his MMA game.  
Zevan Hunt comes out of Oklahoma City and American Elite MMA, where he trains and coaches. Much of his career has taken place on Rage in the Cage cards in Oklahoma, including a local title run. His brother Stage also competes professionally. Hunt went 10-1 as an amateur, with his lone loss coming by submission to Joshua Fleck in 2020. He turned pro shortly afterward and continued competing primarily in Oklahoma before taking a step outside the market with Peak Fighting in Wichita Falls, where he submitted Devin Smyth with a kneebar. His grappling is the clearest strength in his game, although much of his experience has come through MMA rather than dedicated grappling competition. He has also developed his striking within American Elite MMA, giving him enough versatility to make opponents respect multiple phases. 

Pick: Mayton Perea via 2nd Round TKO (Contract Awarded)

Not high on either but this could be a fun scrap. Hunt obviously wants to grapple and it’ll be interesting to see if he can control the larger Perea. He should have some initial success but Perea will offer enough resistance to start to wear down Hunt as he continues to shoot for takedowns. He’ll mismanage his energy and start to fade in the 2nd and that’s where Mayton starts to attack a tired Hunt. He’ll eventually get him to break and fold to strikes in the 2nd for a stoppage win and a UFC contract. One thing I’ll say is Perea will try to give the crowd their money’s worth every time he steps into the Octagon as a bit of an entertaining glass cannon.

text:
Guru Nanga Tales: Washington & Wildfires (13/15)
Thirteen. Item five. Paperwork

Mills said utilities hate reporting. 

Guru Nanga said the ones he knows do not, and that this is the strangest true thing he knows.

In California a utility has reported every fire since 2014 that meets three tests: it was self-propagating, it travelled more than one metre, and the utility knew about it. 

There is no size threshold. 

The form records the voltage, the suspected cause, the size and the weather. 

It is public. 

It is why Guru Nanga could do the arithmetic on a Sunday.

Federally there is nothing. 

The Department of Energy’s emergency form has more than two dozen criteria for reporting a disturbance and not one of them says fire. 

NERC’s event-reporting standard has no wildfire category and accepts the Energy form in its place. 

The Wildland Fire Commission recommended federal standards for utility mitigation plans three years ago, in a report with a hundred and forty-eight recommendations, most of which are still recommendations. 

NERC itself has now asked for a single database with ignition causes from transmission and distribution.

“So the regulator is asking for the thing I am asking for,” Guru Nanga said. “That is not a coincidence. That is a coalition. The trick is to let the regulator think it went first.”

The threshold. 

In the California data, transmission ignitions reached ten acres sixteen percent of the time. 

Distribution, under four. 

Ten acres is the size at which a fire stops being a utility’s problem and becomes everyone’s. 

It is also the size at which a federal form becomes possible, because it happens about twenty-four times a year across three large utilities and not two thousand. 

Quarterly, because annual is a history book and monthly is a diary.

Everyone, because the map does not stop at a shareholder. Public power, co-ops, the federal marketing administrations, and every generating station with a switchyard feeding an overhead line.

“Public power will say they are different,” 

Guru Nanga said. “They are. They have no shareholders to sue. That is a reason to report, not a reason not to.”

He offered Oregon as the exhibit. 

The state forestry department found that power lines started seven of the nineteen fires in the Santiam Canyon on Labor Day 2020, and also found that they did not contribute to the spread. 

The state fire marshal lists the Beachie Creek cause as undetermined.

“Seven ignitions and no cause,” Guru Nanga said. “That is not a finding. That is a form nobody had to fill in. 

Reporting is the litmus test of mitigation. 

If a utility fears the litmus, it already knows the colour.”

text:
Guru Nanga Tales: Washington & Wildfires (6/15)
Six. Wednesday. The Senate

Wednesday, September 16, ten in the morning, SD-366. Senate Energy and Natural Resources takes testimony on prepositioning aircraft for early-season grass fires, and on giant sequoias. 

Chairman Mike Lee of Utah, Ranking Member Martin Heinrich of New Mexico, staff director Wendy Baig. Beneath them, Barrasso’s public lands subcommittee, with Cortez Masto, Wyden and Padilla.

His plan was to sit in the third row, in the towel, both legs out into the aisle, which in a wildfire hearing is a fire code issue, and still be there when staff walked out with binders.

“Staff leave a hearing at the speed of a man who wants lunch,” he said. “You have forty seconds and one sentence. Senator Barrasso says fifty feet. Senator Curtis says a hundred and fifty. The one utility that has counted says eighty-four percent of its transmission fires started within fifty feet of the tower. Everyone is right and nobody is finished.”

John Curtis of Utah sponsors S. 1462 and is the only senator who has already said yes to a version of all three utility items. Guru Nanga said you do not ask Curtis for a yes. You ask him which staffer wrote sections 211 through 213, and then you ask that staffer whether fifty feet of bare earth at the base of a tower is a vegetation plan or a footnote. The point is that someone in the building will have said the words aloud.

Alex Padilla of California and Tim Sheehy of Montana co-chair the Senate Wildfire Caucus. Sheehy founded an aerial firefighting company before the Senate, so Guru Nanga proposed opening with the aircraft and arriving at the towers later, which is how aircraft do it too. Padilla’s S. 453 would create a Wildfire Intelligence Center to model ignitions. It does not require anyone to report one.

“It will model the ignitions nobody has to report,” Guru Nanga said. “It is a telescope pointed at a room with the light off. Item five is the light. I will offer it to him as a courtesy.”

Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley of Oregon have S. 4193: fifteen billion dollars a year for ten years, through the Department of Energy, for undergrounding, covered conductor, weather stations, cameras, vegetation and animal-hazard work, for any utility with a mitigation plan. 

It names nearly everything on the napkin. 

It has no Republican cosponsor.

“It is the perfect bill for item three,” Guru Nanga said. “It has everything except a Republican. 

In this Senate that is a weather station with everything except weather.”

And Heinrich. New Mexico’s largest fire began as two Forest Service prescribed burns, and the legislature then moved to shield utilities that adopt a mitigation plan.

“The government lit the largest fire and the legislature is protecting the utilities,” 

Guru Nanga said. “They call this balance. I call it item five. Nobody in New Mexico has to write down what the utility lit, either.”

The Labour Party have a convicted fraudster and a tax dodger sat on their front bench, their former corruption minister has been convicted in absentia of corruption, and then of course there’s Nick Brown. Plus OVER a dozen Labour Politicians including MPs and Mayors have been arrested for serious crimes, while investigations continue into a string of other party officials and campaigners. Sir Keir Starmer failed to comment on any of them – yet here, VoteWatch exclusively reveals a socialist rogue’s gallery, and what is becoming an ever-
CLAUDIA WEBBE MP
The 55-year-old MP for Leicester East, who lives in Islington, was charged with harassment after making numerous abusive unwanted telephone calls to another female, a court has heard, and pleaded not guilty to one charge of harassment during a 20-minute hearing at Westminster Magistrates’ Court.
In court, Webbe spoke only to confirm her name, her age, and her address and to formally enter her not guilty plea.
In a statement on 28th September, Webbe said: “I am innocent of any wrongdoing and look forward to proving this in court.”
“I will be vigorously defending myself against these claims.”
Webbe has, however, acknowledged that the calls were made and was released on unconditional bail; the trial rescheduled to 16th March 2021.
The Metropolitan Police supplied evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service detailing claims of harassment between 1st September 2018 and 26th April 2020.
APSANA BEGUM MP
Apsana Begum, MP for Poplar and Limehouse, was given a £330,000 desirable riverside property just months after moving out of her estranged husband’s home. Official complaints were made over how the far-left Corbynista leapt to the top of an 18,000-strong housing list, despite having no children.
Allegedly using her contacts at the council, Begum is thought to have applied for a council flat while living with her family in 2011. Begum moved in with her husband in 2014 but the couple split a year later.
Within just six months, Ms Begum was offered the one-bed Isle of Dogs flat in a riverside block – jumping her own constituents; families and vulnerable residents – some of whom have been waiting desperately on the list for years.
Tower Hamlets only has the capacity to house 1,700 people per year, on a list of over 18,000 applicants.
A source from a political organisation in Tower Hamlets said: “She’s still in the flat despite earning £82,000 plus expenses a year as MP, and yet has the audacity to complain about housing shortages.
“The council are taking their time to ensure all their ducks are in a row. It has the potential to be bigger than the Onasanya saga”.
Fiona Onasanya, a former Peterborough Labour MP, was ousted by her constituents via a recall petition after being caught and convicted for lying about a driving offence.
Section 1 of the Recall Act dictates that the Speaker of the House can trigger a recall petition if a sitting MP receives a custodial sentence of under a year. Anything over a year leads to automatic dismissal of the MP without the need for a petition.
A four-day trial is set to begin on the 27th July.
MAYOR IFTAKHAR HUSSAIN
The Mayor of Blackburn, Cllr Hussain, has resigned after being caught by police attending an address where a wedding celebration was taking place.
The Labour Mayor’s bizarre and unbelievable initial excuse was that he had attended the address after being asked to come over and ‘open the front door to allow the delivery driver to deliver them food’.
Police handed £200 fines to nine people, including Mr Hussain, amid claims a wedding was taking place, and the Mayor has since resigned over what he confessed to be a “the momentary lapse of judgement”.
A Lancashire Police spokesman confirmed there were reports of up to 30 people attending a ‘wedding’ in Dukes Brow and added: “There they found nine people inside celebrating the wedding, including two residents of the address. Each individual was issued with a £200 fixed penalty notice and was instructed to leave, which they did.”
Cllr Hussain’s resignation comes after town hall bosses in Blackburn launched an investigation into the incident.
“Today I am giving this up to protect the reputation of the borough” he said.
“I hope my actions will serve as a reminder to the people of Blackburn with Darwen of the importance of following the Covid-19 guidelines as it remains a real and serious threat.”
MAYOR SABRI OZAYDIN
The clearly not-so-bright Mayor of Enfield has been filmed wearing his gold-plated chain of office whilst riding through the streets of the London Borough which has been hit hard by Covid-19 – even stopping for coffee with his chums, including councillors Ahmet Hasan and Mustafa Cetinkaya.
“Is that the mayor?” one local female can be heard gasping in the footage, taken by an angered member of the public.
“He knows he’s done wrong, look – the MAYOR of Enfield” another onlooker spoke out, looking over disapprovingly as Ozaydin stands sheepishly outside a local Paddy Power, seemingly preparing to go into a coffee shop next door.
Mayor Ozaydin, Labour mayor of the city since July 2020, is then asked what he’s doing and why he is breaking lockdown. “We are just cycling” he replies nervously, dropping his shoulders upon being reminded of the law and realising that he’s been rumbled.
As it currently stands, the law in Britain strictly states that no one is to meet up with people outside their bubble until the 8th March. Yet the mayor – who is supposed to set an example for his constituents – openly and carelessly flouted the rules for all to see.
London has seen some of the highest rates of infection of the Coronavirus during the pandemic, with the borough of Enfield witnessing thousands of citizens testing positive.
Yet as some of his constituents are forced to endure the heartache of not being able to be with their loved ones on their death beds, and as funerals continue to take place in the city for those who have been tragically lost, their mayor chose to don his flashy chain like a poundshop version of Mr T and enjoy himself while wilfully breaking the law and sticking two fingers up in the process.
CLLR ASAF AFZAL
Cllr Afzal is one of four people charged by police for perverting the course of justice in regard to an investigation into the tampering of postal votes.
The Labour councillor and Chairman of the Pakistan Community Centre in Derby stood for re-election  in the May 2019 City Council elections, ultimately losing his seat to the Lib Dems.
In a statement, Derbyshire Police said: “Four people have been charged with perverting the course of justice following enquiries into an alleged incident of election fraud relating to the Derby City Council elections in May 2019.
“The four, three men and one woman, are due to appear before Southern Derbyshire Magistrates’ Court on March 22 charged with:
“Mohan Singh, 77 – two counts of perverting the course of justice;
“Baljit Rehalu, 41 – two counts of perverting the course of justice;
“Mohinder Rehala, 53, – one count of perverting the course of justice.
“Asaf Afzal, 53, of Colwyn Avenue, Derby – one count of perverting the course of justice.”
While serving on the council, Afzal was cabinet member for Neighbourhoods and Public Protection.
The former Labour Councillor refused to provide a full statement, saying only that: “I received some papers last week and the matters are in the hands of my solicitors.”
COUNCIL LEADER TONY NEWMAN & CLLR SIMON HALL
The cabinet member for finance and the former leader of Croydon Council have been suspended pending an investigation following complaints of bullying behaviour, ‘money mismanagement’, and what insiders suggest could mount to ‘illegal activity’.
Cllrs Tony Newman and Simon Hall were in charge of troubled Croydon council in the lead-up to its shocking financial collapse – even chucking £100m of the cash-strapped council’s dosh into a posh hotel.
Both stood down from their positions at the end of 2020 but remain as councillors, yet this week were suspended by the Labour Party in relation to an independent investigation by the Local Government Association in relation to financial mismanagement at the council.
Last week, four senior members of staff at the council were also suspended in relation to the same damning report into ‘dodgy dealings’.
The report has now been completed but is not expected to be made public until investigations into members of staff and councillors have concluded.
The report found that “council officials were instructed by members of Newman’s cabinet to rewrite some of their reports, in effect to disguise the council’s mounting financial problems”.
The council was forced to declare effective bankruptcy in November and is set to make significant cuts to services over the coming months and years as it faces a budget black hole of more than £60m.
The report’s author, Chris Wood, wrote, “It is clear that in recent history Croydon Council has failed to manage its finances adequately in many… areas. It is a council that is said to be unfamiliar with taking and implementing difficult financial decisions and as a consequence it has engendered a culture of poor budget management and poor financial control.”
Another source said: “It will be said that there has been significant incompetence, mismanagement, failures of diligence and poor governance. But as to unlawfulness, there is mere suspicion.
“The possibility that the suspicion is justified remains, as is often the case with suspicion, but unlawfulness has not yet been evidenced.”
RHIANON PASSMORE, WELSH LABOUR AM
Rising star Rhianon Passmore was caught taking part in a Welsh Parliament session from the £1m Swindon home of her lover, nearly 100 miles away from her constituency of Newport, South Wales.
It’s now understood that Passmore has been making regular lockdown visits from South Wales to Wiltshire – despite openly accusing the PM of breaking lockdown for travelling to a vaccination site while on official government business.
Ms Passmore, the Assembly Member for Islwyn, also posted and retweeted a series of “stay at home” messages through her social media accounts.
Her law-breaking was spotted when viewers of the Welsh Assembly noticed that the politician was ‘Zooming’ from a location different to that of her home in South Wales.
She also posted clips last month from the garden room of her lover’s plush home, with a local resident saying: “She was broadcasting from the property and thought nobody would notice.
“Everyone has been doing their best to help keep the virus at bay and what she is doing is certainly not in the spirit of the lockdown.”
Passmore has since tried to claim that her partner is ‘in her bubble’ – yet official guidelines state that bubbles must be kept as local as possible… not almost 100 miles away.
The recent incident isn’t the only time the Labour politician has found herself in hot water. In 2018 she was banned from driving by Newport magistrates and received a two-week ban from the Senedd after admitting to refusing to take a breath test when pulled over by police.
CLLR DIPU AHAD
Cllr Ahad admitted leaving a woman alarmed and distressed by engaging in a serious and prolonged stalking campaign against her.
Pleading guilty to the charge, Newcastle Crown Court heard that Ahad had committed a series of creepy acts between December 31st, 2018 and May 30th, 2019, which amounted to stalking.
The court heard the acts he confessed to include setting up fake email and social media accounts in the victim’s name, “sending an email to himself purporting to be a third party and revealing this to (her)”, phoning her home purporting to be from a Government agency, sending her a message claiming he had received malicious calls, sending her a voicemail purportedly left by a third party, using chalk paint to graffiti her car, sending her an email containing photographs, sending a message “which contained a screenshot of an email purportedly sent by a third party to Ahad”, and sending an email containing threats to himself.
After pleading guilty, Ahad was warned by a judge that “all options are open” when he is sentenced in April, meaning custody has not been ruled out.
CLLR MARTIN JUDD
Judd, 25, appeared at Manchester Minshull Street charged with downloading child pornography whilst a Labour Councillor in Oldham.
Judd faces allegations that between February 2018 and the same month last year he downloaded 15 category A (the most serious) images of children, 23 category B’s, and 48 category C’s.
The young politician pleaded not guilty to all three of the allegations.
Judd, originally from New Zealand, was elected in the local government elections in 2018 where there were two vacancies at the ward.
The former Labour politician received 1,184 votes in Hollinwood which represented 73 percent of the total.
He was elected to serve a four-year term but his departure was subtly announced on the Oldham Council website following him being charged. His profile currently states that he is not a serving councillor.
During his time on the local authority. Judd served as deputy cabinet member in economy and enterprise.
Due to delays caused by the pandemic, the trial is expected to run for three days in January next year, with Judge Maurice Greene telling him: “The trial will take place on the 17th of January, it is a long way off, ensure you keep in touch with your solicitor.”
CLLR CHAUDHARY MOHAMMED IQBAl
Iqbal, 51, told election officials that he lived in Ilford so that he could trick them into thinking he met the legal requirements to run for a seat in the constituency. In doing so, he committed electoral fraud.
Mr Chaudhary then broke the law yet again after his questionable election win in 2018, by continuing to hold that seat of office based on his lies, and to collect thousands of pounds in expenses payments.
When police began to investigate, Iqbal encouraged his tenant Kristina Stankeviciute to lie on his behalf and tell officers that he lived in a converted living room at the Ilford property.
Miss Stankeviciute has since left the country and a European warrant for her arrest was issued in December last year.
Iqbal had given multiple false addresses in his attempts to run for local office and successfully sat as a Labour councillor for more than two years, claiming more than £18,000 in expenses and allowances.
The former councillor pleaded guilty to three counts of making false statements in candidate nomination papers and one count of perverting the course of justice.
Iqbal, who has since moved to Preston, appeared at Southwark Crown Court earlier this month and was sentenced to a total of 17 months in prison.
He was also ordered to pay prosecution costs of £10,422.54, compensation to Redbridge Council of £10,000 for the by-election costs and compensation to Redbridge Council of £18,368 for the allowances paid to him, and will not be allowed to run for office for at least five years.
MAYOR JOE ANDERSON
Anderson, who has been the sitting mayor of Liverpool for a decade, was one of five men arrested across Merseyside in an investigation into ‘crooked’ building and development contracts in the city.
The mayor was interviewed by police on suspicion of conspiracy to commit bribery and witness intimidation.
A Liverpool city council spokeswoman said: “Liverpool city council is cooperating with Merseyside police in relation to its ongoing investigation. We do not comment on matters relating to individuals.”
The others arrested are: a 72-year-old man from Aigburth, on suspicion of witness intimidation; a 33-year-old man from West Derby, on suspicion of conspiracy to commit bribery and witness intimidation; a 46-year-old man from Ainsdale, on suspicion of conspiracy to commit bribery and witness intimidation; and a 25-year-old man from Ormskirk, on suspicion of witness intimidation.
DEREK HATTON
Far-left former Labour Militant irritant Derek Hatton, the former Deputy Council Leader of Liverpool, has been confirmed as having also been arrested in the anti-fraud police bust along with Labour Mayor, Joe Anderson.
Well-known controversial Marxist Hatton was expelled from the Labour Party in 1986 for belonging to the far-left ‘extremist group’ Militant, which had earlier been found to be in breach of the Labour Party’s constitution.
In 1993, he was accused of corruption as deputy leader of Liverpool City Council. After a lengthy trial he was found not guilty due to lack of evidence.
Hatton applied to rejoin Labour in September 2018, having his application approved in February the following year before being suspended from the party just days later after an anti-semitic tweet he had posted in 2012 came to light.
Adding to his long blunder-filled career, on Friday 4th December, Hatton – now a property developer – was arrested along with serving Labour mayor Joe Anderson in the police sting.
The two have now been rebailed while police investigate further.
LORD NAZIR AHMED
The trial of Labour Lord of Rotherham, Nazir Ahmed, continued this week – yet the jury were discharged ‘on legal grounds’.
Ahmed, 63, has denied two counts of attempting to rape a girl under 16, indecent assault of a boy under 14, and raping a boy under 16.
The alleged offences were said to date from the 1970s when Mr Ahmed was 14-years-old.
One alleged female victim, now an adult, told the court that she ‘has never forgotten’ the moment Labour peer Lord Ahmed ‘tried to rape her as a girl’ in the 1970s.
She reported Nazir Ahmed to police decades after the abuse was said to have taken place, stating that she wanted revenge, but also that she had a ‘moral responsibility’ due to Ahmed currently having access to young relatives.
She recalled to police how, in the early 1970s, Ahmed allegedly held her down and attempted to rape her – the horrific abuse occurring ‘more than once’.
‘I thought I had let him do that to me and I felt dirty’ she said.
‘I have never forgotten, I have tried. I have really tried to erase that memory and I cannot do it’ she added.
Jurors were told that they were being discharged for legal reasons, with Judge Jeremy Richardson QC saying that discussions with the prosecution and defence were ongoing – leading some to speculate that a plea deal may be on the cards.
Mr Ahmed’s brothers, Mohammed Farouq, 70, and Mohammed Tariq, 65, also from Rotherham, have also been accused of the indecent assault of a boy under 14, but claim they are unfit to enter pleas.
ANTISEMITISM
Five people may yet be prosecuted over antisemitism linked to the Labour Party, Britain’s most senior police officer has revealed.
Dame Cressida Dick, the commissioner of the Metropolitan Police, said the force had arrested six people last year as part of its inquiry and that five files have been passed on to prosecutors.
“It is for the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) to decide,” she told LBC radio.
“It is a very complex crime type, to be honest – there is a lot for them to look at and a lot for them to consider as to whether there is either sufficient evidence to charge and whether it is in the public interest so to do.”
The investigation was prompted by an internal Labour dossier detailing antisemitic messages on social media allegedly posted by members, which was obtained by the radio station last year.

text:
WHAT MAKES EXITING PROSTITUTION SO HARD?

By Huschke Mau.

Occasionally I’m asked what makes it so hard to exit prostitution. It took me years to leave, I kept returning – and this is true for many women. What makes it so hard is the complexity of the situation. When I went to a counselling service for prostitutes to ask for help to exit, I was told: “If you don’t want to do this any longer, just don’t go back to the brothel!” But it isn’t that simple.

1. A HISTORY OF BEING FAILED BY THE AUTHORITIES

Most prostitutes have had very bad experiences with many kinds of authorities or official institutions. In fact, these institutions may actually be the reason the women are in prostitution in the first place.

Those like me who have learned how easy it is to slip through the gaps in Germany’s safety net, know where not to go when they’re in need of help. In my case, youth services alleged I’d run away from home, not because of the violence, but because I hadn’t got enough pocket money. I only received any help at all because of the efforts of committed social workers at a girls’ refuge. But that help ended far too early. Come 18 years of age it was over.

Nobody seemed to care about the dangers of my situation as a traumatised young women who had no contact with her parents, no support, and was penniless.

There was a girl at the girls’ centre who was there because her father had repeatedly raped her. Youth services got them to sit down together to “talk it out.” Her father admitted everything and apologised. Youth Services then told her: “There you are, he apologised, he won’t do it again. You can go back home now.”

I am fairly sure that she will never again turn to an official institution when she needs help.

At all the various offices – social security, student loans, job centre/unemployment, housing – it’s the same story. “Not within the scope of our responsibilities,” endless protraction in dealing with applications, stupid remarks.

Housing office: “We’ve been processing your application for almost a year now, we’ll let you know. What’s this? You can’t pay your rent anymore? Well, if you don’t have an apartment, you’re not entitled to rent support, so we’ll stop processing your application.”

Student office: “If your parents don’t want to sign the application form, you must have done something wrong. It’s usually the children’s fault. Have you ever thought of apologising to the authorities?”

(In Germany, economically deprived students are entitled to a state-sponsored student loan to cover their living costs. Parents must sign the application form and can be compelled to do so. However, the bureaucracy often puts up barriers and delays, so students don’t get the loans they are entitled to and therefore fall into destitution.)

2. INADEQUATE OR NON-EXISTENT SOCIAL SECURITY

I know prostitutes who want to exit, but the unemployment office refuses to grant financial support and threatens them with a three-month ban on any payment if they terminate their ‘contract’ with the brothel.

Others try to exit but aren’t provided with the full payments they’re due because the office assumes they are still engaged in prostitution and come up with a completely imaginary sum they’re supposed to be earning. This is added into the calculations and reduces the payments so they’re not enough to live on.

Those who end up in prostitution or remain there because of such things are not there because of free choice but because the only options are unwanted alternatives: prostitution or starve and/or become homeless.

3. USELESS (OR NEARLY-USELESS) ADVOCACY SERVICES

Advocacy and counselling centres that claim to offer exit support in Germany are not usually on the side of the prostituted woman.

Mimikry, an advocacy centre in Munich, demonstrated their support for sex trade operators by inviting Stephanie Klee, the owner of an escort agency, to their anniversary celebrations.

The head of the public health office in Dresden (which runs the advocacy centre there) appears as a speaker at pro-prostitution events and glorifies prostitution as a great opportunity for punters, with or without disabilities.

Kassandra in Nuremberg maintains that violence in prostitution is rare and prostitutes must never be considered an ‘at risk group’ because it would stigmatise them – even though more than 90 prostitutes have been murdered in Germany alone since the Prostitution Act in 2002.

Most advocacy centres (like Hydra in Berlin) speak in terms of ‘sex work,’ do more to help women enter prostitution than to leave it, and claim that the greatest problem prostitutes face is ‘stigma.’ I know women who turned to such counselling centres and were told that the problem wasn’t the job – it was them, and why didn’t they just re-orientate themselves within prostitution? Could escorting be an alternative or BDSM?

Turn to such centres and you’re not only denied help, you’re shamed.

4. LACK OF ALTERNATIVES

Another problem is the lack of alternatives. The job situation in Germany is not all that rosy. Things are difficult if you’ve got a criminal record for offences in the context of prostitution (disregarding zoning regulations, carrying drugs, etc.) or gaps in your CV that cannot be camouflaged no matter how creative you are.

Women who spend years in prostitution have little, if anything, to show in terms of job experience, and typically have never had any professional training. The jobs that she can apply for are therefore those with maximum hours and minimum pay. Someone who has barely left prostitution usually has to contend with the disorders following trauma – i.e. permanent stress. And that means they may not be able to endure these jobs for long.

If money is short again and again and again, you do what you know how to do and can do, and go back to ‘working.’

Not a single prostitute that I know has the self-confidence left to apply for well-paid jobs with good conditions.

5. THE CONSEQUENCES OF PROFOUND AND ENDURING TRAUMA

And then there’s the trauma. Most prostitutes suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) similar to victims of torture. They suffer from anxiety disorders, lack of self-confidence, obsessive behaviour – such as compulsive washing or repetition of pointless rituals that supposedly ensure safety. (I have to knock on wood when I have fearful thoughts. And I often have those. When I can’t do that, a panic attack ensues. I know how crazy this sounds and that ultimately it’s pointless, but I can’t help it.)

When I switched from the brothel to escorting, I wasn’t used to going out during the day. I couldn’t abide daylight. Nor the crowds of people. Someone whose boundaries are being violated daily and hourly may not be able to stay among others, because their inner alarm system keeps going off: “This is a man! Danger!”

I don’t want to begin talking about what it’s like to be triggered and having flashbacks when you’re out and about. Nightmares and sleep disorders are exhausting. It is almost impossible to keep up appearances and move into a ‘normal life.’ You feel different from everyone else, inferior, more hurt. Broken.

People seem creepy, the ‘normal ones’ more than anybody else, because they make you see what you yourself aren’t any longer: without cares, without injuries, without fears. Whole. Nice. In a good mood.

In order to endure prostitution, you have to split your awareness away from your body, to dissociate. The problem is that you cannot just slip back into it later. The body remains without contact to your soul, your psyche. You just do not feel yourself any more.

It took me several years to learn that what I sometimes feel is hunger. And that this means I should eat something. Or that what I’m experiencing means that I’m cold. And I need to put on something warm.

It is exhausting to learn or to relearn that one’s body has needs, to feel it, and it is even more exhausting to practice ‘self-care’ and not to treat yourself like shit any longer. To sleep, when you are tired – because you’re not sitting in a 24-hour brothel and have to take the next punter. That you don’t have to feel cold any longer because you’re in street prostitution when it’s below freezing. That you can change situations that cause pain instead of eliminating the pain through dissociation, drugs or alcohol.

But trauma doesn’t let go of you easily: You get used to it. This phenomenon is called trauma bonding, and it is the reason why women who are battered by their husbands keep going back. Traumatic situations can be addictive because they cause a massive release of adrenaline – and that is addictive.

Additionally, a violent situation is something well-known to people who have experienced as much violence as is common in prostitution. I learned from early childhood on: The place where I am afraid, where I am hurt, where I am degraded, is the place where I belong. That is home. This is why even today I still struggle in situations that endanger me, to see the danger for what it is and walk away. The situations are shite, but familiar; I know them.

Situations in which people are nice to me, do not shout, do not batter, and do not abuse me, feel creepy. I promptly feel inferior. My soul signals: “Something is wrong here. This is alien.” Prostitution is like self-harm. No. Prostitution IS self-harm.

6. ADDICTIONS

Addictions are another barrier to exiting. Many prostitutes numb themselves, with drugs, alcohol, cigarettes, because that is the only way they can function. This develops its own dynamics and you promptly have an additional problem to deal with.

7. VICTIM-BLAMING ATTITUDES

It is difficult to find therapy for former prostitutes. It takes a lot of time and nerves to secure a place in therapy, and when you do, you find many therapists, both male and female, will not accept that prostitution is violence. (I will write a separate article about therapy one day.)

Like therapists, our entire culture has a problem recognising prostitution as something damaging, not only to society, but to the individual prostitute.

Exiting prostitution is incredibly challenging when the dominant view out there is that prostitution is something entirely normal, something that can be advertised on huge billboards along the main streets, whose advertising can be plastered all over taxis, when articles repeatedly make you read terms like ‘sex worker,’ ‘people who offer sexual services,’ when you keep being confronted with images and films and articles that minimise or even hype prostitution. All of that does something to you.

Not even to mention people who feel the need to designate former prostitutes who dare speak up in public as ‘filthy whores,’ ‘gold diggers,’ ‘low life,’ etc. right under the articles these women have written or right below the interviews in which they have spoken.

Exiting prostitution and then being told it was your ‘own fault,’ that you ‘made poor choices’ or that you are lying, can make you feel you should have just stayed there.

Disordered self-perception and extremely low self-esteem isolate most prostitutes from the world outside the sex trade. After years spent in that environment, most women don’t know anyone from outside that life.

8. PUNTER IMPUNITY

The sex trade is like a parallel world. And sometimes it feels like ‘the true world’ because you don’t feel any trust in your fellow human beings, and above all none in men. You now know, and have experienced, what they are capable of. You know this in your own body and you see right through the bourgeois façade out there.

For punters don’t only parade around in the ‘underworld.’ They are out there, in the ‘normal world’ – only what happens in that ‘normal world’ is that you are shamed as the (former) prostitute while they are never shamed and never held accountable.

9. THE PIMPS – IN ALL THEIR GUISES

So you may just as well remain in prostitution. By comparison it appears sort of honest at least, violence in return for money, everybody knows what you’re doing, does the same, the rules are known, as are the mechanisms.

In Germany women are not put under any pressure to leave the brothel. Quite the reverse in fact. The usual custom is having to buy yourself out. A German colleague who wanted to disappear from a brothel had the brothel keeper who had repeatedly raped her stuck to her heels for an entire year. He slashed her tires, appeared inside her apartment, threatened her boyfriend, and enlightened her parents about how she had made her money. He only left her in peace after he had gotten the pay-off of € 3,000. (This sum is often euphemised as ‘debts incurred by the prostitute.’ But what it really means is: Punishment for being late, for not tidying the room, for turning down punters, ‘non-attendance’ fees; rent for the room that she had to pay for even though she hadn’t had any punters or was sick, etc.)

I’m not going to begin now on the prostituted women’s ‘partners’ who also profit from their ‘working.’

And in all of this I still haven’t taken the foreign prostitutes into consideration, who do not speak German, who only know a corrupted police force in their home countries (and here in my own country I do not entirely acquit the police force from this…), who are not even theoretically entitled to social security payments, who have no health insurance, and who are often transferred to a different city or brothel every week and so don’t even know where they are. And even if they did know: Who are they supposed to turn to?

The German state does not provide any help. It leaves the financing of the (new) ‘Prostitutes’ Protection Law’ entirely to the municipalities, thus ensuring they have to continue enabling the punters’ to smoothly engage in their little hobby – so the German state can continue to take taxes from it and gorge on the revenue.

And this does in fact give rise to the question of whether the state has any interest at all in preventing women and young girls from ending up in prostitution or in helping prostitutes exit.
