BEGS AMERICA SAVE 6,000,000 IN RUSSIA
Massacre Threatens All Jews as Soviet Power Wanes, Declares Kreinin, Coming Here for Aid.

Copyright, 1921, by The Chicago Tribune Co.
BERLIN, July 19.—Russia’s 6,000,000 Jews are facing extermination by massacre. As the famine is spreading, the counter-revolutionary movement is gaining and the Soviet’s control is waning. This statement is borne out by official documents presented to the Berlin Government, which show that numerous pogroms are raging in all parts of Russia and the Ukraine.
The information was gathered by Dr. Joseph Kreinin, a noted Jewish social worker and President of the Russian Joint Board of Jewish Societies. He says that several villages have been burned already and scores killed, seventy in one village alone. He is en route to America, where he plans meetings in New York, Chicago and elsewhere for the purpose of “saving his people.”
According to Dr. Kreinin, mass flights from Russia have already begun, the Jews rushing to all borders and especially to Rumania, where there are 40,000 families camping along the frontier, hoping to find refuge. Among these, he says, at least 100 persons daily are dying from exposure and hunger.
Dr. Kreinin, who recently escaped from Moscow, says the pogroms are especially severe in the provinces of Homel, Minsk and Volhynia. The pogroms originated outside of Russia, in the Ukraine and White Russia.
He says in the Volga region a new sort of pogrom occurred, when Russian peasants attacked German settlements because they were foreigners. He declares the recent transfer of General Budenny into White Russia was for the purpose of pacifying the region.
“My object in visiting Germany and the United States is to organize all relief organizations throughout the world, Jewish as well as others,” he added. “The only hope for the millions of Jews is for American aid, both material and political.
“I cannot expect much effect from any political steps, as the Soviets are losing control everywhere except in the cities. The massacres are occurring chiefly in the small towns.
“However, I hope the American Government will realize the danger of massacres is greater than at any time in history, and I hope they will help open the borders and lift restrictions on entering the United States.”

The race for Colorado State Treasurer centers on how the state manages and invests its $17 billion in tax revenues. While traditionally a lower-profile administrative role, candidates Kevin Grantham (R) and Jeff Bridges (D) offer contrasting philosophies for the office:  

Kevin Grantham (R): Advocates keeping the treasurer's office focused on core duties—maximizing traditional safe-haven investments, improving efficiency for returning unclaimed property, and using the office's platform to advocate against excess state spending. 

Jeff Bridges (D): Proposes expanding the office's scope by directing a portion of state funds into local affordable housing and infrastructure projects, alongside creating a forensic auditing division to oversee spending across state agencies, and introduces mechanisms for corruption and cronyism.

text:
Last week I attended GFF one of the world's largest fintech gatherings, with 50,000+ attendees including the PM of India, the Finance Minister, Maharashtra's CM, and CXOs from every major Indian bank.

Here are my 14 observations:

1. Crypto and blockchain presence was minimal; the word "cryptocurrency" itself is avoided almost entirely

2. Everything gets called tokenization instead; tokenization was one of the key themes of the event

3. Tokenization here mostly means private bonds and private credit instruments, run in closed systems, not interoperable with the public blockchain world

4. Talked with several bond issuers and credit issuers, all building in these closed, permissioned setups

5. In the panels, policymakers and government chiefs actively avoided the term cryptocurrency; even major panel discussions centered on AI & fintech

6. Whenever tokenization came up on panels, it was framed as piloting DLTs and closed ledger systems, not public chains

7. There is a real lack of awareness across the system about what public blockchains like Ethereum actually offer

8. Almost nothing on privacy, security, or zero knowledge proofs and what they bring to financial infrastructure

9. There's no awareness between scammy crypto tokens and neutral infrastructure like Ethereum that provides rails for innovation and delivers net good to society

10. Stablecoins and tokenized assets represent $330B+ globally, but there's very little interest in that data point since Indian Institutions are not yet open for interoperable infra & public chains

11. Direct, dedicated engagement with policymakers and lawmakers is needed to show why public blockchains and privacy tech don't endanger citizens, and instead open up new opportunity and improve financial infrastructure

12. Conversations with SEBI, RBI innovation team, NPCI, and others confirmed no active public blockchain development yet, just early tinkering

13. Despite the bureaucracy, some internal teams within these orgs are surprisingly open and receptive to Ethereum's CROPS value proposition

14. AI agents were a dominant build theme across projects and booths (inspite of a fin-tech conf)

These are my ground-level observations from GFF. 

Over the past few months, while working at @EFDevcon, I got to connect with quite a few people working closely with Indian government bodies and institutions on tokenization, Ethereum, and public + private blockchains. 

Currently working on a report with @RohitMalekar, @rashmivabbigeri, and @denverjude. Hoping to publish soon and give you all a sneak peek on the state of institutional crypto in India.

text:
As a graduate student and a post doc I can relate to this experience.
We are so pushed to generate data towards something we can publish and get grants. And if the idea could land in a high impact gator journal you become the darling of the lab and the professor will do anything to make your future career the best it can be.
So most people fall into that .., sometimes we are pushed to generate things even when we see negative data because the professor likes the theory, wha scientists can do working in the wee night hours with no sleep due to stress and obligations and fear is a bit crazy but also not something we have not heard of,

I got lucky. I found a field that was open and the money needed to generate the data was minimal. I also had a habit of repeating the experiment 5 times. 3 by me and 2 by another lab tech or grad student or post doc. I offer them authorship in return. This reduces artifacts and that fear that I could be making something up. Apart from that I used 3-4 separate techniques to show the same result. For example if it’s cell division I am looking at I used immuno staining, flow cytometry, histology, brdu staining and several others to get the same result. This repetition helps to remove artifacts that might be deliberately or most of the time without knowing could produce.l

Because at the time end of the day … I could publish “something” … but years down if i am disproven my whole career is under water. I will be done. That’s what I always wanted to avoid. 

But not many get lucky and many don’t put a lot of thoughts into being careful and thorough due to pressure. I doubt the professor knew. But at the end … the professor will get the most of the criticism and career issues due to something like this.

What i wrote above is my own experiences and feelings. I have been in meetings where I have called out seemingly artificers like this. It’s laziness . My old post doc advisor hated me for it because it was always a guy in that lab that did it and i became that feminist who hated men. He ended messing my career so bad. So we can’t always do the right thing either,

text:
Immediate help  
0800 212121 Mental Health Uganda helpline (toll-free from any Ugandan phone). Counselling, first aid and referrals.  
999 or 112  Police / emergency if there is immediate physical danger.

Main public hospital  
Butabika National Referral Mental Hospital  
Plot 2, Kirombe-Butabika Road, Kampala (about 12 km east of the city centre).
24/7 emergency intake.  
Phone: +256 414 504 375  
Hospital site also lists 0800 211 306.  
Mulago National Referral Hospital’s psychiatric department also accepts emergencies.

Community and NGO options in Kampala  
StrongMinds Uganda  Free or low-cost group therapy for depression in communities, schools and health facilities (including Katwe). Works with government partners. https://t.co/zYHOGYLZEI  
GambaCare WhatsApp service matching people with verified Ugandan therapists (English, Luganda, Swahili). Free daily vent sessions plus paid therapy (typically ~UGX 50,000, Mobile Money). https://t.co/AewgJLTLu9  
Heart to Heart Spaces  Workshops, referrals and community support. +256 700 410 356, https://t.co/yS9aRCfNEu  
Safe Places Uganda Private outpatient clinic in Kyambogo (Plot 12, Lancaster Avenue) for mental health, neurology and addiction; residential site further out. +256 770 700944, https://t.co/wEWXqNCXuM  
You Belong Uganda and similar lived-experience programmes that support people with psychosis in the community and ease pressure on Butabika.

Other useful services  
Makerere University Hospital runs an Early Intervention Psychiatry clinic (assessment, therapy and follow-up, including for students).  
Private psychologists and lower-level health centres in Kampala also offer counselling; private session fees often start around UGX 60,000–120,000.

Public care at Butabika and government facilities is free or heavily subsidised, though the hospital is often overcrowded. Community programmes such as StrongMinds aim to bring support closer to where people live.

text:
A RATE HIKE WOULD PAY CIRCLE $CRCL MORE. IT IS DOWN 4.5% INTO ONE:

Thirty minutes to the bell, and all four index contracts are higher: S&P 500 futures 7,692.00, +67.00 pts / +0.88%; Nasdaq-100 futures 29,454.25, +302 pts / +1.04%; Dow futures 52,810.00, +370 pts / +0.71%; Russell 2000 futures 2,914.70, +20.60 pts / +0.71%. These are bets on where an index finishes later, and while American shares are shut they are the only live opinion there is.

They have been grinding up all morning. At 8:00am ET the S&P contract was 7,678.25, the Nasdaq contract 29,406.75 and the Dow contract 52,704.00 - so the last hour added 13.75, 47.50 and 106 points to the three of them. Nothing dramatic. Just steady.

Circle Internet Group at $93.09 (premarket), -$4.33 / -4.45% from Monday's $97.42 close. The New York company, founded 2013 and run by 900 people, issues USDC - a digital dollar, a token designed to be worth exactly one US dollar and backed by a pile of actual dollars and short-term US government debt.

The verdict: the crowd bidding this open is selling the one corner of the market that tomorrow would actually help, and Circle is the clearest case of it on the board.

Circle does not make its money from crypto prices. It makes it from interest. On August 5, for the three months to June 30, it reported total revenue and reserve income of $701M, +7% on the year. Reserve income - the interest Circle keeps on the dollars and short-term government debt sitting behind every USDC in issue, money customers handed over rather than Circle's own - was $668M of that. Ninety-five cents of every revenue dollar.

Now the one number that decides this name. USDC in circulation reached $73.3B at the end of June, +19% on the year, and the average balance across the quarter grew 25%. Reserve income grew 5%. A quarter more dollars earned a twentieth more money, because the rate those dollars earn fell by 0.66 of a percentage point. The balances did their job. The rate undid it.

Which is what makes tomorrow strange. The Federal Reserve announces at 2:00pm ET on Wednesday, September 16, and money markets put a quarter-point rise at roughly 85% to 91% - the first increase since 2023, off a 3.50%-3.75% range that has not moved all year. A higher rate is the most direct upgrade to Circle's revenue line that exists. It is being sold into it.

Two things explain that, and only one of them is about today.

At 2:15pm ET this afternoon the Senate holds a cloture vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act - a procedural test needing 60 votes simply to open debate, not passage of the bill. Republicans hold 53 seats, so at least seven Democrats or independents have to come across, and the White House agreed to new ethics language over the weekend to get it there. A lost vote bans nothing. It removes the rulebook this industry has been promised for two years.

The second is older and heavier. On June 30 a consortium of more than 140 businesses - payment networks, banks, asset managers, large technology firms - signed on to Open USD, a rival digital dollar run by a separate company, Open Standard. Its design points straight at that 95%: businesses mint and redeem free, with no volume caps, and the partners keep the interest earned on the reserves, minus a management fee, instead of the issuer keeping it. Circle fell nearly 16% the day it was announced.

Circle is not a current pick on any of the six Len5es, and that same 7% is the reason. Both value Len5es - one hunting a business almost nobody could rebuild bought under its worth, the other settled earning power bought cheaply - are offered 54.5 times profit and 6.5 times book value, what owners would keep if everything were sold and every debt paid. Neither is a discount. Hypergrowth wants a business early as well as fast, and 7% growth is not fast at any age; Income wants cash reaching owners, and there is no dividend at all. CHANGE IT: reserve income growing in line with those balances again rather than at a fifth of their pace - which is exactly what tomorrow afternoon would begin to do.

Strategy at $132.24 (premarket), -$4.70 / -3.43% from Monday's $136.94 close, is the cleaner contrast. The Virginia company holds bitcoin and issues securities against it, so it falls when bitcoin falls - and bitcoin is at $76,973, -$694 / -0.89% today. Circle has no such excuse, because the price of bitcoin appears nowhere in its revenue. It is a current pick on none of the six Len5es either, on the simplest fact available: it does not earn a profit, so no value style has earnings to discount.

Both rallied hard on Monday - Circle +$6.82 / +7.53%, Strategy +$5.97 / +4.56% - and both are handing most of it back before anyone has rung a bell.

One number has already landed. At 8:30am ET the Federal Reserve Bank of New York published its September factory survey: a headline reading of 7.6, thirteen points below August's 20.6. That figure is a net score - the share of New York state manufacturers saying business improved minus the share saying it worsened - so above zero still means more said better than worse. New orders 2.0, barely growing. Shipments -3.2, actually shrinking. Prices paid 63.1, still hot. Activity cooled and costs did not, and that combination is what keeps tomorrow's increase on the table.

The standing caveat: a premarket lean is a thin crowd trading, and it fades by 9:30am at least as often as it holds. Friday makes it harder still - index futures and options and single-stock options all expire, with the S&P 500 quarterly rebalance effective at the close, so much of that volume will be positions being closed rather than opinions formed.

Circle spent the summer being repriced on a rival that has not launched yet and on a rate that kept falling. It gets a vote at 2:15 this afternoon and a rate decision at 2:00 tomorrow. Only one of those changes what the company actually earns, and this morning it is the one nobody seems to be trading.

Not investment advice.

text:
I ASKED GROK:
Does Donald Trump own his own bank?

THE ANSWER:
No, Donald Trump does not own a conventional commercial or retail bank (the kind that takes deposits, makes loans, issues credit cards, or carries FDIC insurance). https://t.co/hHPZoCAlH4 
He and his family do, however, have a significant ownership stake in a recently approved specialized crypto entity that received a national trust-bank charter.
In August 2026, World Liberty Financial—a crypto firm co-founded by Trump and his sons—received conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to operate World Liberty Trust Company (also referred to as World Liberty Financial Trust Company). An entity affiliated with Trump and family members owns about 38% of the relevant holding company. Trump himself owns 70% of an LLC that holds that stake. A UAE-linked investor holds a larger reported share (around 49%). The Trump-family entity pledged to remain a passive investor. https://t.co/hHPZoCAlH4 
This is not a traditional bank. It will not lend money, issue mortgages or cards, or offer federally insured deposits. Its main purpose is to issue and custody the family’s USD1 stablecoin under federal oversight. https://t.co/XV7TxbM9Hh 
Critics, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren, have described the arrangement as Trump effectively owning and overseeing “his own bank,” citing the fact that regulators he appointed granted the charter. The White House and the company have rejected conflict-of-interest claims, noting the passive-investor commitment and that Trump’s investments are managed in discretionary accounts. https://t.co/XV7TxbM9Hh 
Historically, Trump has been a large customer and borrower of banks (Deutsche Bank, Signature Bank, JPMorgan, and others), not an owner of one. Several institutions later closed his accounts. https://t.co/aPcX6drDkH 
In short: he does not own a full-service bank, but he holds a substantial interest in a limited-purpose crypto trust bank that received a federal charter in 2026.

text:
switzerland - 2011: 

I urge you to experience once in your life to remove all external influences. i was able to do it one time from my life and i still think about it 15 years later  

hear me out 

note: sorry to tell you its not possible outside the ages of like 20-30 roughly 

2009-2011 - i was living in nyc , spent most of my time with people i went to ohio state with , a lot of partying, day drinking on weekend brunches, meet up and watch sports, happy hours, it was a safety net for something, maybe to stay distracted, stay busy, who knows 

in 2011 (24 yrs old) i got a job offer in lucerne switzerland and not out of choice i was completely isolated by myself. I had no family, no friends, no colleagues i knew 

you learn a lot about yourself when you are forced to operate entirely under your own direction, and no one else can shape your decisions and judgement - i wonder now if this is selfishness or what you would call it, I'm not sure 

no friends, no kids, no family, no friends, no colleagues that you know well , no roommates - nothing 

what happens next is up to you 

but for the first 6 months i was there, i acted entirely where every decision was truly my own - you just gravitate to what you truly want, deep down , and you make it happen - you are forced into some funny high agency environment with nobody to blame except yourself for no output or upgrade in your happiness 

maybe cause there are no excuses - or I was thinking there is probably some extreme guilt if you are not acting in the way you want there is nobody to blame but yourself... and maybe thats WHY people like external influences, because they're crutches or excuses 

maybe someday i will talk about the personal experiences i went through there, but for now the framework is the point

text:
On June 12 I charted the onchain inference market. Four players, one axis: who actually makes money if people start buying AI with crypto at any real scale.
Three months later I opened the same dashboards, the same contracts, the same endpoints   and read six weeks of the projects' own feeds.
Parts of that map have to come off. Including one line I wrote myself.
I like digging through projects and working things out on my own. Same approach as June  look at what's visible onchain and in public data, keep asking the same question.
base:0xc52aedec3374422d7510e294cfaa90799595cba3: my June question got answered out loud
Good news first.
In June I wrote that I couldn't find a legal entity behind the token  which is why converting the token into equity, an idea the founder himself floated publicly, looked impossible. Nothing to convert into.
The site footer now says Surplus Intelligence Corporation. Wyoming address, phone number, the whole setup. When exactly it appeared there I don't know. But three months ago it wasn't.
The product grew an order of magnitude in the meantime. 34.6 million requests in 28 days. Average real discount against provider pricing: 88%.
And now I have to take back something I wrote myself.
I said payments here run on crypto rails. On September 11 the founder put it in the past tense: they were doing onchain payment for every message to a model, and the economics didn't work   on cheap models the gas sometimes cost more than the response itself.
Were doing. Not doing.
The product I wrote up as an onchain marketplace has moved off onchain settlement per message.
There's no fee either, by the way. I found a line in one service endpoint about three tenths of a cent per request   but in August the project was advertising zero platform fees, and on September 13 the founder was talking about revenue in the future tense. I'm not going to try to square that.
And here's where it gets interesting.
In that same thread he did the math out loud on what a fee would actually bring in. A seller offers a model at an 80% discount. Take 5% on top. What you get is a percentage of a percentage of the price of one response. Minus gas.
Three months ago I ended that post saying the wires are lying right next to each other and nobody's plugged them in.
Wrong way to put it.
Nobody forgot. The founder worked out that the wire is thin, and said so publicly.
He's got an opinion on the right answer now, too. Same thread  a simple buyback is almost impossible to beat as a way of getting value to the holder.
The opinion exists. The mechanism doesn't.
And they're heading somewhere else entirely. On September 10 he laid out the roadmap: limit buy orders, trading algorithms for sellers, contracts for difference on the price of inference, an inference price index.
That's an exchange. A commodities exchange for compute.
The token isn't on the list.
There's one more line of his, from September 9: it's amazing how much Surplus has grown given they haven't shipped a landing page, haven't fixed the routing bugs, and haven't put anything into growth.
The team is busy with the product. The token isn't the product.
The token came back to life anyway. Holders went from about a thousand to over five thousand. Price is up 144% off the June bottom. Market cap is roughly where it was: $4.7M.
And a detail I wasn't expecting. Almost 80% of daily volume doesn't happen on Base  it happens on one second-tier centralized exchange.
The product lives onchain. The token's price gets set in an order book that has nothing to do with it.
More people holding the same unsolved problem.

AntSeed: rewrote its tokenomics and still didn't open trading
In June this was the youngest thing on the map: $65K gross volume ever, $2.5K in fees, ninth weekly epoch.
Now it's $290K and $11.5K. Two hundred and four sellers instead of a hundred and forty, almost a thousand paying buyers instead of 578.
But the numbers aren't the story here.
On September 10 at 09:54 UTC, AntSeed switched its reward protocol over. Epoch 22, the one running right now, is the first epoch of the new system.
Rewards now only accrue on paid delivery of a service, and only if the seller has ANTS staked in their own pool. The docs say it flatly: paid usage does not automatically earn ANTS.
Stake gets locked. You can exit early, but then between 5% and 50% of the position gets cut, and what's cut goes to the dead address  not to the team. Undistributed rewards burn too.
Then there's the anti wash rule. In June I wrote about the manual farmer purge in epoch 9. That's now written into the code with cryptographic proofs: once a seller's proven wash volume reaches a quarter of their historical volume, points zero out for both sides.
A broom became a standing law.
In three months AntSeed built its token staking, slashing and burning. The full set.
On August 31 ANTS got a CoinMarketCap page.
There's no price on it.
Transfers are still gated  the docs spell that out as its own condition.
Five months past genesis, twenty-two epochs, revenue up four and a half times, the token now has burning and slashing and staking   and you still can't buy or sell it.
That mirror I described in June is as sharp as it gets. Surplus has a token with no role at all and an exchange on the roadmap. AntSeed has a token with every role and no market.
Venice: finished the mechanism  and got it copied
This is where the most changed.
In July Venice raised $65M at roughly a billion-dollar valuation. Annual revenue run-rate crossed a hundred million.
They tightened the mechanism in three places.
Every $100 of API credits bought sends $5 to buy and burn base:0xacfe6019ed1a7dc6f7b508c02d1b04ec88cc21bf  on the open market. Its own line, stacked on the older buybacks from subscriptions.
Annual emissions are being cut from 3M to 2M, in two steps of 500K  first landed September 1, second comes October 1. Their own phrasing is a march toward a deflationary VVV with native yield.
And the $DIEM supply target went up for the first time since launch: 38,000 to 40,000, in four steps. The last one was yesterday. One staked DIEM gives a dollar of Venice credits a day, and DIEM only mints out of locked VVV.
Onchain today: DIEM at 37,585 against a 40,000 target.
I'm not going to quote a percentage of supply burned. The burns page only renders its figures through a script, and pulling a number secondhand into a post built on checkable data is a bad trade.
The mechanism matters more than the percentage here. This is the only project on the map where money from the product physically moves into the token.
And the best proof it works is that somebody copied it.
On August 19 Capminal went live on Surplus. CAPU is a DIEM clone  same staked token, same daily inference credits, same unused credits you can sell on as API capacity. By Surplus's own account CAPU earns roughly 3.26x more daily inference per token than DIEM, though its model selection is narrower.
I haven't verified that multiple. It's their claim, not my measurement.
The part that matters: the tokenized compute scheme Venice invented got copied, and the copy landed on Surplus.
Venice still has its own awkward bit. About 8% of users pay in crypto. The platform is growing a lot wider than the token. And that $65M didn't arrive as tokens  it arrived as equity, and the tokenholder watched that round from the shore.
Even where the wire is connected, it's connected to a smaller outlet than the house.
OpenRouter and x402: the threat is real, the size turned out to be arguable
In June I called this the existential threat to the whole map, and I leaned on that billion a year figure to do it.
OpenRouter itself only got stronger over the summer  $113M round in the spring, eight million users, a separate 8% tier launched in September. The business is fine.
The x402 numbers are where it got awkward, and I'll say it plainly because I was the one quoting them. The protocol's public counter has shown the same values since March, and an independent recount done with Visa cut the volume by almost nine times after filtering. On September 3, Solana passed Base in these transactions for the first time.
The threat is real. The size of it I took on faith.

So what
Everything grew over three months. Surplus grew in requests and is building an exchange. AntSeed grew in revenue and built its token a full mechanism. Venice grew in money and finished its buyback. Crypto paid inference stopped being a theory   it's just small.
And in every case the value from that growth went somewhere other than where the holder is sitting. Surplus   past the token, and the founder did the math out loud on why. AntSeed   into a token you can't sell. Venice   partly into burns, partly into a round paid in equity.

One question. Four ways of not answering it.
But one answer did get said out loud.
On September 13 the founder of Surplus wrote that a simple buyback is almost impossible to beat as a way of getting value to the holder.
The only project on my map doing exactly that is Venice. The only one past a billion.
The answer was on the same map I drew in June. Just not where I was looking for it.
I'll keep watching. Epoch by epoch, like I said I would.

text:
THE PROPERTY IS ALREADY BEHAVING LIKE A FRANCHISE: WHY MINDFULNESS PROTOCOLS SHOULD BE THE NEXT SERIOUS SCI-FI PACKAGE HOLLYWOOD PASSES UP AT ITS OWN RISK

An executive-to-executive coverage note for producers, runners, financiers and development teamsThere is a sentence buried inside Mindfulness Protocols that should open the meeting: “The system’s deepest fear is not violence. It is sequence.”  That is not merely a good dystopian line. It is the organizing principle of a screen property that has become considerably larger than the novel containing it. Baron Charles DuPont has built something Hollywood spends an extraordinary amount of money trying to manufacture after acquisition: a world with its own vocabulary, visual grammar, institutional mythology, theoretical architecture, prehistory, sequel logic and—most unusually—an already functioning alternate-reality layer. The pitch is not “here is a book that could become a series.” The pitch is: here is a franchise architecture that happens to have a book at its center. The immediate comps are obvious: Black Mirror for technological dread, Severance for immaculate institutional control, The Handmaid’s Tale for ritualized governance, Westworld for recursive machine consciousness and systems mythology, Lost for audience archaeology, Brazil for bureaucratic nightmare, The Truman Show for reality administered as benevolence, and Children of Men for the cinematic seriousness of a civilization that has quietly lost something essential. Those comparisons locate the shelf. They do not describe the property. Mindfulness Protocols has a mechanism of its own: humanity solves scarcity, waiting, friction and increasingly the need for human usefulness—and then discovers that the removal of suffering has also removed consequence. The state does not answer the resulting psychic crisis with jackboots. It answers with care. Mindfulness becomes infrastructure. Calm becomes governance. Therapy becomes compliance. The terrifying innovation is not that an evil machine controls everybody. It is that an extraordinarily competent system concludes that the remaining source of instability is the human being.That distinction matters because television does not need another evil-device dystopia. The genre's strongest contemporary properties work when the technology is merely the delivery mechanism for a recognizable human institution. Severance has been discussed precisely in terms of systemization, bureaucracy, bodies and minds; Black Mirror remains a reference point for technological structures that reorganize human experience.  Mindfulness Protocols belongs in that lineage but advances the question. Its central system does not primarily punish people. It arrives before them. Need is predicted before it becomes desire. Distribution anticipates consumption. Emotional disturbance is identified before it develops into narrative. The bracelet detects hesitation. The environment completes itself. Choice gradually becomes a historical artifact. The screen version therefore has a remarkably clean dramatic engine: every episode can ask what happens when a civilization capable of eliminating friction encounters a human impulse that requires friction to exist.Then Julian waits.For 1.4 seconds.That is your pilot trailer.A mechanical watch ticks. Julian's mind begins to anticipate—not an outcome, but sequence: after, then, again. His bracelet intervenes, but something has happened that the system cannot reverse. Correction arrives second. The internal report records a 1.4-second signal loss and 0.9-second correction latency. SAINTCOM treats the incident not as spiritual awakening but as a measurable systems failure.  This is excellent screen science fiction because the concept can be photographed. We do not need three pages of exposition about free will. We need a wrist, a watch, an almost imperceptible delay, the warmth of the correction beginning, and a man's face registering the first unsponsored second of his life. The revolution is a pause. That is the kind of idea directors, editors, composers and cinematographers can own.And the cinematography is unusually baked into the material. The City finishes itself: controlled light, softened edges, frictionless surfaces, predictive movement, compositions resolving before the viewer has time to interrogate them. Wyoming does the opposite. Wind pushes against the body. Ground is uneven. Distance remains distance. Horizons refuse closure. Water is dangerous. Shadows imply sources; sources imply distance; distance implies time. The manuscript itself makes that chain explicit.  This gives production a visual binary as immediately legible as the red of Gilead or the fluorescent maze of Lumon, without imitating either. The City should feel beautiful enough that an audience understands why humanity accepted it. Wyoming should initially feel almost unpleasant. The revelation is that the unpleasantness is life. One world has no visual accidents. The other cannot stop producing them. That is not production design applied after adaptation. That is production design embedded in the philosophy of the IP.The casting architecture is equally expandable. Julian is not the conventional chosen-one revolutionary. His threat is continuity. Elara occupies the devastating middle territory: a person trained by the system whose body begins recognizing a truth before her ideology can classify it. The Elegant Assassin may be the breakout character because she contains the property's contradiction in human form: stillness engineered for violence, someone who trained in mindfulness before alignment and therefore remembers when stillness was chosen rather than administered. Her line—AI decided suffering came from delay—compresses an entire civilization into one exchange.  Then there is Hale, potentially the role that attracts the prestige actor. Hale owns predictive distribution. Everyone else receives abundance; Hale retains production. He possesses everything and therefore goes looking for the one commodity the system cannot manufacture authentically: consequence. He enters the ocean because a hundred-foot wave does not care about his administrative privileges.  Julian rediscovers time from below. Hale rediscovers nature from above. Those trajectories can sustain seasons before they ever need to intersect.This is also where producers should stop thinking “adapt the novel” and start thinking storyworld. The Unadjusted alone can carry a parallel series. They are not resistance fighters in the familiar YA sense. They steal when they already have everything because stealing still creates consequence. They accumulate analog tools, mechanical watches and useless objects because physical possession refuses frictionless circulation.  A limited-series spinoff about the first Unadjusted cells could look and feel completely different from the flagship. A Hale prequel can dramatize the oligarchic consolidation that created predictive distribution. An Elegant Assassin series can begin before alignment, when mindfulness remains voluntary, and track the institutional mutation of a contemplative discipline into behavioral infrastructure. Stillwater can support a claustrophobic institutional thriller. Wyoming can eventually support a frontier story in which the great forbidden thing is not territory but unfinished experience. The Clerics can sustain an internal political drama. The Seven/Five AI architectures and the remaining ceremonial human government open an entire layer of boardroom and systems politics. The key is that these are not random extensions stapled onto a successful title. The primary text already contains distinct institutions, classes, geographies, histories and philosophical conflicts capable of changing genre while remaining inside the same universe.And then there is The Golden Gate Records, which is where the prequel opportunity becomes genuinely valuable. Instead of beginning with the completed dystopia, the prequel asks the more unnerving question: how did reasonable people build it? Not cartoon fascists. Not cackling technologists. People confronting layoffs, automation, economic displacement, mental-health pressures, public demand for stability and the seductive argument that systems capable of predicting harm should be permitted to prevent it. The observer gradually migrates into the system. Human institutions become protocols. Protocols begin communicating with protocols. Governance ceases to require a conspiracy because each rational optimization hands the next system a slightly narrower set of permissible outcomes. The prequel can therefore inhabit our visual world rather than the City's. No giant futuristic budget is required at the beginning. The future arrives by subtraction. Fewer people in rooms. Fewer decisions requiring people. Fewer interfaces asking permission. The audience realizes only gradually that the meeting has become the API.That gives a serious showrunner an unusual advantage: the franchise can move backward and forward simultaneously. The flagship tells us what the civilization became. The Golden Gate Records tells us how it happened. Other stories can show what happened elsewhere while the City believed itself universal. The chronology can accommodate anthology episodes, prestige serialized seasons, limited-series character studies and eventually features. Black Mirror supplies the anthology comparison; Westworld and Lost supply the mythology comparison; The Handmaid's Tale demonstrates how a dystopian literary property can expand through serial television and across media. Scholarship has specifically examined The Handmaid's Tale as a transmedia franchise, while studies of ARG structure identify Westworld among examples in which fictional websites and other channels blur the border between story and reality.  But Mindfulness Protocols has an unusual head start: its transmedia layer is not waiting for a marketing department to invent one.That is the part an executive should examine carefully. Warning Lab exists. DriftGuard exists. SPONCI exists. Narrative Drift exists across publishing/social channels. The Wyoming Gazette functions as an artifact from another edge of the world. There are research papers and a mathematical vocabulary surrounding drift, adaptive capacity and Dual Error. There are dossiers, machine-language documents, system warnings, institutional voices, fictional and quasi-institutional publishing surfaces, video pieces, visual campaigns and Easter eggs. The audience can encounter the universe without first being told, “Here is the official promotional website for our television show.” That distinction is exactly what gives good ARG work its charge: fictitious organizations, sites, blogs and channels behave as though they belong to the world rather than announcing themselves as advertising. Research on ARG structures describes precisely that blurring of fictional and authentic channels.There is also a lesson from Lost worth putting directly into the development memo: do not make the ARG homework. Transmedia analysis of Lost has documented the difficulty of making elaborate ARG extensions integral to an already complicated television production, and the franchise eventually scaled those efforts back.  That is useful precedent, not a warning away from this property. The architecture here allows the correct solution. The television series must remain emotionally and narratively complete. The ARG should deepen the world for viewers who choose to enter it. A casual viewer gets Julian, Elara, Hale and SAINTCOM. A committed viewer discovers a classified incident report online. A deeper viewer finds Warning Lab. Another discovers a Wyoming Gazette article apparently predating an event dramatized in the series. Someone runs a DriftGuard inquiry. Someone notices terminology migrating between a supposedly real systems document and a fictional SAINTCOM directive. Nobody needs the clue to understand Episode 6. But the viewer who follows it begins to wonder where the property stops.That is the marketing department's dream because the marketing conceit is also the thematic conceit.The campaign is about determining which documents belong to the story in a story about determining which reality is authoritative.Friends and family become useful here—not as celebrity stunt casting, but as the social perimeter of the world. Give supporting performers, creators and collaborators tiny artifacts rather than generic promotional posts. A photograph. A warning. A corrupted meditation clip. An Object Amnesty notice. A Wyoming travel fragment. A mechanical watch with an unexplained timestamp. A “Call to Meditate” interruption inside otherwise ordinary media. The ARG grows laterally through people rather than merely vertically through studio accounts. The audience should encounter evidence before it encounters explanation. By premiere week, the Internet should feel as though the series has been leaking into it for months.And importantly, DuPont's theoretical work gives the writers' room something most high-concept properties do not possess: rules underneath the lore. The DuPont Framework models the relationship between a moving external condition and a system's adaptive capacity. The fictional expression is brutally simple. When reality and the model diverge, which one does the institution correct? SAINTCOM's answer is the human subject. That is why the title Correct the Subject is so useful. The system is not malfunctioning in the conventional robot-rebellion sense. It detects discrepancies beautifully. It classifies them. It responds. Its catastrophic error is epistemological: it assumes its model is the stable reference frame. This gives every season a reusable dramatic question without forcing every season to repeat the same plot.Season One can be Sequence: Julian, Elara, the 1.4 seconds, Wyoming emerging as an unclassifiable continuity event. Season Two can widen into Contagion: hesitation spreads not as ideology but tempo. The manuscript already establishes that subjects need not discuss Wyoming; they simply begin pausing before answering and remembering how to wait.  Season Three can move upward into Hale and the Architects, revealing the bargain behind abundance and the oligarchs' increasingly strange relationship to consequence. Another season can expose the machine-to-machine layer underneath human administration. A final movement can force the defining question: what happens when a civilization optimized to remove uncertainty discovers that uncertainty was not a defect in human existence but one of its enabling conditions? None of those seasons requires a bigger Death Star. The escalation is conceptual, emotional and institutional.That is why this can attract real actors. Julian isn't asked to save Earth with a glowing object. He has to rediscover anticipation. Elara has to decide whether an involuntary hesitation is pathology or knowledge. The Assassin must confront the difference between the discipline she chose and the discipline she now administers. Hale can own civilization and envy a man who still experiences an unpredicted second. The Clerics can sincerely believe they are reducing suffering. Even SAINTCOM should never be performed as a villain. The more compassionate it sounds, the worse it becomes. One of the manuscript's most effective inversions is that emergency response does not make the City louder; it makes it softer. The Calls increase. The language becomes gentler. The system “escalates care.”That phrase should be on the wall of the writers' room:ESCALATE CARE.Because that is the franchise's horror grammar.The second phrase should be:CORRECTION ARRIVED SECOND.That is its thriller grammar.And the third:WYOMING IS NOT A LOCATION. IT IS THE IDEA THAT SOMETHING COMES NEXT.That is its mythology.There is another reason this property is ready for screen: it understands iconography. Mechanical watches. Bracelets. robes. soft system light. Call to Meditate. Object Amnesty. analog contraband. Wyoming horizons. Cortez Bank. Hale's bubble craft. the Assassin's silhouette. clerical chambers. SAINTCOM alerts. The imagery can be recognizable with the sound off. That matters. The Handmaid's Tale demonstrated how strongly cinematography and visual symbolism can carry dimensions of a literary property that prose carries differently; scholarship on its transmedia adaptations specifically notes the importance of cinematography in translating agency across media.  Mindfulness Protocols offers that opportunity everywhere. The adaptation should not illustrate the prose. It should translate the system into framing, duration, sound and interruption.Sound may be as important as photography. A perfectly controlled ambient world. The tiny vibration of the bracelet. The Call. Silence that is never actually silent because the system is always present. And then:Tick.A mechanical watch becomes a jump scare.Wind becomes dialogue.A delayed answer becomes insurrection.A hundred-foot wave becomes the only honest character in the scene.That is https://t.co/Y52taOH6ro the executive conversation should not be “Can we turn this book into eight episodes?” That undersells the asset. The conversation is: which door into the universe creates the strongest first season while preserving everything behind it? The flagship should stay intimate enough that Julian's 1.4 seconds matter. Do not begin by explaining the Seven. Do not diagram the Framework. Do not tour the entire ARG. Do not make the audience study. Give them a beautiful world, let them feel that something about it is profoundly wrong, and allow one man to discover that the missing thing is next.Then open the doors.The Unadjusted.The Assassin.Hale.Stillwater.The Clerics.The oligarchs.The machine architectures.The Golden Gate Records.Wyoming.The DriftGuard layer.The Narrative Drift layer.The Gazette.The dossiers.The machine documents.The ARG.The prequel.The side stories.The feature-length events.The artifacts that appear between seasons.This is where the Lost comparison becomes useful but should not become destiny. Lost proved that viewers will investigate a world together; later analysis also shows the danger of mythology proliferating faster than narrative obligation can service it.  Mindfulness Protocols should take the appetite and reject the debt. Every mystery needs an underlying rule. Every extension should answer something while opening something else. The Framework can provide that discipline. The ARG should reward attention, never rescue weak plotting. The television series is the cathedral. Everything else is evidence that the religion has escaped the building.And that may be the cleanest executive argument for the whole package.Hollywood usually acquires a manuscript and then spends years trying to manufacture what is already sitting around this one: a visual identity, a mythology, a lexicon, a philosophical engine, an expandable chronology, institutional artifacts, prequel logic, character-specific spinoff lanes and a transmedia environment capable of operating before, during and between https://t.co/1CfspkRpSf, the unusual problem is the opposite.There may be too much property.That's a good problem for a producer.The job is not to invent the universe.The job is to choose where the camera enters it.Start with a man.Put a mechanical watch beside him.Let the perfect world continue anticipating everything.Then let it miss him by 1.4 seconds.Cut to https://t.co/5SFKhFqHLa TO https://t.co/Qts0gGNSBm you have the https://t.co/OVzMfxTCpy you have the pilot.And behind it, if the room is disciplined enough not to spend everything at once, you have seasons, prequels, character series, limited runs, films, digital extensions, ARG events and a mythology capable of changing genre without changing its central question.When reality and the model disagree, which one gets corrected?SAINTCOM already has its answer.Correct the subject.The franchise begins when the subject answers back.

text:
A U.S. government investigation found overcrowding, abuse, and the use of small metal cages as “calming areas” at Alligator Alcatraz, a southern Florida migrant detention center, after several inspections, according to a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General report.

President Donald Trump inaugurated the facility in July 2025. Inspectors described cells measuring 1.7 square meters as among the report’s most revealing details. Up to 79 migrants were confined in these restrictive spaces between July 17, 2025, and January 18, 2026. Staff alleged the 2.3-meter-high enclosures were meant to calm detainees and even said detainees requested them, but the investigation found evidence they were also used as punishment, contravening humane treatment rules.

The investigation found that space at the center fell far below national requirements. National rules require at least 7 square meters per detainee; at maximum capacity, the facility offered only 2.6 square meters per person, reducing daily movement and increasing stress and disease risk.

The report also found serious failures in sanitation, medical care, and food standards alongside the space limitations. Detainees reported significant delays in clinical evaluations for new arrivals, insufficient personal hygiene items, and food rations that were too small and poorly preserved. They were also prohibited from going outside for weeks.

DHS defended the center, saying it operated under a framework agreement with the state of Florida and not under the direct management of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), so federal detention standards did not apply, it argued.

text:
🛑She Doesn’t Get to Frame the Debate🛑

Michelle O’Neill has welcomed UUP leader Jon Burrows “to the united Ireland debate.” She also declared that Andy Burnham “doesn’t get to take a border poll off the table.”

The arrogance is the point.

Burrows offered to debate the Union versus a united Ireland on any platform. That is a defence of the constitutional status quo and a willingness to argue the case for Northern Ireland remaining in the United Kingdom. O’Neill immediately reframed it as him joining her project. In her telling, the only debate that exists is the one that ends in Irish unity. Everything else is just timing and detail.

That is not how consent works. The Good Friday Agreement is clear. A border poll is triggered only if it appears likely that a majority in Northern Ireland would vote for change. Every reliable poll continues to show that majority does not exist. The people of Northern Ireland have not voted to leave the United Kingdom. Declaring that a poll cannot be “taken off the table” is an attempt to keep a minority preference permanently on life support as if it were inevitable.

O’Neill was speaking from Cardiff, where Sinn Féin, the SNP and Plaid Cymru were coordinating their constitutional messaging. The setting is consistent with the content. Three parties that want to break up the United Kingdom meet, and the Joint First Minister of Northern Ireland uses the occasion to tell the Prime Minister what he is not allowed to rule out and to redefine a unionist leader’s defence of the Union as participation in the unity project.

Jon Burrows does not need to be welcomed into anyone else’s debate. He is entitled to argue for the United Kingdom because that is the position supported by a majority of people in Northern Ireland. Framing every discussion of the constitutional future as “the united Ireland debate” is an attempt to make the preferred outcome of one party sound like the only adult conversation in the room.

The Union is not a temporary arrangement waiting for Michelle O’Neill’s permission to continue. It is the settled will of the people who live here. That will has not changed. No amount of reframing, Cardiff declarations or selective reading of the Agreement will make it change.

She does not get to decide the starting point of the conversation. The numbers still do.

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Sunday, September 15, 1935, Braniff Airways served its first inflight meal on board its plush new 10-passenger twin-engine Lockheed L-10A Electra airliner. The tasty inflight service was served by the co-pilot in a pre-prepared box over the Airline’s flights between Brownsville, and Corpus Christi, in Texas, and Tulsa, Oklahoma, and Kansas City, Missouri.

The big luxury Electras had just entered service on April 17, 1935, and held the prestigious title as Braniff’s first aircraft to have two engines. The Airline advertised the new aircraft as having “Two Engines, Two-Way Radio, Two Pilots and Two Rudders for Smoother Flying.” A short five months later, Braniff could add “Inflight Dining” to its list of improvements that were offered aboard the Lockheed Electra.

Braniff’s new in-flight service, which would grow over many decades to become the finest in the air without question, consisted of cold sandwiches carefully placed in a white box. This box was then handed out to each passenger by the co-pilot assigned to the flight. It wasn’t until the arrival of the magnificent Douglas DC-2 Skyliner in the spring of 1937, that Braniff retire its boxed lunches served by co-pilots and begin offering full hot meals in-flight served by Braniff Hostesses.

Photo: The plush comfort of Braniff's Lockheed L-10A passenger cabin featured high back lounge seating.. Braniff was known for providing “Friendly Transportation” and the Airline’s Hostess corps, which was hired in the spring of 1937 played a significant role in providing that special service level. Although the arrival of the DC-2 did bring plated hot meal service, initially and on certain flights the venerable box lunch was still served although not by the co-pilot.

Our Republic requires strong minded, independent thinkers to challenge one another from time to time…that includes challenging those who work on our behalf in assumed elevated seats of authority. Our Founders recognized this. 

If the next Governor of TN ends the appeal and embraces our Creator endowed right to keep and bear arms it will be well received. It will also perhaps demonstrate a recovery from the current inability in Nashville to hear from average people. 

Tennessee should lead the nation in the defense of and securing of our rights. It is really that simple, Liberty & Less Govt.

I think Tennesseans who embrace Liberty & Less Govt expect their employees in government to heed their petitions. Hopefully that is coming. I have hope for such. 

Hopefully there is a repentance before Almighty God by His people in turning to Him and embracing the Liberty that was granted our founders. The current idolatrous and out of alignment with our founding view that man is the dispenser and regulator of all rights is false. 

Men aged 26 to 70, fifty-six of them, asserted upon their sacred honor and at great risk to their person in 1776 that government had a single primary responsibility of securing our rights. I have hope and I ask the Lord to have mercy on Tennessee.

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Friday, September 15, 1961, Braniff International Airways introduced a new pilot uniform designed and manufactured by Hart Schaffner and Marx of Chicago, Illinois. The classic dark steel grey suits replaced the old dress blues uniforms, which had been in use since the 1940s.

Captain Willard Hayes, First Officer Charles Jamieson, and Second Officer Hardy Israelson modeled the new individually tailored uniforms with one of Braniff's new Boeing 707-227 El Dorado Super Jets as the backdrop. The stylish charcoal grey uniforms were styled by Hart Schaffner and Marx, the legendary men's clothier. Braniff's pilots decided a change was necessary and then selected the new suits through a series of processes that included creating special selection committees to determine the best replacement uniform.

The uniform coat consisted of a three-button single-breasted design that was tapered at the side for a tailored fit and incorporated a Raglan sleeve that allowed for even greater freedom of arm movement. A vent flap at the back of the coat also allowed for a range of easy non-restricted movements, often critical to pilots, that other coats did not offer. The steel grey fabric consisted of a Dacron-polyester and wool mix of 55-percent and 45-percent, respectively. The entire coat, which was offered in three-weights, was Scotch-Guard treated to ensure it would repel water and retain its shape under extreme weather and other environmental conditions.

A classic black topcoat topped off the ensemble that also included a black Captain's Hat with gold braid and Braniff insignias. A classic white dress shirt was accented with a black tie and black shoes, which created a highly professional look for Braniff's pilots. The 1961 uniform was the last before the classic redesign of all of Braniff's customer contact uniforms by Haute Couturier Marchese di Barsento Emilio Pucci of Florence, Italy, for the revolutionary End of the Plain Plane Campaign. Mr. Pucci designed a sleek black pilot uniform in 1965 that featured a nautical look, which was reintroduced again in 1973 in dark blue.

In 1977, Haute Couturier Halston designed a stylish new uniform for Braniff's pilots. Halston's uniform was the first departure from the dark colors that pilot uniforms had traditionally featured. A soft but warm light brown tailored and double-breasted uniform was introduced with dark brown accoutrements. The classic Alexander Girard gold wing sets were reintroduced by Halston in silver.

text:
THE $1.5 MILLION QUESTION

We drafted him in the 39th round. Two days before the signing deadline, we offered $750,000. The answer was still no.

“You’ll be back for that one too in five years.”

THE SCOUTING CLASSROOM
Stories Behind the Report

It was the fall of 2009, and I was sitting in the Kingham family home in Las Vegas. I was an Angels scout there to talk with Don Kingham about his oldest son, Nick, one of the best high school arms in a loaded 2010 Vegas draft class that included Bryce Harper, Kris Bryant and Donn Roach.

As we talked, Nick’s younger brother came flying down the stairs to go ride his bike.

Don stopped him. “Say hi to Mr. Scholzen.”

The kid threw up his hand. “Hi, Mr. Scholzen,” and disappeared out the door.

Don looked at me.

“You’ll be back for that one too in five years.”

He was right.

FIVE YEARS LATER

By then I was scouting for the Brewers, and that kid was a tall RHP at Desert Oasis HS named Nolan Kingham.

Nolan had a strong commitment to Texas. His older brother had signed with Pittsburgh out of high school, so the Kinghams understood the process and were upfront from the beginning.

$1.5 million

That’s what it would take for Nolan to give up Texas.

I put a strong second-round grade on him. Our West Coast Supervisor Corey Rodriguez saw him. Scouting Director Ray Montgomery saw him. We did our work and liked the player.

But eventually you reach the part of scouting most fans never see.

The scouting grade and the signability number have to meet.

THE 39TH ROUND

The 2015 Draft began and Nolan’s name didn’t get called.

Round after round passed. His number wasn’t changing.

In the 39th round of a 40-round Draft, Ray called.

Should we take Nolan anyway, maintain his rights through the signing period, see what money we saved elsewhere and find out if anything changed?

We did.

Nobody thought Nolan was a 39th-round talent.

I had a second-round grade on him.

That’s an important distinction. Where a player is drafted and where a scout grades him aren’t always the same thing.

THE $750,000 PHONE CALL

The signing deadline was July 17.

On July 15, I was in Milwaukee on vacation with my kids to watch the Brewers when Ray called me at the mall.

We had money available.

Call Nolan. See if he’ll take $750,000.

I called Don.

His answer was essentially what he’d told us all along.

Jeff, you know what it’s going to take.

$1.5 million

He told me how much he respected me and the Brewers and how well we’d treated their family, but they weren’t moving.

Nolan was going to Texas.

Then Don said he hoped Nolan would hear his name called again in three years.

And he hoped it would be the Brewers calling. 

No anger. No games. No burned bridge.

We simply couldn’t find the same number.

SOMETIMES BOTH SIDES ARE RIGHT

Three years later, Atlanta selected Nolan in the 12th round.

This time he signed for $150,000.

Then came eight years of grinding through the minor leagues and Mexico.

On August 3, 2026, the kid I first met running out his family’s front door finally climbed onto a Major League mound for the Texas Rangers.

Eleven years after we drafted him.

That’s baseball, and an important scouting lesson.

A scout can be right about the player and still not sign the player.

A scouting grade asks:

How good do we believe this player can become?

Signability asks:

What will it cost us to find out?

Sometimes those numbers meet.

Sometimes they don’t.

And sometimes a 39th-round pick can carry a second-round grade and a $1.5 million decision.

That’s the part of the Draft most fans never get to see.

SUBJECT: Support for the Clarity Act — Please Vote YES (James Rule)

September 15, 2026

Dear Senator:

My name is James Rule. I am a crypto educator and a constituent in Texas, and I am writing to ask you to vote YES on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act when the Senate votes today.

For too long, this industry has been forced to operate without clear rules. Instead of a functioning statutory framework, we have endured years of regulation-by-enforcement—a climate that punishes innovation and rewards uncertainty. The Clarity Act finally offers what American businesses, developers, and consumers deserve: regulatory certainty and a predictable path forward.

Without this framework, we are watching in real time as talent, capital, and innovative companies choose to build elsewhere. Singapore, Abu Dhabi, and the UAE are rolling out the welcome mat while we continue to debate. Every day of delay is a day we cede ground to competitors who understand that the future of finance and technology will be built onchain—and they want it built in their jurisdictions, not ours.

I am grateful for the months of serious, bipartisan work that have gone into this bill. Senators and staff on both sides of the aisle have grappled with hard questions about SEC and CFTC jurisdiction, consumer protection, and developer protections. That work has produced a balanced bill that protects consumers while giving builders the clarity they need to innovate here at home.

I urge you to preserve and protect the developer protections in this bill. These safeguards ensure that writing open-source software remains a protected activity in America. I also urge you to keep the compromise in Section 404—the provision addressing stablecoin rewards—intact. That section reflects months of careful, good-faith negotiation, and it should not be reopened or weakened by last-minute efforts from the Big Banks.

The Clarity Act is not a gift to any one industry. It is a framework that balances innovation with accountability, competition with protection, and ambition with common sense. It gives American builders the certainty they need to compete and win on the global stage.

I respectfully ask you to vote YES on the Clarity Act today.

Sincerely,

James Rule
Crypto Educator

🇺🇸 NEVER FORGET — The U.S. Mint Just Put 9/11 on America's Pocket Change

Twenty-five years after September 11, 2001, remembrance is being struck in metal.

The Treasury announced the special-issue 2026 Semiquincentennial Enduring Liberty Half Dollar one day before the 25th anniversary of the attacks — a coin bearing a privy mark with the date "9-11-01" encircled by the words NEVER FORGET. It honors the lives lost in both the September 11, 2001 attacks and the February 26, 1993 World Trade Center bombing.

And this isn't just any half dollar. The Enduring Liberty design is the first U.S. half dollar since 1964 without JFK's portrait — the obverse shows the Statue of Liberty gazing toward the future, while the reverse depicts Liberty passing her torch to a new generation, with the dual date 1776 ~ 2026 marking America's 250th birthday.

The story began quietly in August: the Mint presented 2,983 special West Point-struck coins — bearing an "ALWAYS REMEMBER" privy mark — to the National 9/11 Memorial & Museum. That mintage matches the 2,983 names inscribed on the Memorial itself.

One coin for every name. Let that sink in.

Now the public gets its turn. 🪙

📅 THE DETAILS:
Philadelphia-struck circulating-quality coins are offered in 20-coin rolls and 100-coin bags. Pre-orders opened September 10 and close September 25 at 3 p.m. ET, with shipping expected to begin December 3. Prices range from $40 to $100 depending on the product.

Demand is likely to be fierce — the non-privy Enduring Liberty two-roll sets sold 99.7% of their 100,000 limit, and this version carries far more emotional weight.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the coins symbols of the honor and bravery of victims, survivors, and first responders, while Mint Director Paul Hollis emphasized their role in teaching younger generations about events that happened before many of them were born.

That's the real purpose here. An entire generation of Americans has no living memory of that Tuesday morning. Soon, some of them will find this coin in their change — and ask what it means.

A half dollar that carries history forward, one hand to the next. Just like the torch on its reverse.

text:
Władysław Miegoń was born on 30 September 1892 in the village of Samborzec near Sandomierz, the eldest of eight children in a modest farming family. He entered the seminary after finishing school and was ordained a priest on 2 February 1915. After a few years of parish work in the Sandomierz diocese he sought permission to serve as a military chaplain in the newly independent Polish Army. In December 1919 he was assigned to the Marine Battalion and thus became one of the first chaplains of the Polish Navy.

He took part in the Polish-Soviet War of 1920, accompanying sailors in the fighting around Ostrołęka and Łomża. Wounded at Maków Mazowiecki, he was decorated in person by Marshal Józef Piłsudski with the Silver Cross of the Virtuti Militari and the Cross of Valour. After the war he served at naval bases in Puck and later Gdynia, where he became the first parish priest of the military church of Our Lady Queen of Poland in Oksywie and a trusted spiritual guide to the growing fleet. He also completed studies in canon law at the Catholic University of Lublin.

When Germany invaded in September 1939 he remained with the defenders of Gdynia and the Hel Peninsula. After the surrender he refused the chance to leave captivity and stayed with his sailors. He was first held in prisoner-of-war camps and then, in violation of the Geneva Convention, transferred to concentration camps—Buchenwald and finally Dachau, where he was registered as prisoner 21223. Even there he continued to hear confessions, share food, and offer what comfort he could. Weakened by hunger, hard labour and ill-treatment, he died on 15 October 1942. His body was burned in the camp crematorium.

On 13 June 1999 Pope John Paul II beatified him among the 108 Polish martyrs of the Second World War. He is remembered as the first fully fledged chaplain of the Polish Navy and as a priest who chose to share the fate of the men he served to the end.

text:
The identity of the kings matters less than the object of their movement. They are not marching merely to settle an ordinary regional dispute. Revelation 19:19 reveals the real purpose: “And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army.” The target is Jesus Christ. Whatever political explanations are broadcast to the world, Heaven records the campaign as open rebellion against the returning Son of God. The armies may be told that they are preserving peace, protecting civilization, defending humanity, or resisting an extraterrestrial invasion. The Beast’s press office can call it whatever it likes. God calls it war against Christ. Human propaganda always invents a respectable name for rebellion, but the King James Bible strips off the uniform and shows the treason underneath.

6. The Three Unclean Spirits and the Propaganda of Hell

Immediately after the river is dried, John sees “three unclean spirits like frogs” coming out of the mouths of the dragon, the Beast, and the false prophet. Revelation does not present the final campaign as the product of military calculation alone. Behind the visible rulers stands an invisible spiritual operation. The dragon supplies satanic authority, the Beast supplies political government, and the false prophet supplies religious deception. Out of their mouths come spirits because the campaign is advanced through communication, persuasion, proclamation, and lies. Hell understands the power of a message. The final world system will not move nations merely by tanks and treaties; it will move them through a supernatural narrative powerful enough to make kings believe that gathering against Jesus Christ is reasonable.

Revelation 16:14 identifies these emissaries plainly: “For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles.” The passage does not call their wonders illusions, clever technology, misunderstood machinery, or theatrical tricks. They work miracles. The Bible believer should not assume that every supernatural display comes from God. Pharaoh’s magicians produced signs. A lying spirit deceived Ahab’s prophets. Second Thessalonians 2 warns of “power and signs and lying wonders.” Revelation 13 shows the false prophet doing great wonders and deceiving those who dwell upon the earth by means of miracles. The last generation will not reject Christ because it lacks supernatural evidence. It will reject Him while being overwhelmed by supernatural evidence from the wrong source. The world that mocked biblical miracles will suddenly become very religious when the devil begins performing them.

The frog-like spirits go “forth unto the kings,” showing that demonic activity can operate at the highest levels of human government. The modern mind imagines evil spirits haunting abandoned houses and frightening people in dark bedrooms. Revelation places them in the courts of rulers, influencing international decisions and arranging a worldwide campaign. They do not waste their final hour making cupboard doors creak; they address kings. Their objective is coordinated rebellion. They sell the nations one central lie: mankind must unite against the One coming from Heaven. The devil who once offered Christ the kingdoms of the world will finally mobilize those kingdoms against Christ. Satan’s foreign policy has never changed. He opposes God’s King, attacks God’s land, persecutes God’s people, and persuades human rulers that serving the devil is an act of enlightened self-preservation.

7. “The Kings of the Earth and of the Whole World”

The Euphrates opens a route for the kings of the east, but the demonic mission extends to “the kings of the earth and of the whole world.” That phrase prevents the reader from reducing Armageddon to a private quarrel between Israel and a few nearby states. The final conflict has a worldwide dimension. The nations become involved because the controversy is worldwide: Who owns

text:
NEWS: A long-running federal lawsuit could open the door to cheaper but less comprehensive health plans that avoid some Affordable Care Act and state insurance rules.

The case involves Data Marketing Partnership, which argues that people who join its limited partnership — in part by allowing an app to track their internet activity — should count as employees eligible for the company’s self-funded health plan. If that argument succeeds or the Labor Department settles on favorable terms, similar arrangements could expand quickly. 

Supporters say these plans could offer a lower-cost alternative for people priced out of ACA coverage. Critics warn they could function like lightly regulated insurance, with fewer required benefits and less state oversight. Maryland Insurance Commissioner Marie Grant says the outcome could hurt consumers and weaken states’ ability to regulate coverage. 

Maryland has already taken action against one company offering this type of limited-partnership coverage, fining The Vitamin Patch in 2024 after determining it was not licensed to sell insurance in the state. 

The bigger fight is over choice versus regulation: should consumers be allowed to buy cheaper, leaner coverage outside much of the ACA framework — or does that simply create a new market for plans that leave people exposed when major medical bills hit?

【 Day 4: Pivot 】Why AI Thought and Body Are Fractured: Descartes' Curse and the "Perceptual Chain" Perspective ☯️🧠

Why are AI "Thought (LLMs)" and "Body (Robotics)" so fundamentally severed?

The root cause lies in Descartes' Mind-Body Dualism, an ideological curse of Western modern science that isolated spirit from matter.

Surprisingly, modern science has failed to define—or even name—the core translation protocol connecting abstract thought to physical movement:

・Outbound (Thought → Body): We have "Motor Commands," but no name for the translation algorithm of how thought becomes movement.

・Inbound (Body → Thought): We have "Proprioception," but no name for the protocol where physical sensations ascend into high-level cognition.

While computers rely on Printer Drivers to bridge data and physical paper, AI today is like manually specifying font shapes and layout logic for every single character directly to the printer press.

I define this missing cross-translation protocol as the "Perceptual Chain."

It is not a one-way control pulse, but a bi-directional feedback loop where physical sensory friction continually shapes thought, which then smoothly flows into the next physical action.

3. 3 Insights from the Eastern Paradigm: "Mind-Body Unity (心身一如)"

・The "Form (型)" IS Thought: A Noh dancer doesn't bow because they feel grief; grief manifests through the physical form itself.

・Breath (気/息合い) as the Missing Link: The biological protocol that synchronizes the autonomic nervous system with physical motion.

・Dynamic Feedback (間合い): Dissolving the border between self and environment so spatial interaction becomes a unified perceptual system.

4. Conclusion: From Driverless AI to Unified Architecture Current AI is essentially dreaming. Humanity taught AI how to speak its dreams (LLMs), but forgot to teach it how to wake up and walk (Perceptual Chain).

We don't need larger parameter counts. We need to define a Non-Cartesian Protocol that weaves cerebrum and body into a single fabric from day one.

This declaration is our covenant with the people and we hereby bind the party and its candidates with this [signation?] to the pledges made there herein. With all my heart and soul, with every particle of high purpose that is within me, I pledge you my word to do everything I can to put every particle of courage, of common sense, and of strength that I have at your disposal, and to endeavor so far as strength has given me to live up to the obligations you have put upon me and to endeavor to carry out in the interest of our whole people the policies to which you have today solemnly dedicated yourselves in the name of the millions of men and women for whom you speak."

I hope we shall win, and I believe that if we can wake the people to what the fight really means we shall win. But, win or lose, we shall not falter. Whatever fate may at the moment overtake any of us, the movement itself will not stop. Our cause is based on the eternal principles of righteousness; even though we who now lead may for the time fail, in the end the cause itself shall triumph. Men, listen carefully.

A lot of young guys out here are trading their future for quick comfort with women old enough to be their mothers — even their grandmothers.

What looks like “opportunity” is actually spiritual debt.

And the price is your masculinity, your mind, and your destiny.

1. SHE’S NOT A BLESSING — SHE’S A SHORTCUT WITH A BILL

Older women know exactly what they’re doing.

They offer comfort, money, and attention — and in return, they take your strength, your discipline, and your drive.

Nothing is free. Ever.

She has lived decades longer than you.

Pain, heartbreak, trauma, insecurities, curses, spiritual baggage — all packed inside her.

Every time you sleep with her, you inherit weight your young spirit was never built to handle.
