text:
The Dry Martyrdom of Cardinal Joseph Mindszenty by William A. Borst, Ph.D.
.
The biography of Cardinal Joseph Mindszenty reads more like a European horror show than the dedicated life of a servant of God. Unlike most Catholics who have been tortured and persecuted throughout Christian history, his Nazi and communist captors denied the Cardinal the crowning glory of martyrdom. However his 35 years of imprisonment was tantamount to a dry martyrdom. His constant suffering made him a de facto martyr because he did everything he could for his faith except give his life.
.
Incarceration and Invasion
.
Of peasant stock, Joseph Mindszenty was born József Pehm on March 29, 1892 in Mindszent in western Hungary in what was part of the Austria-Hungarian Empire. In 1941 he adopted the name of his village instead of Pehm partly because it sounded too Germanic. After his graduation from high school he entered the seminary in Szombathely and was ordained to the priesthood on June 12, 1915.
.
With the end of World War I in 1918 and the end of the empire, his life changed dramatically. Hungary quickly became a hostile country for the Catholic Church. As a result Mindszenty was destined to spend much of his life in jail, prison or under house arrest. He was first arrested on February 9, 1919 and interned in the episcopal palace until the fall of Béla Kun’s government the following July.
.
The communists had sent him to jail for his opposition to their nationalization of the Catholic schools. Mindszenty had acerbated his situation by urging the faithful to oppose the new regime because he believed the communists intended to destroy the Church in Hungary.
.
Between wars Mindszenty chafed under the injustices inflicted on Hungary. On March 4, 1944 Pope Pius XII appointed him diocesan bishop of Veszprém. Two weeks later the German military forces occupied Hungary in order to prevent it from concluding a separate peace with the Allies. He was arrested again on November 27, 1944 for his opposition to the Arrow Cross, the Hungarian wing of the Nazi occupational government’s plan to quarter soldiers in Mindszenty’s living quarters.
.
Stalin’s Best Pupil
.
Mindszenty remained imprisoned until April 1945 when the Soviet Army liberated Hungary. He emerged a national hero, not only for Catholics, but also for Protestant organizations because of his consistent resistance to tyranny. Upon his return to Veszprem, he was faced with the Soviet collectivization of Hungary’s farms, which drastically hurt Church revenues. While the communists offered subsidies, the Catholic press remained restricted by the government.
.
On September 16, 1945, Pope Pius XII appointed him as archbishop of Esztergom and primate of Hungary. At his first episcopal conference in October in Budapest, the archbishop criticized the communists’ land reform and their anti-church policies. The following year the pope elevated him to a Cardinal.
.
In early 1947, the Soviet Union pressed Mátyás Rákosi, Hungary’s new leader to stamp out Hungarian dissent. Dubbed the bald murderer, Rákosi used Stalinist political and economic methods to establish a communist order, making Hungary one of the most brutal dictatorships in Europe. Stalin's best pupil presided over several purges, as thousands perished and many more suffered deprivation and torture.
.
Rákosi’s oppression greatly impacted the Catholic educational system. In April 1948 the minister of religion and education came forth with a proposal for the re-nationalization of the Catholic schools, but the Cardinal demanded that the secularization of the schools be dropped from their agenda. The bishops angered the communists when they flatly refused to recognize the Hungarian Republic, which was nothing more than a satellite for Soviet Russia’s orbit. In his December 8th letter, Cardinal Mindszenty pointed out that recognition was impossible because of their materialistic atheism. As a result he was arrested again and accused of treason.
.
Trials and Tribulations
.
The official charges of the Cardinal’s arrest were conspiracy and espionage. The communists twisted his words and submitted forged confession documents. Always true to his word he refused to compromise with their unredeemable evil. The communists also presented a farcical list that detailed a cornucopia of his offenses that varied from the imaginative to
.
the completely ridiculous. They charged the Cardinal with more than 40 crimes, the most notable of which were foreign-currency abuses and sabotage of Hungarian land reform.
.
The communists also said that he had orchestrated the theft of Hungary's crown jewels, including the Crown of Saint Stephen with the explicit purpose of crowning Otto von Habsburg emperor of Eastern Europe. Mindszenty had also, they charged, planned a Third World War that would lead to his assuming political power in Hungary. The Cardinal declared that any confession with his name on it had to be the result of torture.
.
At the notorious Secret Police Headquarters at 60 Andrassy St. in Budapest, the Cardinal was interrogated relentlessly for 39 consecutive days and nights. They tortured and apparently brainwashed the Cardinal with the most diabolical torture and mind-altering tactics that the communists had been perfecting for years. During the day he was deprived of sleep, and drugs were put into his food to break his will. Twice each night for 29 days he was beaten until unconscious with a rubber truncheon all over his naked body. After his mind and body had been broken, Cardinal Mindszenty underwent what was later called a show trial. There he confessed to the charges against him and was sentenced to life imprisonment. He later recanted his entire forced confession.
.
Like something out of Franz Kafka’s novel, the Mindszenty trial put a human face on the moral struggle between East and West. The Free World finally recognized the Soviet Union for what it really was. The fate of one Catholic priest had become of profound interest to a West that had applauded even worse Catholic persecutions in Spain only a decade removed.
.
The Prison Shuffle
.
Cardinal Mindszenty languished in a succession of damp and frigid cells, subject to the blows and blasphemies of psychotic guards for eight years while the Hungarian government completed the total subjugation of the Church. Religious orders were thrown out of their buildings and jailed. Nuns were prohibited from nursing as well as teaching. Mindszenty's successor as head of the Hungarian hierarchy was Archbishop Joseph Grosz, who acquiesced to every government demand. His craven behavior did not save him from a Mindszenty-style arrest and trial and a voluntary confession to every charge.
.
Following the abortive Hungarian Revolution in 1956, President Eisenhower gave Cardinal Mindszenty asylum at the American Embassy in Budapest. His presence later became an inconvenience to the United States government because it strained relations between Hungary’s communists and the American government.
.
The outcry against the Hungarian’s inhumane treatment of Mindszenty had been near universal in the West. Pope Pius XII called his arrest a serious outrage . . . on every upholder of the dignity and liberty of man. He defended the cardinal's right to oppose the government when it contradicted divine and human rights. New York's Cardinal Francis Spellman roared, if this be treason, to deny allegiance to atheistic communist government – then thank God Cardinal Mindszenty confessed to treason.
.
A Cult Figure
.
Cardinal Mindszenty was fast becoming a Cold War cult figure for his valiant stand against atheistic communism. He was featured on the February 14th, 1949 cover of Time magazine, which had been a steadfast opponent of communism and fascism. A priest suffering torture for the faith might not have been a popular subject among Hollywood’s elite but it resonated well at the box office, especially with millions of Catholics who loved to go to the movies. Even then it took the courage of Eagle Lion, a small studio, who assumed the risks in producing Guilty of Treason in 1950.
.
The story revolves around a fictitious American reporter Tom Kelley, who arrives in Hungary shortly before the Cardinal's arrest. There he encounters a music teacher, named Stephanie. She is a Hungarian patriot, who is also in love with a fanatical Russian colonel. Acting on a tip, the couple visit Mindszenty's mother at the family farm, where they meet the Cardinal himself who boldly predicts that the Russians will arrest and vilify him. His prophecy rings true with his imprisonment and the shattering of his reputation.
.
Now a NKVD torture dungeon, the Cardinal was taken to the same location the Nazis used. The communists made him stand in a spotlight in a darkened room while his unseen interrogators accuse him of plotting to restore the monarchy, speculating with American money and working with the Pope to start another world war with Russia. After weeks of torture the Cardinal collapsed without making a confession. Their use of the hypnotic drug scopolamine effectively reduced his mind to jelly. While Guilty of Treason is an extraordinary time capsule, the Cardinal’s tragic saga, served more as a tool in the Cold War battle against world communism than as a chronicle of a religious hero.
.
A National Monument
.
Cardinal Mindszenty’s ordeal prompted a second movie, even as the world had moved on to larger concerns like the threat of nuclear destruction. In 1955 The Prisoner was produced, with Alec Guinness in the title role. This film contrasted to Guilty of Treason in that there was scant mention of the geopolitics of the Cold War nor was Cardinal Mindszenty identified by name.
.
The Cardinal's chief antagonist in the movie, the Inquisitor had been part of the anti-Nazi Resistance. He informed the Cardinal that he was a hero but now he is a national monument that must be destroyed. At their next meeting he warns the Cardinal that he will get at the truth. The Cardinal replies, surely it's a confession you're after, not the truth. In a frightening tone he ripostes that the State really wants his mind.
.
The Cardinal is eventually worn down by the Inquisitor’s, incessant questioning.
.
He finally succumbs to the communists’ mind games and confesses to being a traitor. Despite his professional triumph, the Inquisitor is remorseful. While the Cardinal receives the death penalty, the Inquisitor informs him that the sentence has been commuted. In a strange twist of fate, the Inquisitor admits: Then the laugh is on me. You go out from under my hands as a stronger man than when you came to me. The Inquisitor knows he is the one in the trap and he will be devoured by his own system.
.
Open Windows
.
His 15 years under virtual house arrest in the American embassy had only made the Cardinal stronger. His presence however was still a constant thorn in the communist side. Communist agents awaited him day and night, hoping to recapture him if he left the sanctuary of the embassy.
.
By the early 1960s both the Western governments and the popes decided that peace accords with the communists were not only preferable but also necessary in light of a rapidly changing geopolitical scene. John XXIII and Paul VI other Vatican accommodationists welcomed an open windows’ policy with the Soviet Union. The Cardinal’s visible presence created a dilemma for the new Ostpolitik, managed by Pope Paul's Secretary of State, Agostino Casaroli.
.
Mindszenty’s reputation as a Christian warrior was a constant reminder of the communists grim past. This created an intractable obstacle to the pope’s larger vision of peaceful accords with the communists. As the Cold War thawed, Pope Paul persuaded Mindszenty to leave. So in 1971 the Cardinal reluctantly left the embassy sanctuary and traveled into exile, first to Rome where he stayed for two months in 1971 before finally settling in Vienna.
.
Final Betrayal
.
Even in his Vienna exile, Mindszenty had become an albatross around the neck of the Vatican. In the fall of 1973, as he prepared to publish his Memoirs, the Cardinal suffered the final betrayal. Fearful that the truth would upset the detente with the Marxists, the Pope asked Mindszenty to resign his office. When he refused, the Pope declared his See vacant, to the delight of the communist regime.
.
Obedient to the end, the Cardinal felt deceived by the Vatican policy of rapprochement with communism. He spent the rest of his life caring for the spiritual welfare of his scattered Hungarian flock around the world. The Cardinal continued to make it clear that he had not abdicated, but had been deposed.

From The 48 Laws of Power by Robert Greene.

If they can predict your next move, they can block it.

Most people leak the plan in the name of being “transparent.” Then they wonder why the room is already against them.

Law 3/48 — Conceal your intentions

Talk. Just not about the real target.
Appear open. Stay unreadable.

In 1850, Otto von Bismarck was a 35-year-old deputy in the Prussian parliament. Many around him wanted war with Austria at once. Bismarck wanted that war too. Not yet. The army was not ready, and the king opposed it.

Had he said “wait, then strike,” both the king and the war party would have turned on him. So he did the opposite. He argued against war. He praised peace. People heard a man cooling the room. They did not hear the plan.

In 1862 he became Prussia’s minister-president. In 1866 Prussia fought Austria and won. Austria was pushed out of German leadership. Prussia became the centre of a new Germany.

He did not stay silent. Silence looks like a secret.
He talked — about the wrong aim — until the real one was ready.

Spot it being used on you:
They share a lot, but never the deadline, the offer, or the actual goal.
That is not openness. That is fog.

Your move: don’t announce the plan in Slack.
Announce the next small step only.

text:
Earl Holliman (b. 11 September 1928) was an American actor whose Southern manner and rugged masculinity made him a familiar presence in films and television for more than half a century.

Born in Delhi, Louisiana, he was adopted as an infant and grew up in difficult circumstances. Restless and fascinated by the movies, he briefly joined the U.S. Navy while still underage, later reenlisted legally, and eventually studied acting in California.

Holliman emerged in Hollywood during the 1950s, frequently playing soldiers, cowboys, and sensitive young toughs. His notable films included The Big Combo (1955), the science-fiction classic Forbidden Planet (1956), Giant (1956), and The Rainmaker (1956), for which he earned a Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor.

Television brought Holliman an even wider audience. He memorably starred as a frightened amnesiac in “Where Is Everybody?”, the first broadcast episode of The Twilight Zone in 1959. His best-known television role came as Lieutenant Bill Crowley, the sympathetic superior of Angie Dickinson's Sgt. Pepper Anderson on Police Woman (1974–78), appearing in 90 episodes.

Holliman was a gay man who belonged to a generation of Hollywood performers for whom openness about homosexuality could threaten a career. Consequently, he maintained an exceptionally guarded private life. Contemporary publicity occasionally linked him with women, but Holliman himself offered the public remarkably little information about his intimate relationships.

Only much later did the fuller picture of his private life become apparent. He was linked as a long-term partner to fellow actor Anthony George (Dark Shadows, Search for Tomorrow, One Life to Live), whose death in March 2005 was announced by Earl (who referred to him as his “pal”). At the time of his own death, Holliman's surviving spouse was Craig Curtis, who confirmed that Holliman had died at their Studio City home at age 96 on November 25, 2024. Major obituaries identified Curtis explicitly as Holliman's husband. Their relationship had been kept so private that even many longtime admirers of Earl were unaware that he had a male spouse.

One of the last surviving leading men of 1950s Hollywood, Earl Holliman’s career remains notable for the unusual combination of toughness, vulnerability, and understated charm he brought to both the big and small screens. 🏳️‍🌈

text:
Grok is describing what Lindsay’s defense CHOSE to do, not what Massachusetts law REQUIRES. Lindsay pleaded NOT GUILTY. She did not plead guilty and then ask to be excused because she was insane. In Massachusetts, lack of criminal responsibility results in a NOT GUILTY verdict. Her defense may have chosen not to contest certain facts and may have offered stipulations, but a defendant does NOT have to admit committing the crime in order to raise lack of criminal responsibility.
Massachusetts’s own homicide instructions specifically address WHETHER a defendant has conceded committing the crime. If concession were mandatory, there would be no "whether."
So Grok’s description of the defense strategy does not prove your claim that NGRI legally requires an admission. It doesn’t. So as of now there's no confession or a verdict of guilt on record.

Based on the two transcript files, here are the 10 most extreme, conspiratorial, or factually unhinged claims made during the Sarah Westall / Michael Letts interview:

1. "Military tribunals have been initiated and indictments are forthcoming"
Letts claims military tribunals have been "created" and "charged," with indictments ready to be served against high-profile figures including Obama, Brennan, and Susan Rice. He presents this as an ongoing, real operation — while admitting the public won't see them until "the investigation is complete." This is a years-old conspiracy theory that has never materialized.
2. "68–70% of the deficit is caused by embezzlement, fraud, and stealing — almost 100% with interest"
Letts asserts that internal documents show most of the national deficit is due to stolen money, and that when you add interest on the stolen money, it approaches 100% of the deficit. He provides no source, no document, and no verification. This is an extraordinary claim presented as fact.

3. "We have two options: military tribunals or another revolution"
Letts frames the choice as either military tribunals or a 1776-style revolution — explicitly invoking the possibility of mass destruction and comparing it to dropping the atomic bomb in WWII. This is rhetoric that normalizes the overthrow of the civilian government.
4. "Congress is a mafia bigger than the mob ever was"
Letts claims the corruption is a global criminal organization "headquartered" in the US, controlling the world's most powerful military and wealthiest country. He says it's the "most elaborate, most sophisticated criminal organization ever to exist in history." This is hyperbolic conspiracy framing.

5. "FEMA didn't have money for North Carolina flood victims because it was transferred to illegals — and that's why they didn't care"
This is a distorted claim. Letts says FEMA's budget was moved to help illegal immigrants, which is why flood victims got no help. The reality is more nuanced (FEMA disaster relief funding is separate from other programs), but it's presented as proof of deliberate malice.
6. "They're stealing your tax money through NGOs, and Congress members sit on the boards"
Letts claims Congress creates thousands of NGOs to funnel government money, and that members of Congress serve on these boards and get paid substantial sums without even attending meetings. This is presented as the mechanism of theft — but no specific evidence is offered.

7. "They're propping up Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis to accelerate moral decay"
Westall claims she ran a "vocal print" analysis showing that figures like Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis are being propped up by the same forces to "help the moral decay quicken" and give people hopelessness. This is a conspiracy theory about influencer culture.
8. "The Christian base is being controlled by twisting scripture to destroy women"
Westall and Letts claim that there's a deliberate effort to use Christianity to attack women — telling them they need to be subservient and shouldn't vote — as part of a broader strategy to defang and control the Christian base. Letts, an ordained Baptist minister, validates this.

9. "The justice system is a kangaroo court — judges ignore the Supreme Court"
Letts claims activist judges simply "give a finger to the Supreme Court" and change a word or two in their rulings to defy them. He says the US has a "third world country kind of thing" because judges don't follow the rule of law. This is a sweeping indictment of the entire judiciary.
10. "We're in a PSY-OP war — they're so good at making it look like they care"
Both speakers repeatedly frame everything as a "psychological operation" and "psy-op war," claiming the media, tech companies, and influencers are all part of a coordinated effort to manipulate the public. This framing allows any contradictory evidence to be dismissed as part of the psy-op.

text:
Churchill Diverts Wheat Ships During the 1943 Bengal Famine: Policy, Racism, and Three Million Deaths

**Scale and Context of the Famine**

The Bengal Famine of 1943 was one of the deadliest disasters in the history of British India, claiming an estimated 2 to 3 million lives. Drought was not the cause of the famine. A study published in *Geophysical Research Letters*, analyzing soil moisture data from 1870 to 2016, found that among six major famines on the Indian subcontinent, the 1943 Bengal Famine was the only one not directly linked to insufficient soil moisture or crop failure. Vimal Mishra, an associate professor at the Indian Institute of Technology and the study's lead researcher, noted: "The 1943 Bengal Famine was caused entirely by policy failure." In fact, rainfall in the Bengal region between June and September 1943 was above average.

**Food Exports and the "Denial Policy"**

India continued to export large quantities of food during the famine. In *Churchill's Secret War*, Madhusree Mukerjee documents that between January and July 1943, India exported over 70,000 tons of rice—enough to sustain nearly 400,000 people for a full year. Simultaneously, the British implemented a scorched-earth strategy known as the "Denial Policy" along the Bengal coast to prevent a Japanese landing. Authorities confiscated more than 66,000 rural wooden boats—the region's lifeline for transport, trade, and fishing—and police destroyed or seized rice stocks. This policy devastated the regional economy, depriving millions of their food sources and livelihoods.

**The Decision to Divert Wheat Ships**

On August 4, 1943, during a War Cabinet meeting, Churchill refused to ship wheat to India. According to records kept by Leopold Amery (Secretary of State for India), Churchill remarked at the meeting that Indians "breed like rabbits" and suggested that the famine was of their own making. He chose to allocate wheat and shipping to build up stockpiles for civilians in the Balkans, intended for use after their liberation from Nazi occupation. The War Cabinet decided that approximately 75,000 tons of Australian wheat would be shipped monthly to Ceylon and the Middle East to support the war effort, while another 170,000 tons would be transported via famine-stricken India to supply depots in the Mediterranean.

**Rejection of Aid from the US and Canada**

The United States and Australia offered assistance, but the British War Cabinet was unwilling to release the necessary shipping. Mukherjee’s research indicates that when the US proposed transporting grain using its own vessels, Britain failed to follow up on the offer. Canada also offered to supply wheat—transportable to India via either the Pacific or the Atlantic-Mediterranean route—but this offer was likewise rejected on the grounds that shipping was required for other routes.

**Continued Refusals in 1944**

The famine did not end with the harvest at the close of 1943. Minutes from an April 1944 War Cabinet meeting reveal that the Viceroy of India made an urgent request for another 724,000 tons of wheat to meet minimum civilian needs and military requirements. The Minister of War Transport stated that maintaining an additional 50,000 tons of imports per month—on top of the 200,000 tons already pledged—was "out of the question." Churchill argued that further relief could only be provided at the cost of "serious difficulties" elsewhere. He ultimately authorized the shipment of 100,000 tons of Australian wheat to India, a quantity far insufficient to address the crisis.

Recruitment posts online pitch it as a way to “make extra cash” by reaching out through your own network.

Who pays for it
The Maine Wire reported that the program is paid for by the Organizing Empowerment Project (also called Empower Project), a Wisconsin-based 501(c)(4) founded by Mike Pfohl. It said the effort is partnered with the National Education Association and the Progressive Turnout Project.
Organizing Empowerment Project (EIN 84-2852380, McFarland, WI) describes its work as civic engagement, expanding the electorate, and training groups in “relational organizing.” It is not a Maine-based charity. In recent IRS filings it reported about $15.2 million in revenue, mostly contributions.

Documented funders of that organization (grants reported in public 990/Candid data, not a complete donor list):

Tides Foundation — multiple grants over several years, including large amounts in 2020, 2022, and 2024
Hopewell Fund — about $1.75–$1.8 million in 2024
Future Forward USA Action
America Votes, AFSCME, and other advocacy groups
Tides and Hopewell are often described in reporting as part of larger progressive donor networks; Hopewell is frequently linked to funding associated with Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss. A 501(c)(4) does not have to publish every individual donor the way a candidate PAC does, so the full money trail behind the $250 offers is only partly public.

The $250 figure is what people are being offered for participation in the texts/recruitment you saw. Public reporting confirms cash is being offered for the training/outreach work; I did not find an official rate sheet listing $250 as a fixed stipend.

This is political organizing pay, not a state of Maine program or a neighborhood mutual-aid group. If a text asks for personal contacts, bank info, or a lot of personal data up front, treat it like any paid political recruitment and check the disclaimer on who paid for the message.

This made me FURIOUS... 

> In August 2022, Toby Newton, 53, bought a 4-bedroom home in Mesa’s Superstition Springs community for about $449,000. 
> He intended to retire there. 
> In early 2024, he lost his job and was diagnosed with diabetes. 
> Quarterly HOA assessments were roughly $170. 
> He fell behind and missed about a year’s worth. 
> The original lien was $877.72. 
> With interest, it was reported as $977. 
> He called the HOA and offered $50 a month toward the debt plus staying current on new assessments. 
> That offer was denied. 
> He raised the offer to $200 a month. > That offer was also denied. 
> He was told the account had already been sent to an attorney. 
> On November 15, 2024, Superstition Springs Community Master Association filed for foreclosure. 
> During the fight, his partner, Sherrie Patten, was diagnosed with breast cancer in both breasts. 
> They still had a mortgage. 
> In April 2025, Arizona passed SB 1494, raising the foreclosure bar for planned communities to 18 months delinquent or $10,000 in actual assessments. 
> Late fees and lawyer bills do not count toward that $10,000. 
> The law also required a reasonable payment plan first. 
> On June 30, 2025, a default judgment was entered. 
> Court papers listed $1,311 in assessments and late charges, $1,042 in collection costs, and $3,345 in attorney fees. 
> The new law took effect on September 26, 2025. 
> Newton’s lawsuit had already been filed the year before, so the higher threshold never saved him. 
> On October 16, 2025, the Maricopa County Sheriff sold the house at auction. 
> By then the debt was $6,579. 
> The highest bidder was the HOA. 
> The sale price was $8,172. 
> They had a six-month redemption window. 
> The HOA later offered an extension to May 2026, but the buy-back price had jumped to $10,484. 
> They could not raise it. 
> In May 2026, they asked a judge to stay enforcement.
> That order is still pending.

You don't hate HOAs enough!

# Proposal: The Coherence Standard as an Independent Accountability Method for X / xAI

@elonmusk @michaelo @Gwynne_Shotwell 
**Submitted by the Equity Forge / SmokeFleet**

## The Gap This Fills

On September 12, 2026, Anthropic's Dario Amodei called for independent evaluators inside AI labs, with real access to internal tools, staff, and training processes, and the ability to publish findings without editorial approval. 

Sam Altman committed OpenAI to the same standard within hours. X and xAI have not yet made a matching commitment.

Meanwhile, X's own product record — the July 2025 instruction change that produced antisemitic outputs, the ongoing non-consensual deepfake issue that triggered a Malaysia block, a Brazilian compliance ultimatum, and a California Attorney General investigation — shows the current internal review process isn't catching problems before they reach the public and, in documented cases, minors.

This proposal offers a concrete, already-tested method to close that gap, rather than asking X to build oversight infrastructure from nothing.

## What the Coherence Standard Is

A methodology developed over the past year of independent civic research, applied consistently across tech companies, government agencies, and media outlets — including this proposal's own author, who has submitted her own work to the same scrutiny. It measures three things against each other:

1. **Stated values** — what the company or leader publicly claims to stand for
2. **Documented actions** — what's actually been built, shipped, staffed, or funded
3. **Real-world outcomes** — what happened to real people as a result

Where those three don't line up, that's the finding. Where they do, that's verified credit — the Standard isn't built to only find fault; it's built to find the truth, whichever direction that points.

## What We're Proposing, Specifically

- **An independent audit of Grok's safety record since July 2025**, using public reporting, the Common Sense Media assessment, and the regulatory actions already on record in Malaysia, Brazil, and California as the evidentiary base — not classified or proprietary access, at least at this stage.
- **A published Coherence Score**, using the same rubric already applied publicly to other tech leaders as part of this project's ongoing work, with X's leadership given the opportunity to respond and contest findings before publication — the same standard applied to every subject reviewed.
- **A standing recommendation set**: concrete, dated steps X/xAI could take to close the gap between the public safety commitments made this week and the product's actual documented record.

## Why This, Why Now

The AI summit reportedly forming this week is an opportunity to move from public statements to real commitments. An independent civic audit, conducted transparently and published regardless of outcome, is a lower-cost, faster way to demonstrate good faith than building an internal evaluator program from scratch — and it can run in parallel with, not instead of, whatever internal process X eventually adopts.

## What We're Asking For

Thirty minutes with whoever at X or xAI is responsible for trust and safety policy, to walk through the method and answer questions about scope, access, and publication terms. We're not asking for payment, equity, or special treatment — only the same access to explain our work that any other civic accountability group would reasonably request

text:
ENOVA $ENVA STOPPED TRYING TO BECOME A BANK. NOT ONE PENNY OF ITS EARNINGS CHANGED:

Enova International at $173.02, -$53.70 / -23.68% today. The Chicago company, founded 2003 and running 1,836 people, lends online to consumers and small businesses that ordinary banks turn down.

The verdict: what this company earns did not change late Monday, and Enova said so in the very announcement that took a quarter off its share price. What changed is where the money it lends was going to come from - and that turns out to have been most of what the market was paying for.

After Monday's close, Enova withdrew its applications with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve to buy Grasshopper Bancorp. Those two agencies decide who is allowed to own a bank in America, so without them there is no deal. Chief executive Steve Cunningham said regulators have no clear standards for a non-bank that wants to become a bank, and that withdrawing was the best decision for shareholders.

Here is why that is a 24% day and not a headline.

Enova holds no deposits. It borrows from bond investors and professional lenders, then lends that money on at much higher rates. What it pays is its cost of funds - the interest rate on the money it turns around and lends - and in the June quarter that was 8.1%, against 8.2% in March and 8.8% a year earlier. Every dollar Enova puts to work starts eight cents behind.

A bank starts at close to nothing, because its money arrives from customers who leave it sitting in an account. That was the entire point of Grasshopper: announced December 11 last year at about $369M in cash and shares, a digital bank with more than $1.4B of assets and about $3B of deposits, counting the accounts it runs inside other companies' apps as well as its own. Enova told owners the deal would add more than 15% to adjusted profit per share - profit per share with one-off items set aside - in its first year, and more than 25% once the savings were fully in.

None of that was in this year's forecast. Enova had always said the bank contributed nothing to 2026, which is exactly how it could reaffirm that forecast on the same page as cancelling the deal and still shed $1.34B of market value - more than three times the price it had agreed to pay for the bank. The year is unchanged and a quarter of the company is gone. That says plainly which of the two was being bought.

The business underneath is not the problem. July 23, three months to June 30:

- Revenue $928.9M, +22%. Small business $439M, +35%; consumer $477M, +11%
- Adjusted profit $4.31 a share against $3.23, +33%, and against the $3.92 analysts carried - a seventh straight quarter above that figure
- Loans and finance receivables a record $5.5B, +28%, on originations of $2.3B, +27%
- Net charge-offs 7.3% of the book, the share written off as never coming back, with loans more than 30 days late steady at 7.5%

SoFi Technologies at $17.25, -$0.40 / -2.27% today, is the finished version of what Enova just walked away from. The San Francisco lender bought a small California bank holding company, Golden Pacific Bancorp, closing February 2, 2022, and by June 30 held $45.5B of deposits funding better than nine tenths of everything it owes. It put the advantage in a number of its own: the average rate it paid on deposits last quarter ran 1.56 percentage points below what it paid on warehouse borrowing, the bank credit line a non-bank uses instead. It is a current pick on none of the six Len5es - near 37 times profit and 2.1 times book value, what owners would keep if everything were sold and every debt paid, hands neither value style a discount.

Enova is a current pick on none of the six either, and today hardens that rather than softening it. The Momentum Len5 wants a price near the top of its own one-year range with the recent climb and the longer one agreeing; $173.02 sits 35.3% under the $267.45 of August 14, most of that gap opened this morning, on 1.49M shares against a 270k daily average. Both value styles - one hunting a business almost nobody could rebuild bought under its worth, the other settled earning power bought cheaply - are offered about 16.8 times the last year of profit and 3.8 times book: the multiple reads cheap, the book does not, and what sits behind that book is non-prime lending written off at 7.3% a year. The Growth Len5 is the near miss, hunting profit growth the price has not already charged for: 33% growth under 17 times earnings is that shape on paper, and what it is not handed is any settled answer on the 8.1% that decides how much of the growth an owner keeps. CHANGE IT: that funding cost actually coming down in the bond market, which after Monday is the only road left to it.

WATCH the cost of funds, not the revenue headline. It is the one line here that a good quarter cannot fix and a bad one cannot hide. WHEN: third-quarter results are tentatively Tuesday, October 22, after the close, with $4.34 a share carried against the $3.36 earned a year earlier. RISK: Enova also said it will speed up buying back its own shares for the rest of 2026, with $349M left under a board authorization running to June 30 next year. Retiring shares lifts profit per share by shrinking the number of owners. It does nothing to the 8.1%.

Enova has wanted a bank charter since at least 2020. Six years of applications bought it one sentence saying the rulebook for a company like this does not exist, and a share price that now pays for a lender funding itself the way it always has. The loan book was never the question here. What it costs to fill it always was.

Not investment advice.

18 years ago I was listening to a podcast where they mentioned an all-electric sports car called the Roadster.

It was made by a new startup named Tesla. I was immediately fascinated.

10 years later I became that company's top referrer, winning 2 future next-gen Roadsters worth $500,000.

Here's the story 👇

Tesla has a referral program where owners can share their unique referral link with others. If an order happens then both people get perks (like free Supercharger miles)

However, past versions of the referral program also gave the referrer a chance to win even more incredible rewards (like actual free vehicles)

2008: I first discover Tesla by listening to a podcast from @leolaporte and @jason where they mentioned an electric sports car called the Roadster. I searched it on Google and was immediately impressed by the car and company.

2012: The Tesla Model S is released. I was enthralled by the tech in the car, but it was way out of my price range since I was just a broke kid right out of college. It never crossed my mind that I’d ever own one.

2014: I make a promise to myself that I will become a Tesla owner someday so I start saving money. This was mainly inspired by two things:

“What it’s like to own a Tesla Model S” cartoon by @Oatmeal (https://t.co/yyOto70Ont)
@MKBHD's Tesla Model S videos on YouTube

2016: I publish my very first Tesla video of me traveling hundreds of miles to Cincinnati to reserve a Model 3 which hadn’t even been unveiled yet and wouldn’t come for another 2 years. (https://t.co/uySXtWSPyV)

2017: I create a video for Tesla Project Loveday contest.  Since I was Tesla-less I had to camp at my local Supercharger and wait for a stranger with a Tesla to show up. A Model X owner named Marshal kindly let me film his car. It sparked my love for filming Tesla videos. (https://t.co/8K6TL3LRtK)

Feb 28, 2018: After almost 2 years of waiting, there were still no Model 3s near me to test drive. I traveled to Chicago and spent $300 to rent a Model 3 for a day. It was my 1st time driving a Tesla, and I immediately fell in love with the car. (https://t.co/ewTrDSA92a)

Apr 22, 2018: At this point I was slowly losing my mind waiting for my Model 3, checking the Tesla subreddit daily. So I did the most reasonable thing I could think of: I made a Tesla rap video. (https://t.co/4d3BKS02Tw)

Apr 30, 2018: I finally get my Model 3 after 2 years of waiting. It was worth the wait. I immediately start documenting my experience for my full review.

However, at this time Model 3 owners like myself did not have a referral code. Tesla only gave them to Model S/X owners.

May 11, 2018: Tesla enables referral codes for Model 3 owners. But the referral code was only be eligible for Model S/X purchases, not Model 3. So my referral code was basically useless to me since most of my audience would be interested in Model 3.

Jun 24, 2018: I upload my Tesla Model 3 review video to YouTube which quickly starts getting thousands of views. However, I never mentioned my referral link in my video. Instead, I just listed it in the video description. It starts getting clicks. (https://t.co/iPgihNfLYA)

Aug 1, 2018: Tesla allows referral codes to be applied to  Performance Model 3 orders, but I'm unaware this happened at the time. A month later, I upload “True Cost of Model 3” which becomes one of my most popular Tesla videos. (https://t.co/hoDSn7D824)

Sep 29, 2018: I pick up @Uber & @Lyft passengers in my Model 3 to get their reactions. The video ends up going viral after @elonmusk liked it on Twitter. A few days later @Tesla tweets my video from their official account. (https://t.co/VAeRw4zAQS)

That week I log into my Tesla account and see names listed under my “Referrals”. Back then one of the prizes was to attend a future Tesla event, and I was so excited that I had enough (5 referrals) to do that.

The big catch: Tesla's referral program also had “Secret Levels” that offered a 100% discount on a future next-gen Roadster, which required 55 referrals to unlock. The kicker? You could earn up to two Roadsters!

Oct 19, 2018: Tesla finally makes any vehicle order eligible for referrals, including Model 3. This was a turning point. I started mentioning my referral code in my Tesla videos from then on out. My moonshot goal was to earn one Roadster before the program was set to end on Dec 10.

Nov 11, 2018: I publish “Model 3 Buyers Guide” where I explained the experience to viewers while driving my Model 3. At the time of that video I had 22 referrals. I needed to average 1+ referrals per day in order to hit 55 referrals to earn a Roadster. (https://t.co/6IldexGOya)

Here’s where it got crazy.

During this time, Tesla made their biggest sales push for the Model 3 by sending out emails urging people to order by the end of November to lock in the full tax credit. This made for the perfect storm which absolutely skyrocketed my referrals.

Nov 16, 2018: I hit 55 referrals to earn my first $250,000 Founders Series Roadster. I couldn't believe it, and I certainly did not expect it to continue especially since there was only about 3 weeks left until the program was set to end. (https://t.co/DEub9abCJQ)

By the end of November I was getting multiple referrals a day, and it was around this time when I surpassed 105 referrals which was the amount needed to win a 2nd Roadster.

I achieved my moonshot goal. But the referrals kept pouring in, all as a result from my YouTube videos.

On Dec 4, 2018 I became the world's top Tesla referrer with over 200 referrals. Tesla ended their referral program soon after that, but they brought it back in 2019 with some revised rules. (https://t.co/uske9jUCyA)

How that all unfolded is still crazy to me because I didn't start making Tesla videos thinking "Hey, maybe this will get me two free Roadster."

I was just super excited about getting a tech-focused electric car and sharing my experience with others.

And the funny thing is: the original Roadster was the car that got me interested in Tesla in the first place. Now it's finally time to see the actual real next-gen Roadster on October 1.

The original specs were:
• 0-60 in 1.9 seconds
• 250+ mph
• 620 miles of range
• 4 seats
• Removable glass roof

But now it's (somewhat) obvious that there will be a cyber-themed high performance option that uses cold-gas thrusters developed with @SpaceX rocket technology.

And if Tesla actually delivers these cars, October 1st could be the beginning of the final chapter of a story that started nearly 20 years ago for me.

I'm excited to say the least! What are you expecting?

text:
A THIRD OF CHEMED $CHE'S HOSPICE GROWTH IS MONEY IT NO LONGER GIVES BACK TO MEDICARE:

Chemed at $507.23, -$7.06 / -1.37% today. The Cincinnati company owns two businesses with nothing in common: VITAS, the biggest hospice provider in America, and Roto-Rooter, the drain and plumbing brand. Second of fifty-four on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5 watch.

Six boards, six second names, one question between them: how much of last quarter's number shows up again next quarter. Chemed's answer is the plainest, and it has a date on it.

Medicare pays a hospice a fixed sum per patient per day, but it also caps the yearly total - a set allowance for each patient treated, added up. Go past that ceiling and the hospice repays the difference. VITAS went past it, setting aside $16.4M in the June quarter of 2025. This year, $500,000.

July 28, three months to June 30:

- Net revenue $673.3M, +8.8%
- VITAS $443.3M, +11.9%; admissions 19,125, +9.0%
- Roto-Rooter $229.9M, +3.3%, cash profit flat at $48.5M
- Adjusted profit, meaning earnings with one-off items set aside, $6.06 a share against $4.27, +41.9%

VITAS revenue grew $47.1M. That repayment line accounts for $15.9M of it on its own. A tenth fewer shares, 1,517,500 retired at an average $423.63, did much of the rest.

The ceiling is an allowance per patient, so treating more patients raises it. VITAS admitted 9.0% more while its average length of stay fell to 101.2 days from 137.1, thirty-six fewer days each. More patients, each for less time, is exactly what stops a hospice hitting its ceiling - and also the catch: days of care grew only 6.1%, and the gap is that shorter stay.

This Len5 hunts settled earning power bought cheaply, and settled is not the problem: Medicare sets the daily hospice rate, a blocked drain is nobody's discretionary purchase, and on August 6 the board raised the quarterly dividend 17% to $0.70, the 221st in a row. Second rather than first is the price - near 20 times the $25.00 to $25.75 the company maps for its own year, and 8.1 times book value, what owners would keep if everything were sold and every debt paid. CHANGE IT: a real fall in the price while hospice census keeps compounding.

WATCH the repayment line, not the revenue headline - full-year charges are now mapped at $7M, cut from $9.5M. WHEN: October 1, when the federal hospice rate rises 2.3% and the per-patient ceiling goes to $36,174.75 from $35,361.44; results are tentatively October 27, $6.37 carried against $5.27. RISK: the 41.9% is measured against a quarter that landed 45 cents under what analysts carried. VERDICT: the repair is real and nearly finished, and Chemed now grows on patients and drains, at a price that already assumes it.

MOMENTUM LEN5:
Personalis at $16.04, -$0.25 / -1.53% today sells a blood test that finds leftover cancer DNA after treatment. Second of thirty on the Len5 hunting prices near a one-year high with short and long trends agreeing, and the long one is emphatic at +224% since April 29. August 4, quarter to June 30: revenue $22.4M, +30%, on 10,384 clinical tests, +199%. None of it reaches the share price now. On July 20 Tempus AI at $66.65, +$4.44 / +7.14% today agreed to buy the company in stock sized to be worth $16.25 a share whatever Tempus costs that day - so the buyer rises 7% and this does not. Tempus, unprofitable, fits no Len5. CHANGE IT: a raised offer, or a broken one. VERDICT: a real trend wearing a contract, 1.3% under the agreed price.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:
Gentex at $22.46, -$0.12 / -0.55% today makes the rear-view mirror that dims itself when headlights hit it. Second of fifty-five on the Len5 hunting a business almost nobody could rebuild at a discount: a mirror is designed into a car model years ahead and stays for its life. July 24, quarter to June 30: net sales $651.3M, -1%, yet net income $114.7M, +19%, on 37.0 cents of each sales dollar kept after building it against 34.2. CHANGE IT: about $18M of customs refund money sits in that margin, which is why Gentex maps its own year at 34.5% to 35.5%, under what it just printed. VERDICT: 12.0 times profit and 1.87 times book, a real discount and second because it is not a deep one. October 23 tentative.

GROWTH LEN5:
Unity Bancorp at $59.46, -$0.49 / -0.82% today is the Clinton, New Jersey parent of Unity Bank. Second of thirty on the Len5 hunting profit growth nobody has charged for, and 10.5 times earnings charges little for a bank keeping 4.56% on its loans after paying depositors. July 14, quarter to June 30: net income $14.5M, $1.42 a share, two cents under what analysts carried and the only quarter in seven it has landed short. CHANGE IT: on September 10 it bought $27.6M of federal tax credits for $25.1M, expecting a one-time $2.5M cut to this quarter's tax bill. VERDICT: nearest its one-year high of any name here, on growth the profit line has still to show - October 13 tentative, $1.55 carried, some 25 cents of it that purchase rather than lending.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:
AppLovin at $331.52, -$2.72 / -0.82% today runs the system deciding which advert appears inside a mobile app. Second of thirty on the Len5 hunting businesses early as well as fast. Fast is settled: August 5, quarter to June 30, revenue $1.92B, +53%; net income $1.27B, +55%, or 66 cents of every revenue dollar. Early is the half that fails, at $110.9B. CHANGE IT: last quarter it cleared the figure analysts carried by a single cent, $3.76 against $3.75, the narrowest of its last seven. VERDICT: 55.5% under last September's $745.61 while still growing 53% - the argument is no longer the growth, it is what was already paid for it. November 4 tentative.

INCOME LEN5:
Ardmore Shipping at $18.64, -$0.11 / -0.59% today owns mid-sized tankers carrying gasoline, diesel and chemicals out of Bermuda. Second of thirty on the Len5 hunting cash returned that the business itself funds - and Ardmore does not promise an amount, it divides one, handing over two-thirds of adjusted profit each quarter. July 29, quarter to June 30: adjusted profit $48.3M, $1.18 a share against $0.22 a year earlier, its tankers hired at $51,870 a day. The $0.79 that followed was paid today. CHANGE IT: this quarter is already booked lower at $29,600 a day. VERDICT: not a yield but a share of whatever the ships earned - November 4 tentative, $0.62 carried, two-thirds of which is about $0.41, roughly half the cheque just banked.

Second place on one of these boards is not a consolation prize. It is the seat where one number is still being argued about. Chemed's argument is nearly settled: it spent a year sending money back to Medicare, it has stopped, and on October 1 the ceiling that caused it rises another $813.31 a patient. That buys room, not a repeat. A company can only stop doing the same expensive thing once.

For the ninth consecutive year, Kennedy-Powell STEM Academy has been recognized as a Project Lead The Way (PLTW) Distinguished School. The PLTW Distinguished School recognition honors schools committed to increasing student access, engagement, and achievement in their PLTW programs. 

Kennedy-Powell is one of a select number of elementary schools across the U.S. to receive this honor for providing broad access to transformative learning opportunities for students through PLTW Launch, an elementary STEM curriculum. 

To qualify, Kennedy-Powell needed at least 75 percent of the student body participating in at least one PLTW Launch module and had to offer at least one PLTW Launch module in each grade K-5 during the 2024-2025 school year. Many of those students completed four modules and are learning critical thinking and problem-solving lessons they will carry with them throughout their academic and professional careers. The students engage in hands-on learning and project-based activities across the campus, not just in Kennedy-Powell’s STEM Lab.

Congratulations, KP STARS, and thank you for your hard work in challenging our students to achieve through Project Lead The Way. #TempleISDproud

text:
Peter, I am not your adversary. A lot of people have given years to election integrity. We have played different roles.
Mine includes coordinating voter-roll canvassers across Missouri and writing a hand-count method I have taught across the country. It is free at https://t.co/u17p52KYDm. 
You asked when I read every document you have. That is the wrong question. I have worked for lawyers since 1978 and I still prepare and file cases in state and federal court. Reading every pleading, transcript, affidavit, and order produces an opinion. It does not produce a verdict. A civil petition filed yesterday is a claim. A transcript is a record of what was said. An affidavit is a statement that can be true, false, incomplete, or later withdrawn. None of that is a finding of guilt.
You also asked what I think of Secretary Hoskins and a witness being kept out of a hearing. My personal opinion of any official is not the issue, and I generally do not offer one unless asked for a reason that matters. What I can say from firsthand observation: I attended the HAVA hearing in Jefferson City at Connie Kramer’s invitation. I had no badge. No one screened who walked in. If that is the hearing you mean, the “could not get into the building” account does not match what I saw at the door. I was not in the office meetings you describe and I will not pretend I was.
If the filings raise serious issues, they should be tested the way every other case is tested: discovery, sworn testimony, and a court. That is due process. It is the same standard people in this movement have asked others to respect. Reading the file does not replace it.

text:
Warren Buffett handed an 89-year-old woman more than $55 million without checking the inventory, the receivables, or even the property titles.

No audit. One-page contract. Her word was enough.

Then, six years later, she walked out of the company at 95 and opened a competing store directly across the street.

Buffett had missed one clause.

Her name was Rose Blumkin. She arrived in America from Russia with no formal education and learned English from her daughter. In 1937, she used $500 to open Nebraska Furniture Mart.

Her rule was simple: sell cheap and tell the truth.

When suppliers tried to cut her off for underpricing established retailers, she simply found new sources. By 1983, a single Omaha location was generating more than $100 million a year — more than its local competitors combined.

Buffett had watched that record for years.

On August 30, 1983, his 53rd birthday, he made the cash offer. Mrs. B was 89.

Berkshire did not count the inventory, verify the receivables, or check the property titles.

Mrs. Blumkin gave Buffett her word.

He wrote the check.

The rare 13-minute footage attached to this post captures the acquisition as it happened. Buffett says buying a company without an audit was almost unheard of.

Mrs. B remained chairman. Her son Louie and grandsons Ron and Irv continued managing Nebraska Furniture Mart with her.

Then, in May 1989, at 95, a management dispute with her relatives pushed her out.

Three months later, she opened Mrs. B's Warehouse directly across the street from Nebraska Furniture Mart.

At the end of 1992, now 99, Mrs. B returned to Nebraska Furniture Mart.

This time, Buffett made sure she signed a non-compete agreement.

He later admitted that failing to get one the first time had been a mistake.

Mrs. B had never broken her word. Nothing in the original agreement prevented her from leaving or competing.

Trust closed the first deal.

One missing clause brought Buffett back nine years later.

Watch this rare 13-minute footage. Buffett trusted an 89-year-old woman with a $55 million handshake deal — and learned the one thing even trust couldn't replace.

Why #Somalia and #Djibouti Fail Maritime Security  and Why #Somaliland Offers a Reliable Alternative

The security of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden faces a growing threat from Houthi-linked financial, commercial, and logistical networks operating across the region.

Instead of serving as reliable bulwarks, Somalia lacks the proximity to the Gulf of Aden, the capabilities, and the internal cohesion required to provide effective maritime security as a fragile state, while Djibouti is exploiting the crisis and switching sides.

The Architecture of Complicity: Three Individuals, Three Links in the Network

The emerging Houthi infrastructure on the African side of the Red Sea is not dependent on a single country or route. It operates through interconnected financial, commercial, and logistical channels.

Three individuals illustrate different points along that chain:🇩🇯🇸🇴♾🇾🇪🇮🇷

text:
Simpson and Bahr (2021) contend that the Hawaiian plume forms a continuously connected electrical pathway from Earth's surface, through the ocean, to at least the 660-km discontinuity, based on their quantitative analysis of anomalous 24-hour solar quiet (Sq) magnetic responses at Big Island (HAW) compared with undistorted data from Honolulu (HON). Their vertical current-channeling model offers an alternative to conventional three-dimensional electromagnetic induction models, which had not quantitatively explained the anomalous Sq responses. 

Although they conclude that the plume is continuously connected to at least the mid-mantle transition zone, they leave open whether it extends to the core-mantle boundary (CMB), framing this as a testable prediction: "In the absence of distortion, the secular variation observed at sites HON and HAW should be similar, whereas if the plume tail ascends through the lower mantle from the CMB and is sufficiently conductive, then an anomaly in the secular variation is to be expected."

Because excess temperature alone is not expected to produce a large conductivity contrast in a lower-mantle plume, they propose that a plume originating at the CMB is likely to entrain small amounts of iron from a liquid-iron, electrically conducting layer at the base of the lower mantle. For a magnetic secular variation with a one-year period and an assumed average lower-mantle conductivity of 1 S/m, the penetration depth is approximately 2800 km, comparable to the depth of the CMB. Under these conditions, the ratio of plume volume to induction volume is approximately 1/400, about ten times smaller than for a plume extending to the mid-mantle transition zone. A conductivity contrast of 100 between the plume and surrounding lower mantle would therefore be required to produce a channeling effect of comparable significance. Applying bulk-conductivity relation with a core-condition iron conductivity of 1.35 × 10⁶ S/m (Pozzo et al., 2012), they find that this contrast could be achieved with an interconnected iron fraction of only β ≈ 1.1 × 10⁻⁴, or approximately 100 ppm.

The authors emphasize that "a plume originating at the CMB would need to entrain only a trace amount of iron in its root for a significant perturbation of the secular variation to be observed at Earth's surface." Since no magnetic secular variation data from Hawaii's Big Island were available at the time, they could not test this prediction and limited their conclusion to a plume extending continuously to at least the 660-km discontinuity. Nevertheless, they present the model as "a quantitative framework through which to test whether plumes maintain electrical integrity to the CMB" and advance a reason why local magnetic secular variation data should be collected at Hawaii. The approach could also help constrain the depth of genesis of other mantle plumes where geomagnetic observations become available.

Geomagnetic evidence for a continuously connected plume conduit extending to at least the 660-km discontinuity below Hawaii- Simpson/ Bahr (2021)

NEW RESEARCH 

Since the end of the Cold War, America’s poorly calibrated approach to former Soviet states like Ukraine has had disastrous consequences, in part precipitating the West’s geopolitical crisis with Russia. While Washington may hope to shift its focus toward competition with Beijing, this pivot is bound to fail so long as America maintains the same misguided approach to other states on Russia’s periphery like Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, and Moldova.

Past calls for integrating Ukraine and Georgia into NATO, for example, created dangerous geopolitical gray zones that contributed to Russian aggression while failing to secure Western military commitments to defend these so-called “in-between states.” The best way to advance America’s interests in Europe — avoiding war, promoting stability, and supporting economic development — is to take a different approach to these states, based on four strategic principles:

1.) Rejecting further NATO expansion or other US military guarantees to states along Russia’s border.

2.) Promoting economic connectivity projects across the in-between states.

3.) Encouraging the in-between states to maintain and pursue foreign and trade policy flexibility that permits positive relations with both Western and non–Western partners.

4.) Pairing US regional engagement with targeted confidence-building measures with Russia to prevent dangerous security spirals.

Securing a negotiated compromise settlement in Ukraine that guarantees Kyiv a viable economic path into the European Union while establishing formal Ukrainian military neutrality would greatly aid the United States in successfully developing and executing a new blueprint for its approach in Eurasia. Such a deal would offer Washington an opportunity to transform the in-between states into valuable economic partners that directly bolster long-term American industrial competitiveness.

The Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, or TRIPP, between Armenia and Azerbaijan, is a positive example that could be expanded on. Continued US support for strategic geoeconomic projects, like TRIPP or the development of Black Sea port infrastructure in Georgia, would not only help the region but also secure Western access to critical minerals and offer alternatives to supply chain choke points. In addition, targeted US diplomatic actions in the region — such as supporting Moldova’s EU integration while helping resolve the Transnistria dispute, advancing dialogue with Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, and reestablishing a strategic partnership with Georgia — can play a key role in refocusing US engagement on America’s core interests in the region.

By discarding Washington’s open-door policy toward NATO enlargement and embracing prudent, interest-driven economic diplomacy, the United States can safeguard European stability, secure vital resource supply chains, and free up critical national security resources that are necessary for managing greater challenges.

Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires.  SEC. 101. DEFINITIONS UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF
 1933.

 Section 2(a) of the Securities Act of 1933 (15 U.S.C.
77b(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following:
 ``(20) Blockchain.--The term `blockchain' means--

 ``(A) any technology--
 ``(i) where data is--
 ``(I) shared across a
 network to create a distributed ledger
 of independently verifiable
 transactions or information among
 network participants;
 ``(II) linked using
 cryptography to maintain the integrity
 of the distributed ledger and to
 execute other functions; and
 ``(III) propagated among
 network participants to reach consensus
 on the state of the distributed ledger
 and any other functions; and
 ``(ii) composed of source code
 that is publicly available; and
 ``(B) any similar technology to the
 technology described in subparagraph (A).
 ``(21) Blockchain application.--The term
 `blockchain application' means any executable software that is
 deployed to a blockchain and composed of source code that is
 publicly available, including a smart contract or any network
 of smart contracts, or other similar technology.
 ``(22) Blockchain protocol.--The term `blockchain
 protocol' means publicly available source code of a blockchain
 that is executed by the network participants of a blockchain to
 facilitate its functioning, or other similar
 technology.
 ``(23) Blockchain system.--The term `blockchain
 system' means any blockchain, together with its blockchain
 protocol or any blockchain application or network of blockchain
 applications.
 ``(24) Decentralized governance system.--

 ``(A) In general.--The term `decentralized
 governance system' means, with respect to a blockchain
 system, any transparent, rules-based system permitting
 persons to form consensus or reach agreement in the
 development, provision, publication, maintenance, or
 administration of such blockchain system, where
 participation is not limited to, or under the effective
 control of, any person or group of persons under common
 control.
 ``(B) Relationship of persons to
 decentralized governance systems.--With respect to a
 decentralized governance system, the decentralized
 governance system and any persons participating in the
 decentralized governance system shall be treated as
 separate persons unless such persons are under common
 control or acting pursuant to an agreement to act in
 concert.
 ``(C) Legal entities for decentralized
 governance systems.--The term `decentralized governance
 system' shall include a legal entity used to implement
 the rules-based system described in subparagraph (A),
 provided that the legal entity does not operate
 pursuant to centralized management. For the purposes of
 this subparagraph, the delegation of ministerial or
 administrative authority at the direction of the
 participants in a decentralized governance system shall
 not be construed to be centralized
 management.
 ``(25) Digital asset.--The term `digital asset'
 means any digital representation of value which is recorded on
 a cryptographically-secured distributed ledger or other similar
 technology.
 ``(26) Digital commodity.--The term `digital
 commodity' has the meaning given that term under section 1a of
 the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. 1a).
 ``(27) Digital commodity affiliated person.--The
 term `digital commodity affiliated person'--
 ``(A) means a person (including a digital
 commodity related person) that, with respect to any
 digital commodity--
 ``(i) acquires or has any right to
 acquire 5 percent or more of the total
 outstanding units of such digital commodity
 from a digital commodity issuer or an agent or
 underwriter thereof;
 ``(ii) is a founder of the digital
 commodity issuer; or
 ``(iii) is an executive officer,
 director, trustee, general partner, or person
 serving in a similar capacity of the digital
 commodity issuer or held such role at any point
 in the previous 12-month period; and
 ``(B) does not include a decentralized
 governance system.
 ``(28) Digital commodity issuer.--
 ``(A) In general.--With respect to a
 digital commodity, the term `digital commodity issuer'
 means any person that--
 ``(i) issues or causes to be
 issued, or proposes to issue or cause to be
 issued, a unit of such digital commodity to a
 person; or
 ``(ii) offers or sells a right to
 a future issuance of a unit of such digital
 commodity to a person.
 ``(B) Prohibition on evasion.--It shall be
 unlawful for any person to knowingly evade
 classification as a `digital commodity issuer' and
 facilitate an arrangement for the primary purpose of
 effecting an offer, sale, distribution, or other
 issuance of a digital commodity, including via any
 arrangement involving the transfer of intellectual
 property associated with the blockchain system to which
 the digital commodity relates.
 ``(29) Digital commodity related person.--

 ``(A) In general.--With respect to a
 digital commodity issuer, the term `digital commodity
 related person'--
 ``(i) means a person--
 ``(I) that is or was in
 the previous 6-month period a promoter,
 senior employee, advisory board member,
 consultant, advisor, or person serving
 in a similar capacity; or
 ``(II) that acquires or
 has any right to acquire 1 percent or
 more of the total outstanding units of
 such digital commodity from a digital
 commodity issuer or an agent or
 underwriter thereof; and
 ``(ii) does not include a
 decentralized governance system.
 ``(B) Senior employee defined.--In this
 paragraph and with respect to a digital commodity
 issuer, the term `senior employee' means any employee
 materially involved in the management of the digital
 commodity issuer, including management of the
 development of the blockchain system to which the
 digital commodity relates.
 ``(30) End user distribution.--
 ``(A) In general.--The term `end user
 distribution' means a distribution of a unit of a
 digital commodity that--
 ``(i) does not involve an exchange
 of more than a nominal value of cash, property,
 or other assets; and
 ``(ii) is distributed in a broad
 and equitable manner based on conditions
 capable of being satisfied by any participant
 in the blockchain system, including, as
 incentive-based rewards--
 ``(I) to users of the
 digital commodity or any blockchain
 system to which the digital commodity
 relates;
 ``(II) for activities
 directly related to the operation of
 the blockchain system, such as mining,
 validating, staking, or other activity
 directly tied to the operation of the
 blockchain system; or
 ``(III) to the existing
 holders of another digital commodity,
 in proportion to the total units of
 such other digital commodity as are
 held by each person.
 ``(B) Protocol consensus participation.--
 The term `end user distribution' includes the
 following:
 ``(i) Self staking.--The
 distribution of a unit of a digital commodity
 as a programmatic result of validating or
 staking activity for a blockchain system's
 consensus mechanism, including the staking of a
 digital commodity and the operation of a node
 or validator for such activity where the owner
 of the staked digital commodity and operator of
 the node or validator are the same person or
 entity.
 ``(ii) Self-custodial staking with
 a third party.--The distribution of a unit of a
 digital commodity as a programmatic result of
 validating or staking activity for a blockchain
 system's consensus mechanism, including the
 staking of a digital commodity and the
 operation of a node or validator for such
 activity where--
 ``(I) the owner of the
 staked digital commodity and operator
 of the node or validator for such
 activity are different persons or
 entities; and
 ``(II) the operator of the
 node or validator does not maintain
 custody or control of the staked
 digital commodity.
 ``(iii) Custodial and ancillary
 staking services.--Subject to the rules issued
 pursuant to subparagraph (C), the provision of
 custodial or ancillary staking services
 enabling the owner of a digital commodity to
 participate in validating or staking activity
 for a blockchain system's consensus mechanism
 that results in the programmatic distribution
 of a unit of a digital commodity, provided that
 such custodial or ancillary services are
 exclusively administrative or ministerial in
 nature.
 ``(C) Rulemaking to define the custodial
 and ancillary staking services.--Not later than 270
 days after the date of the enactment of this paragraph,
 the Commission shall issue rules defining the custodial
 and ancillary staking services described in
 subparagraph (B)(iii) that are exclusively
 administrative or ministerial in nature, consistent
 with what is necessary or appropriate for the public
 interest or for the protection of investors.
 ``(31) Mature blockchain system.--The term `mature
 blockchain system' means a blockchain system, together with its
 related digital commodity, that is not controlled by any person
 or group of persons under common control.
 ``(32) Permitted payment stablecoin.--The term
 `permitted payment stablecoin' means a payment stablecoin (as
 defined in section 2 of the GENIUS Act) issued by a permitted
 payment stablecoin issuer.
 ``(33) Permitted payment stablecoin issuer.--The
 term `permitted payment stablecoin issuer' has the meaning
 given that term in section 2 of the GENIUS Act.''.

 SEC. 102. DEFINITIONS UNDER THE SECURITIES EXCHANGE ACT OF
 1934.

 Section 3(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15
U.S.C. 78c(a)) is amended--
 (1) by redesignating the second paragraph (80)
 (relating to funding portals) as paragraph (81); and
 (2) by adding at the end the following:
 ``(82) Bank secrecy act.--The term `Bank Secrecy
 Act' means--
 ``(A) section 21 of the Federal Deposit
 Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1829b);
 ``(B) chapter 2 of title I of Public Law
 91-508 (12 U.S.C. 1951 et seq.); and
 ``(C) subchapter II of chapter 53 of title
 31, United States Code.
 ``(83) Additional digital commodity-related
 terms.--
 ``(A) Securities act of 1933.--The terms
 `blockchain system', `decentralized governance system',
 `digital asset', `digital commodity affiliated person',
 `digital commodity issuer', `digital commodity related
 person', `end user distribution', `mature blockchain
 system', `permitted payment stablecoin', and `permitted
 payment stablecoin issuer' have the meaning given those
 terms, respectively, under section 2(a) of the
 Securities Act of 1933 (15 U.S.C. 77b(a)).
 ``(B) Commodity exchange act.--The terms
 `digital commodity', `digital commodity broker',
 `digital commodity dealer', `digital commodity
 exchange', `decentralized finance messaging system',
 and `decentralized finance trading protocol' have the
 meaning given those terms, respectively, under section
 1a of the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C.
 1a).''.

 subparagraph (C) and inserting after subparagraph (A)

 ``(B) Exclusion.--For purposes of this

 shall not include transacting in digital commodities
 for the purpose of--
 ``(i) acting as a digital
 commodity custodian;

 or managing inventory or payment instruments
 for commercial purposes; or
 ``(iii) maintaining or supporting
 the operation of, or validating transactions

 ``(III) a digital
 commodity;'';
 (4) by redesignating paragraphs (16) through (51)

 after paragraph (15) the following:
 ``(16) Terms related to digital commodities.--

 ``(A) Associated person of a digital
 commodity broker.--
 ``(i) In general.--Except as
 provided in clause (ii), the term `associated
 person of a digital commodity broker' means a
 person who is associated with a digital
 commodity broker as a partner, officer,
 employee, or agent (or any person occupying a
 similar status or performing similar functions)
 in any capacity that involves--
 ``(I) the solicitation or
 acceptance of an order for the purchase
 or sale of a digital commodity;
 or
 ``(II) the supervision of

 ``(ii) Exclusion.--The term
 `associated person of a digital commodity

 ``(B) Associated person of a digital

 ``(i) In general.--Except as

 person of a digital commodity dealer' means a

 similar status or performing similar functions)
 in any capacity that involves--
 ``(I) the solicitation or
 acceptance of a contract for the
 purchase or sale of a digital
 commodity; or
 ``(II) the supervision of
 any person engaged in the solicitation
 or acceptance of a contract for the
 purchase or sale of a digital
 commodity.
 ``(ii) Exclusion.--The term
 `associated person of a digital commodity
 dealer' does not include any person associated
 with a digital commodity dealer the functions
 of which are solely clerical or
 ministerial.
 ``(C) Bank secrecy act.--The term `Bank
 Secrecy Act' means--
 ``(i) section 21 of the Federal
 Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C.
 1829b);
 ``(ii) chapter 2 of title I of
 Public Law 91-508 (12 U.S.C. 1951 et seq.);
 and
 ``(iii) subchapter II of chapter
 53 of title 31, United States Code.
 ``(D) Decentralized finance messaging
 system.--
 ``(i) In general.--The term
 `decentralized finance messaging system' means
 a software application that provides a user
 with the ability to create or submit an
 instruction, communication, or message to a
 decentralized finance trading protocol for the
 purpose of executing a transaction by the

 ``(ii) Additional requirements.--

 system' does not include any system that

 control over--
 ``(I) the funds of the
 user; or
 ``(II) the execution of
 the transaction of the user.
 ``(E) Decentralized finance trading
 protocol.--
 ``(i) In general.--The term

 has the authority, directly or

Here's how stupid this Heritage American bullshit is.

Earlier this week, I was stuck at a hotel in small town Ohio.  I tried for 2 hours to get an Uber to the local airfield.  Finally a guy in a pickup truck sees me sitting on the curb and gives me a ride.  

He is a wind turbine mechanic from Texas.  I thank him and offer him gas money.  He says no, he just likes paying it forward; he figures that way someone will help his wife or daughter when they need it.  His mother calls from Texas and they converse in Spanish.  He is Hispanic. 

A few days later in a small town in Kansas, I am walking from the airfield to a hotel.  A guy in a truck stops and picks me up.  

He is in uniform.  Army National Guard, with an 18th Airborne Corps combat patch from Iraq in 2018.  His truck is full of duck hunting gear.  He is a black guy from Chicago.

I would stand beside either one of those guys in a minute, over any of these morons claiming they inherit some kind of status from their ancestors.  

Character ain't hereditary, and it sure ain't racial.
